docs.title: MassFlow
docs.text:
MassFlow is a config-first Python toolkit for local, reproducible tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) annotation workflows. It is designed to be dead easy to run locally, producing highly reproducible scientific outputs.

TL;DR - Dead easy to run

Run your entire annotation pipeline in just two commands: 

# 1. Generate a default config file
uv run massflow init

# 2. Run your annotation pipeline
uv run massflow annotate --config massflow_config.yaml

# 3. Or, run interactively and watch for file changes
uv run massflow watch --config massflow_config.yaml

docs.title: Mission
docs.text:
MassFlow v0.1 delivers a reliable and easily configurable pipeline that takes open-format experimental spectra and reference libraries, applies standard matchms processing, performs classical similarity searching, and produces predictable tabular results.

We prioritize stability, predictability, and correct data handling over cutting-edge features.

docs.text: Surface Status Notes massflow annotate --config ... Stable Recommended for reusable local libraries. db inspect reports build lineage: input files, config hash, processing parameters, target-decoy configuration, and exact build timestamps (records written by db build, db merge, and annotate library-store builds) cosine and modified_cosine Stable Best-supported classical scoring paths CSV export Stable Main reporting surface, with YAML provenance reports. FBMN export is not shipped mzTab-shaped export (format: mztab) Experimental Not mzTab-M standards-conformant: it uses MassFlow-specific SMH/SML columns and omits mandatory mzTab-M structure and null encoding. Retained for diagnostic interchange only; do not treat it as mzTab-M Chemical metadata checks (fixed 5 ppm policy, theoretical isotopic envelopes) Stable Implemented in MassFlow.models/cheminformatics; enforced as a processing gate on spectra with declared structural claims in the classical annotate/db build paths (query rejections counted per file; raw reference-library violations abort annotate), plus the streaming ingestion gate. Spectra without structural claims are exempt. These software checks do not establish identification accuracy or a universal instrument tolerance massflow watch --config ... Experimental Interactive live-reloading workflow ([watch] extra) massflow stream-server Experimental Real-time gRPC streaming (loopback default, TLS/auth required for remote) massflow tui Experimental Interactive terminal console ([tui] extra) Advanced Engines (spec2vec, ms2deepscore, consensus, cascade) Experimental Higher setup and complex scientific validation; outside the stable support promise GraphML networking & Visualization Planned Documented in places, not implemented — do not rely on it Language Server (LSP) Removed The standalone LSP module is not part of the codebase; docs/api/server.md documents the removal

docs.title: Why MassFlow?
docs.text:
MassFlow is designed specifically for domain experts (Analytical Chemists, Metabolomics Researchers) who just want their annotations to work, predictably and reliably.

  1. Stop writing ad-hoc scripts: No more copy-pasting code from old projects. Keep all your noise thresholds and match tolerances in one easy-to-read, version-controlled YAML file.
  2. Use open formats directly: Stop worrying about converters. Feed your mzML, mzXML, MGF, and MSP files directly into the pipeline, or use our massflow convert wrapper for vendor files.
  3. Say goodbye to memory crashes: Instead of loading massive 10GB reference libraries into RAM every time, use MassFlow to compress them into lightning-fast local SQLite databases.
  4. Protect your science: We strictly enforce scientific constraints. MassFlow physically validates precursor masses against their theoretical exact mass and adduct to within a strict 5.0 ppm tolerance, preventing impossible matches.
  5. Easy Excel-ready exports: Review your final annotations via standard, clean CSV files. We even provide a "receipt" alongside every CSV so you know exactly which settings produced it for your paper.

docs.text: Ready to dive in? Head over to the Installation and Quickstart guides to configure your first MS/MS annotation run.

docs.title: MassFlow Architecture
docs.text: This file is a component-level reference only. The authoritative product contract, capability matrix, contradiction log, and core/experimental/future research boundaries live in docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md. Where the two documents disagree, CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md governs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
MassFlow is a local, CLI-first toolkit for tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) annotation workflows.

The core execution path is:

  1. load a YAML configuration
  2. load an experimental file or directory of files
  3. load a reference library
  4. process spectra with configurable matchms filters
  5. run similarity search against the reference library
  6. apply score and legacy numerical confidence filtering (uncalibrated)
  7. write per-file CSV result tables

The architecture is intentionally modular. Configuration, I/O, processing, similarity scoring, database access, and workflow orchestration live in separate modules so the main annotation path stays predictable and testable.

The proposed restricted 1.0 candidate scope centers on:

  • massflow init and massflow annotate --config ...
  • SQLite-backed library workflows through massflow db
  • open-format ingestion for mzML, mzXML, MGF, and MSP
  • transparent matchms processing
  • cosine and modified_cosine candidate ranking
  • CSV (stable) and experimental mzTab-shaped output with source-record metadata

Numerical confidence diagnostics are not calibrated FDR or confirmed identities. Tutorial, conversion, ML, networking, streaming and other experimental utilities are outside the supported candidate-release path.

docs.title: Simple Data Flow Workflow
docs.text: mermaid graph LR Config[YAML Config] --> CLI{MassFlow CLI} Input[Input Files] --> CLI Library[Reference Library] --> CLI CLI --> Processed[Processed Spectra] Processed --> Sim[Similarity Search] Sim --> Filter[Candidate and Numeric-Estimate Filtering] Filter --> Out[CSV / experimental mzTab-shaped + YAML Report]

docs.title: User-facing surfaces
docs.text:
• src/MassFlow/cli.py
  • Defines the CLI commands:
    • init
    • annotate
    • convert
    • db build
    • db inspect
    • db merge
    • stream-server
    • serve
    • watch
    • tui
  • Python API
  • Core modules can also be imported directly for scripting or testing.

docs.title: Terminal console
docs.text:
• src/MassFlow/tui/
  • A Textual-based interactive console (massflow tui, requires the tui extra) with four tabs: Browser (find/upload/load spectral files), Viewer (interactive centroid stick plots), Candidate Review (experimental score/mirror plots), and Diagnostics (problems with plain-English fixes plus the quarantine log).
  • All science-facing helpers are pure functions (NumPy/text in, text out) so the plot glyph math and file logic are unit-testable headlessly; heavy core imports (matchms, pyteomics) are deferred to worker threads.

docs.title: Orchestration
docs.text:
• src/MassFlow/workflow.py
  • Runs the end-to-end annotation pipeline.
  • Coordinates loading, processing, candidate searching, numerical confidence reporting, and export.
  • Uses multiprocessing to process experimental input files in parallel.
  • Runs strict pre-flight checks (preflight_annotation_run) before any expensive work: engine/optional-extras availability, reference-library and query-input existence/format, vendor-raw rejection — with actionable errors and no output artifacts on failure.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• src/MassFlow/config.py
  • Defines the Pydantic models used to validate YAML configuration files.
  • Expands ~ for relevant input paths.
  • Stores processing, similarity, workflow, and export settings.

docs.title: Data access
docs.text:
• src/MassFlow/io.py
  • Loads spectra from supported open formats and SQLite libraries.
  • Rejects vendor raw formats instead of converting them implicitly.

  • Writes match results to CSV (stable) and an experimental mzTab-shaped format, and can export spectra as MGF or MSP.

  • src/MassFlow/database.py

  • Stores and retrieves spectra in SQLite format.
  • Supports database build, inspection, and merge workflows.
  • Supports a hybrid storage mode where SQLite retains metadata plus a zarr_ref/zarr_index reference pair and fragment arrays live in a chunked Zarr store (see src/MassFlow/zarr_store.py), with a migration utility (scripts/migrations/0002_blobs_to_zarr.py) for existing BLOB libraries.
  • Implements a fast NumPy-based Triage Bitmask scan during insertion to flag structurally significant features (e.g., Tyrosine immonium ions at 136.076 Da). These flags are stored as JSON in the triage_flags column for future ML routing.
  • Records a lightweight library-provenance history (store_meta + library_builds tables, PRAGMA user_version >= 1) for every build/merge event — input files with SHA-256, config hash, processing and similarity (target-decoy) configuration, exact timestamps — surfaced by db inspect and linked from annotation result sidecars.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text:
• src/MassFlow/processing.py
  • Applies metadata cleaning and peak filtering using matchms.
  • Handles operations such as retention-time extraction, intensity filtering, minimum peak enforcement, m/z range truncation, Top-N peak reduction, and normalization.

docs.title: Similarity
docs.text:
• src/MassFlow/similarity.py
  • Implements similarity engines and result models.
  • Core engines:
    • cosine
    • modified_cosine
  • Experimental engines:
    • spec2vec
    • ms2deepscore
    • consensus (via the ConsensusEngine)
    • cascade
  • src/MassFlow/acceleration.py
  • Numba-accelerated peak/neutral-loss matching prefilter that skips query-reference pairs below min_matched_peaks before exact modified-cosine scoring (pure-NumPy fallback with identical results).
  • src/MassFlow/hnsw.py
  • hnswlib-backed HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) index over two-channel binned spectral vectors ([binned exact m/z, binned neutral losses]) for optional approximate candidate retrieval libraries. The neutral-loss channel adds a candidate channel for shifted analogues under modified cosine. Used by the cascade engine as an approximate pre-stage with no general recall guarantee; exact scoring follows only for candidates returned by the index.

docs.title: Data models and consensus scoring
docs.text:
• src/MassFlow/models.py
  • Defines strict Pydantic data contracts (AnnotationHit, ConsensusInput, ConsensusResult, ConsensusConfig, MolecularStructure).
  • Provides a dependency-free, engine-agnostic language for communication between the lightweight core and heavy ML satellite repositories (e.g., massflow-ml).
  • Implements rigorous structural validation (e.g., 5 ppm precursor m/z checks) and automatically calculates theoretical isotopic_envelope distributions for valid molecules.
  • Consensus scoring is provided by the ConsensusEngine in src/MassFlow/similarity.py, which combines cosine, modified_cosine, and (when the [ml] extra is installed) Spec2Vec/MS2DeepScore sub-engines into a weighted consensus score. An earlier standalone MassFlow.consensus orchestrator module (with generate_consensus) is not part of the current codebase; the tie-breaking and credibility-check logic it implemented was removed alongside it.

docs.title: Scientific Data Integrity
docs.text: MassFlow checks declared metadata at ingestion under fixed software rules. Passing these checks does not establish a molecule's identity or universal chemical validity.

docs.title: Precursor Validation (5 ppm Tolerance)
docs.text:
The processing gate checks a recognized declared adduct/charge pair for signed-charge consistency even when precursor m/z is missing. When a structure and usable precursor are also declared, the SpectrumMetadata contract compares precursor m/z with the theoretical mass under the fixed 5 ppm policy. The theoretical m/z uses the formula-derived exact mass and registered adduct offset. These checks cover declared metadata consistency, not universal instrument tolerances or identity confirmation.

Enforcement surface — the verdicts are consumed by three gates:

  1. Classical annotate / db build metadata gate (MassFlow.processing, run after matchms harmonization): every record with a recognized explicit adduct/charge pair is checked for signed-charge consistency; records declaring a formula, SMILES, or InChI also receive structural and 5 ppm checks.
  2. query spectra failing the gate are rejected with a human-readable reason, counted in spectra_rejected, and recorded in the quarantine log; a query file whose spectra are all rejected is an explicit failed result (<stem>_failed.report.yaml), never an empty success;
  3. a raw reference library containing a failing entry aborts the annotate run with processing.PhysicalIntegrityError before any file is processed — silently shrinking the reference pool would change candidate searches and legacy numerical estimates. Pre-built MassFlow stores are trusted (they are produced by db build, which runs the same gate and quarantines invalid entries);
  4. spectra without structural claims skip the structural/5 ppm mass checks; explicitly declared supported adduct/charge pairs are still checked.
  5. Streaming ingestion gate (MassFlow.streaming.engine.validate_streaming_spectrum, experimental stream-server) rejects packets failing the Pydantic field constraints before scoring.
  6. Model layer — direct construction of SpectrumMetadata/MolecularStructure always computes the verdict.

Supported Adducts (22 entries in the _ADDUCT_SPECS registry; docs/user-guide/validation.md holds the authoritative offset table and the notation rules): - Positive Mode: [M+H]+, [M+NH4]+, [M+Na]+, [M+K]+, [M]+, [M+2H]2+, [M+3H]3+, [M+2Na-H]+, [M+H-H2O]+, [M+CH3CN+H]+, [M+CH3OH+H]+ - Negative Mode: [M-H]-, [M-2H]2-, [M+Cl]-, [M+Br]-, [M+I]-, [M+HCOO]-, [M+CH3COO]-, [M+TFA-H]-, [M+HCO3]-, [M+NO3]-, [M]- - Notation and ionisation mode are read from the chemistry, not the string: MassFlow.cheminformatics.normalize_adduct canonicalises library spellings (M+H, [M+H]1+, [m+h]+, M+OAc, legacy [M+FA-H]-) onto these keys before lookup, and MassFlow.cheminformatics.adduct_charge reports the resolved signed charge, so e.g. [M+HCOO]- is negative despite the +. Notation that cannot be resolved still fails closed.

docs.title: Theoretical Isotopic Envelopes
docs.text: For advanced structural verification, the MolecularStructure model automatically calculates and caches the theoretical isotopic envelope (M, M+1, M+2, etc.) for any parsed SMILES string. By generating abundance-weighted centroid masses normalized to the base peak, the pipeline establishes a ground-truth MS1 signature for every reference candidate. This allows the ConsensusEngine and orthogonal ML models to evaluate candidate credibility by checking experimental MS1 isotopic patterns, providing a powerful orthogonal tie-breaking mechanism when MS2 fragmentation scores are ambiguous.

docs.title: Component Diagram
docs.text: mermaid graph TD CLI[CLI & API] --> WORKFLOW[Workflow] WORKFLOW --> CONFIG[Configuration] WORKFLOW --> IO[I/O Layer] IO <--> DB[Database] WORKFLOW --> PROCESS[Processing] PROCESS --> SIM[Similarity Engine] SIM --> WORKFLOW SIM --> ML[ML Engines]

docs.title: Actual Annotation Workflow
docs.text:
The main production path begins with:

  • massflow annotate --config path/to/config.yaml

The CLI loads the config and calls run_annotation_pipeline().

docs.title: Pipeline steps
docs.text:
1. Pre-flight validation (fail fast)

  2. Before any library store is built or any file is searched, preflight_annotation_run() validates: (a) the configured similarity surface is constructible with the installed optional extras (a pure ML engine without massflow-msms[ml] aborts with the install instruction instead of crashing workers later); (b) the reference library is configured, exists, and is a loadable open-format/store input (vendor raw and unknown formats abort with zero artifacts); (c) the query input exists and is dispatchable — vendor files inside a directory are announced and then fail explicitly per file (batch robustness). Warnings (optional_extra_warnings) surface degradations from missing [ml]/[hnsw] extras. The CLI prints fix: hints (MassFlow.tui.diagnostics.suggest_fix) for every failure.

  3. Configuration loading

  4. The YAML file is parsed into MassFlowConfig.

  5. Paths such as input_path and library_path have ~ expanded.

  6. Library loading

  7. The workflow requires a configured library path.
  8. In the preferred config terminology, this is input.library_path.
  9. The library is loaded first and processed through the configured matchms pipeline.
  10. If no valid spectra are found, the run fails.

  11. If the library is small, the workflow logs a warning that FDR estimates may be weak.

  12. Experimental input discovery

  13. The workflow reads input.input_path, which may point to a single spectral file or a directory of files.

  14. If a directory is used, files are discovered recursively.

  15. Pre-loading and Multiprocessing

  16. The parent process generates the decoy library ONCE.
  17. The fully processed reference library and decoys are loaded into shared memory.

  18. Each experimental input file is dispatched to a worker process.

  19. Query spectrum loading and processing

  20. Query spectra are loaded from the experimental file.
  21. Each spectrum is passed through metadata and peak processing.

  22. Missing query IDs are filled in automatically.

  23. Chunked reference searching (bounded library chunks)

  24. The worker searches its queries against the pre-loaded shared memory library in chunks to preserve RAM, entirely bypassing disk I/O.

  25. Results are aggregated.

  26. FDR calculation

  27. Entropy-based decoys are generated from the reference spectra: each decoy preserves the precursor m/z, its source's complete peak list, and the Shannon entropy of its source's noise-filtered fragment intensities while randomizing the fragmentation pathways, avoiding the null-distribution bias of naive fragment shuffling.
  28. Target and decoy scores are combined to estimate q-values. Decoys are scored and gated exactly like targets; because the position randomization keeps a decoy from coinciding with its source at scoring tolerance, decoy hits are rare at production score/matched-peak gates, and an empty decoy null (no decoy competition) is reported explicitly: the engine exposes decoy_diagnostics + the decoy_null_empty flag, the workflow flags fdr_uncalibrated (q-values are then 1/N rank diagnostics, not error bounds) and the exported rows are labeled Uncalibrated.
  29. The workflow logs a target-decoy entropy-divergence diagnostic to report descriptive target/decoy entropy differences. See scoring_logic.md §5.1 for the empty-null contract.

  30. Final results are filtered by:

    • score thresholds
    • matched-peak thresholds where applicable
    • configured historical q-value threshold (not calibrated FDR control)

  31. Result Export

  32. The workflow writes one result file per experimental input file.
  33. Output filenames follow the pattern:
    • <input_stem>_results.<ext>

docs.text:

docs.title: Supported direct input formats
docs.text:
MassFlow directly loads:

  • mzML
  • mzXML
  • MGF
  • MSP
  • SQLite libraries:
  • .db
  • .sqlite

docs.title: Unsupported direct input formats
docs.text:
MassFlow intentionally does not perform vendor raw conversion internally.

Examples of vendor formats that must be converted before use include:

  • .raw
  • .d
  • .wiff
  • .lcd
  • .t2d
  • .baf

Users should convert these to open formats such as mzML or MGF before running the annotation workflow.

docs.title: Standard outputs
docs.text:
The stable output format is CSV. An experimental mzTab-shaped table is also available, but it is not mzTab-M standards-conformant and is outside the stable export contract.

  • CSV (stable) or experimental mzTab-shaped result files written per experimental input

The export format is selected via export.format in the config (csv is the stable value; mztab is experimental and non-conformant).

docs.title: Core candidate-retrieval path
docs.text:
These are the features the docs should treat as the main supported path:

  • massflow annotate --config ...
  • YAML configuration via MassFlowConfig
  • open-format ingestion for mzML, mzXML, MGF, and MSP
  • explicit SQLite reference-library workflows
  • matchms-based metadata and peak processing
  • cosine and modified_cosine
  • legacy query-level numerical confidence filtering (uncalibrated)
  • per-file CSV (stable) and experimental mzTab-shaped result export
  • massflow db build, inspect, and merge

docs.title: Experimental or less-stable surfaces
docs.text:
These features exist in the repository but should be treated more cautiously:

  • spec2vec
  • ms2deepscore
  • consensus
  • cascade

See README.md for the user-facing guide to what is currently experimental, why it is classified that way, and how to approach those features safely.

docs.title: MassFlow.cli
docs.text: Parses command-line arguments, configures logging, and dispatches CLI commands into the workflow or database layers.

docs.title: MassFlow.workflow
docs.text: Implements the annotation pipeline. It loads and processes the reference library, discovers input files, processes query spectra in parallel, performs chunked searching, reports uncalibrated query-level confidence diagnostics, and writes output tables.

docs.title: MassFlow.config
docs.text: Defines the nested configuration schema used by the CLI and workflow. Validation is focused on structural correctness and basic parameter constraints rather than full runtime guarantees.

docs.title: MassFlow.io
docs.text: Provides the file-system boundary for MassFlow. It loads spectra from supported formats, rejects unsupported vendor raw inputs, and exports result tables.

docs.title: MassFlow.database
docs.text:
Provides SQLite-backed storage for spectral libraries and helper methods for build, inspection, merge, and spectrum streaming. In addition to the default BLOB mode (mz_array / intensity_array), it supports a hybrid mode where SQLite retains only metadata plus a zarr_ref / zarr_index reference pair and fragment arrays are persisted in a chunked Zarr store (see MassFlow.zarr_store). The migrate_blobs_to_zarr helper (wrapped by scripts/migrations/0002_blobs_to_zarr.py) migrates existing BLOB libraries to the hybrid backend with bitwise verification.

SQLite-backed stores also carry a lightweight library-provenance schema (store_meta + library_builds, PRAGMA user_version >= 1): every db build, db merge, or annotate library-store build records its input file(s) with content SHA-256, the effective config hash, the processing and similarity (target-decoy) configuration JSON, and an exact UTC timestamp. massflow db inspect renders this history (library versions, processing history, target-decoy configuration), and the annotate provenance sidecars link every result to the exact build row. The schema is additive and idempotent — raw SQL CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS upgrades pre-provenance databases in place on their next open, and provenance writes never alter scientific payload bytes.

docs.title: MassFlow.processing
docs.text: Applies the configured matchms metadata repairs and peak filtering pipeline.

docs.title: MassFlow.similarity
docs.text: Creates and runs the scoring engines. It also defines decoy generation and result structures used during numerical confidence reporting. Modified-cosine full scoring is the default. An experimental Numba peak/neutral-loss prefilter (MassFlow.acceleration) is opt-in and has no general candidate-recall guarantee. The experimental cascade can optionally use HNSW (MassFlow.hnsw) for approximate candidate retrieval; no universal recall or sub-linear performance claim is made. External ML engines (Spec2Vec, MS2DeepScore) sit behind the MLEngineProtocol boundary and may run remotely over REST/gRPC (MassFlow.ml_client, ml_endpoints in the config); a circuit breaker plus classical modified_cosine fallbacks in the meta-engines and workflow keep runs alive when the ML service is unreachable or heavy dependencies are missing.

docs.title: MassFlow.streaming (experimental)
docs.text: Implements the gRPC real-time annotation server (StreamSpectra bidirectional RPC plus GetStatus health probe). Incoming packets are validated through a Pydantic/matchms gate, buffered in a bounded async queue with quality-gated high-water-mark backpressure (low-quality spectra are shed under overrun and reported as spectra_dropped_low_quality), micro-batched, and routed through the ConsensusEngine; annotations stream back to the client as they complete.

docs.title: MassFlow.tui (interactive, requires the tui extra)
docs.text: Implements the interactive terminal console (massflow tui): a spectral file browser with workspace upload, an interactive spectrum viewer with Unicode-glyph stick plots, an experimental candidate-review tab with mirror plots, and a diagnostics tab that surfaces problems with plain-English fixes plus the quarantine log. All heavy work runs in Textual worker threads, and the science-facing helpers (peak downsampling, mirror alignment, plot rendering, file discovery, error hints) are pure functions covered by headless unit tests. See docs/api/tui.md.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
MassFlow follows a few simple design rules:

  • Config first: reproducible CLI runs are preferred over ad hoc scripts.
  • Open formats only: vendor conversion happens before MassFlow.
  • Small focused modules: I/O, processing, scoring, and orchestration stay separated.
  • Predictable outputs: the core workflow should either produce CSV results or return actionable errors.
  • Experimental boundaries: advanced engines and interactive utilities may evolve without expanding the core support promise.

docs.title: Practical Example
docs.text:
A typical config-driven run looks like this:

project:
  output_directory: "results/standard_analysis"

input:
  input_path: "data/experiments/experiment.mzML"
  library_path: "data/libraries/library.msp"
  format: "mzml"

similarity:
  algorithm: "cosine"
  ms1_tolerance: 0.02
  ms2_tolerance: 0.02
  tolerance_unit: "Da"
  min_score: 0.6
  min_matched_peaks: 3
  fdr_threshold: 0.05

Run it with:

uv run massflow annotate --config massflow_config.yaml

This will process the experimental file, search it against the reference library, and write a CSV file into the configured output directory.

docs.title: MassFlow Product Contract & Capability Matrix
docs.text:
STATUS: AUTHORITATIVE — single source of truth for what MassFlow is, what it ships, and what it must not be mistaken for.

This document is the result of a full repository reconciliation audit (2026-08-25). Where this document conflicts with README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, docs/index.md, docs/CHANGELOG.md, or the external research specification, this document governs until those files are updated to match it.

docs.title: 1. Authoritative product scope (the contract)
docs.text:
The proposed restricted MassFlow 1.0 scope is local MS/MS candidate retrieval and review for small-molecule spectral libraries. It ingests open-format spectra, applies transparent matchms processing, ranks local-library candidates with classical similarity scores, and exports source-linked tabular evidence. Numerical target/decoy estimates are explicitly uncalibrated; this software does not establish chemical identity or controlled FDR.

The proposed supported candidate-release surface (subject to the evidence gates below):

Surface Detail CLI commands massflow init, annotate, db build, db inspect, db merge Configuration YAML → MassFlowConfig (project, input, processing, similarity, export) Ingestion mzML, mzXML, MGF, MSP, MassFlow SQLite (.db/.sqlite); vendor raw formats rejected with UnsupportedVendorFormatError Processing matchms-based metadata cleaning, RT extraction, intensity/m/z filters, top-N reduction, normalization Similarity cosine, modified_cosine (always available) Confidence Pooled per-query target/decoy numerical diagnostics with explicit estimated_uncalibrated/unavailable/invalid states; no calibrated-FDR claim (see the confidence contract) Storage SQLite libraries (massflow db build/inspect/merge) with persisted build lineage; Zarr/hybrid and migration utilities are experimental Exports Per-input CSV tables (stable) and experimental mzTab-shaped tables, with YAML provenance and source-record metadata. The mztab format is not mzTab-M standards-conformant; its stable conformance claim is withdrawn Metadata checks Recognized declared adduct/charge pairs must agree in signed charge; fixed 5 ppm precursor checks require structural and precursor context. These checks do not confirm identity or establish universal instrument/adduct validity Python API MassFlow.config, io, processing, similarity, database, storage, zarr_store, workflow, models, cheminformatics, protocols, ml_client

Excluded from the proposed 1.0 support promise:

  • Peptide/proteomics search of any kind (see §6).
  • TIIP indexing, O(1) peptide retrieval, BIN/BEST consensus spectra (see §6).
  • The synthetic tutorial generator is a source-checkout-only repository script; the unsupported massflow tutorial CLI command has been removed and is not part of the installed wheel/sdist support promise.
  • SIRIUS / MS-GF+ / MaRaCluster / FragPipe interoperability (see §6).
  • FBMN export, GraphML molecular networking, massflow visualize — documented in places but not implemented (§4.4). Treat as aspirational until shipped.
  • ML engines (spec2vec, ms2deepscore), meta-engines (consensus, cascade), routing, streaming, TUI, HNSW, and watch — all experimental, not part of the support promise (§4.2).

docs.title: 2. Capability matrix
docs.text: Status legend: ✅ Stable (implemented and tested within the supported candidate scope) · 🧪 Experimental (implemented and tested, outside the support promise) · 🟡 Partial (implemented for a subset of the documented surface) · 📕 Missing (documented somewhere in-repo, no code) · 📋 Planned (roadmap/research only).

docs.title: 5. External research specification — explicit non-contract status
docs.text:
A technical specification/research document exists outside this repository describing a substantially different architecture:

TIIP peptide indexing, O(1) peptide retrieval, BIN/BEST consensus generation, SIRIUS / MS-GF+ / MaRaCluster interoperability, and proteomics-oriented peptide search.

Verified status (full-text search of this repository, 2026-08-25):

  • TIIP, BIN/BEST, MaRaCluster, MS-GF, SIRIUS, FragPipe, and peptide-indexing terms appear nowhere in src/, tests/, pyproject.toml, configuration files, or documentation.
  • No config schema, CLI command, module, test, or data contract relates to peptide search.
  • The repository's "consensus" vocabulary refers to ConsensusEngine weighted spectral scoring — not BIN/BEST consensus-spectrum generation.

Mandate for all future agents:

  1. The research specification is research context only. It is not a requirement, a roadmap item, or a description of the current product.
  2. Do not implement TIIP, peptide indexing, BIN/BEST, or SIRIUS/MS-GF+/MaRaCluster interop as part of MassFlow v0.x work.
  3. If work on the research vision begins, it must start with a new product contract (a successor document to this one), not by extending the v0.1 surfaces.
  4. Any file that describes MassFlow (README, ARCHITECTURE, AGENTS, copilot-instructions, mkdocs docs) must be written from §1 of this document.

docs.title: 6. Core product vs experimental extensions vs future research (one-glance)
docs.text: Tier Contents Change discipline Core (v0.1 contract, §1) annotate/init/db */convert CLI; YAML config; mzML/mzXML/MGF/MSP/SQLite ingestion; matchms processing; cosine/modified_cosine; entropy decoys + explicit uncalibrated/unavailable target-decoy diagnostics (no calibrated-FDR claim); CSV + YAML exports (experimental mzTab-shaped output is outside the stable core); 5 ppm/isotopic validation enforced on the classical annotate/db-build processing path (structural claims only) + streaming gate; SQLite + optional hybrid Zarr storage Must not regress; full test suite + coverage gate; extra scrutiny on changes Experimental (§2.2) HNSW, cascade, consensus, spec2vec/ms2deepscore, remote ML boundary + satellite, MLRouter, streaming server, TUI, watch, Numba prefilter, hybrid/Zarr storage, convert May evolve freely; must not break the core; guards and fallbacks required Future research Generative spectral augmentation, PINNs (in-repo roadmap); TIIP peptide indexing, O(1) peptide retrieval, BIN/BEST consensus, SIRIUS/MS-GF+/MaRaCluster interop, proteomics peptide search (external spec) Do not implement as v0.x requirements; requires a new contract first

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to MassFlow will be documented in this file.

Historical entries may describe surfaces later removed or reclassified; the Unreleased section and current documentation take precedence.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Removed the unsupported massflow tutorial CLI command. The synthetic generator remains a source-checkout-only repository script (scripts/generate_tutorial_data.py); it is not packaged in the wheel or sdist.
  • Release qualification now installs only the default/core dependency set. Optional extras (ml, hnsw, watch, tui, chem) remain experimental and unqualified.

docs.title: Changed — release publication
docs.text: • The guarded release workflow can upload the exact qualified wheel and sdist to PyPI with GitHub Actions OIDC Trusted Publishing. It uses no long-lived API token and does not rebuild distributions in the publish job.

docs.title: Changed — release packaging and export claims
docs.text:
• Adopt the owned PyPI distribution name massflow-msms while keeping the MassFlow import package and massflow command unchanged. The previous massflow name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project.
  • Withdraw the stable mzTab-M conformance claim. format: mztab now writes an explicit experimental, non-conformant mzTab-shaped table and omits the mzTab-version header. CSV remains the stable supported export.

docs.title: Fixed — fragment filtering and cache semantics (#95)
docs.text:
• Apply filter_by_mz to fragment peaks only; retain spectra whose precursor lies outside the fragment window. Preserve intensity/count order, the current empty-spectrum policy and the fixed 5 ppm physical-integrity gate.
  • Include an explicit processing-semantics revision in canonical cache/build fingerprints. Managed prepared caches rebuild without mixing legacy rows; explicit persistent store inputs require a manual rebuild from raw sources into a new destination. See the processing guide for migration and PR #103 integration requirements.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Opt-in retrieval-funnel diagnostics (similarity.collect_retrieval_diagnostics) emit a versioned JSON sidecar with bounded typed preprocessing rejections, sequential target/decoy pair-stage counts, mutually exclusive query outcomes, confidence states, effective configuration, and input/library fingerprints. The benchmark harness keeps truth labels separate and adds query-level truth-record loss/rank attribution. Diagnostics do not alter scoring or candidate order; unknown causes remain explicitly unattributed.

  • Added massflow annotate --build-library-store to prepare or reuse the configured SQLite/hybrid/Zarr reference store without scoring queries, using the existing strict physical-integrity gate and build provenance. See CLI reference.

  • massflow tutorial CLI command: First-class command that generates a self-contained synthetic dataset (reference library, experimental queries, and pre-configured YAML) for instant local evaluation. No external files required.
  • Enhanced tutorial generator: scripts/generate_tutorial_data.py now prints formatted next-steps with the exact db build and annotate commands to run after generation.
  • Hybrid SQLite + Zarr storage (Phase 1): SpectralDatabase now supports a hybrid mode (zarr_path=... or --backend hybrid) where SQLite retains metadata plus a zarr_ref/zarr_index reference pair and fragment arrays live in a chunked, compressed ZarrPeakArrayStore with lock-free concurrent reads for multiprocessing.
  • BLOB → Zarr migration: scripts/migrations/0002_blobs_to_zarr.py (wrapping MassFlow.database.migrate_blobs_to_zarr) migrates existing SQLite BLOB libraries to the hybrid backend with per-batch bitwise verification, idempotent re-runs, and orphaned-array recovery.
  • Algorithmic acceleration (Phase 2): Numba-accelerated peak/neutral-loss prefilter (MassFlow.acceleration) that skips query-reference pairs below min_matched_peaks before exact modified-cosine scoring, with identical results and a pure-NumPy fallback.
  • HNSW candidate retrieval (Phase 2): MassFlow.hnsw wraps hnswlib for sub-linear approximate candidate generation over binned spectral vectors, integrated into CascadeEngine as an optional pre-stage. Construction parameters (hnsw_m, hnsw_ef_construction, hnsw_ef_search, hnsw_candidates_per_query, binning) are exposed in SimilarityConfig with recall-friendly defaults because spectral similarity is non-metric. Requires the new [hnsw] extra.
  • Entropy-based decoy generation (Phase 3): generate_decoys now produces entropy-preserving decoys that keep the precursor m/z and the Shannon entropy (ion information content) of each target while randomizing fragmentation pathways via intensity permutation and fragment-position jitter, replacing naive fragment shuffling. ProcessingConfig gains decoy_min_relative_intensity (strict baseline noise filtering before entropy computation) and decoy_mz_shift_da; the workflow logs a target-decoy entropy-divergence diagnostic for FDR calibration.
  • Real-time streaming hardening (Phase 4): the gRPC StreamSpectra path now routes every packet through the ConsensusEngine (weighted multi-engine scoring) and enforces quality-gated backpressure: when the bounded queue reaches a configurable high-water mark, low-quality spectra are shed (reported via the new ServerStatus.spectra_dropped_low_quality field) to prevent memory exhaustion and latency collapse under instrument overrun. massflow serve gains --queue-high-water-mark and --queue-low-quality-threshold; GetStatus now also reports rolling processing latency.
  • ML API boundary (Phase 5): external ML scoring is now fully decoupled behind MLEngineProtocol: SimilarityConfig.ml_endpoints routes Spec2Vec/MS2DeepScore scoring to remote REST (http(s)://) or gRPC (grpc://, the new massflow.v1.ml service) services via a CircuitBreaker-protected RemoteMLEngine client (no heavy dependencies required in core). ConsensusEngine, CascadeEngine, MLRouter, and the workflow now degrade gracefully to modified_cosine + empirical p-values when the ML service is unreachable or PyTorch/Gensim are missing.
  • Audit fix — HNSW neutral-loss channel: spectrum_to_binned_vector now encodes a 2-channel concatenated vector [binned exact m/z, binned neutral losses], so HNSW candidate retrieval can find precursor-shifted analogues (modified-cosine matches with disjoint exact m/z) that an exact-m/z-only index was blind to. bin_spectra and HNSWSpectralIndex dimensionality updated accordingly.
  • Audit fix — spectral entropy physics: spectral_entropy and the decoy generator now apply the spectral-entropy I**0.5 weighting and a hard baseline filter (peaks below decoy_min_relative_intensity × the base peak, default 1%) before computing the information content, preventing chemical noise from inflating entropy and biasing FDR calibration.
  • Golden scientific-validation suite: tests/test_scientific_validation.py locks down the scientific contract end-to-end with known-answer assertions — perfect and near spectral matches (hand-computed cosine), precursor-mass and adduct violations, RT-tolerance filtering, deterministic entropy-preserving decoys, the per-query target-decoy FDR contract, duplicate-score ranking, large-peak-count round trips, and SQLite/Zarr storage equivalence (byte-identical result CSVs). The known-answer fixture set is produced deterministically by tests/scientific_validation/generate_ground_truth.py (the previously committed static MGF fixtures were removed); the suite runs in the default test selection under the scientific marker and explicitly in CI. See docs/user-guide/scientific_validation.md.
  • Terminal console (massflow tui): a keyboard-first interactive console for finding, uploading, viewing, and identifying MS/MS data without leaving the terminal. Four tabs — Browser (recursive spectral-file discovery, vendor-format conversion hints, collision-safe upload into a workspace directory, library inspector), Viewer (interactive centroid stick plot with precursor marker; metadata panel with precursor m/z, RT, charge, adduct, base peak, TIC, spectral entropy), Identify (target-decoy search with q-value/p-value calibration, ranked hits, mirror plots), and Diagnostics (plain-English fixes plus the massflow_quarantine.log tail). New options --input, --library, --workspace (default ./massflow_workspace); requires the new [tui] extra (textual>=8). Experimental — outside the stable product contract. See docs/api/tui.md and tests/test_tui_*.py.
  • Physical-integrity gate in the classical annotation paths (D-8 executed, see docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md): MassFlow.processing now runs the existing SpectrumMetadata/MolecularStructure 5 ppm contracts (MassFlow.models) on every spectrum that declares a structural claim (formula/SMILES/InChI) after matchms harmonization, via processing.physical_integrity_reason (wired into process_spectra/process_spectra_batch with an optional rejection reporter). Malformed structural metadata (unparseable formula/SMILES/InChI claims, formula/exact-mass conflicts beyond 5 ppm, non-registry adducts in a complete context) and >5 ppm precursor deviations are rejected with human-readable reasons, quarantine-logged, and never searched. Spectra without structural claims are exempt (raw experimental files pay no measurable cost; envelope auto-fill is suppressed in the gate — it is not consumed by the classical path). Semantics: query files count rejections in spectra_rejected with reasons surfaced in the failure report when the file fails; raw reference libraries abort annotate/watch with processing.PhysicalIntegrityError before any file is processed (a silently shrunk pool would corrupt every query's FDR calibration) and the partial store is removed; db build quarantines invalid entries (curation workflow). massflow annotate prints run-level failures to the console. Tests: tests/test_physics_gate.py; docs updated (docs/user-guide/validation.md, docs/user-guide/data-requirements.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/index.md).
  • Library-build provenance (lineage schema): SQLite-backed stores now persist a lightweight lineage history — store_meta (schema version, first-open timestamp) and library_builds (PRAGMA user_version >= 1). Every db build, db merge, and annotate library-store build records the input file(s) used with a streaming SHA-256, the effective config hash (config_digest_sha256), the processing fingerprint, full processing and similarity (target-decoy) configuration JSON, the MassFlow version, and an exact UTC timestamp; merges additionally list their input databases and per-input spectrum counts in details.merged_sources. The schema is additive and idempotent raw SQL (pre-provenance databases self-upgrade on their next open; scientific payload bytes are untouched; Zarr stores are not modified). massflow db inspect is now a lineage query surface: it reports store metadata, the full build history (library versions), the recorded processing parameters, and the target-decoy configuration. The annotate YAML sidecar gains a library: block linking every result to the exact store searched and its library_builds row (build id, built-at timestamp, source file, config digest, processing fingerprint) so run config can be checked against build config. Programmatic access: SpectralDatabase.record_library_build / get_library_builds / get_latest_library_build / get_schema_version / get_store_created_at; MassFlow.library.processing_fingerprint is now public. Tests: tests/test_db_lineage.py. Docs: docs/user-guide/database.md, docs/user-guide/results.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
  • Pre-flight validation (fail fast before any expensive work): massflow annotate, db build, and db merge now validate their inputs before any library store is built or any file is searched. MassFlow.workflow.preflight_annotation_run (wired into run_annotation_pipeline before the output directory is even created) checks, in order: (1) the configured similarity surface can be constructed with the installed optional extras — a pure ML engine such as spec2vec without massflow-msms[ml] aborts here with the install instruction instead of crashing workers as an opaque BrokenProcessPool after the store build; (2) the reference library is configured, exists, and is a loadable open-format/store input — vendor raw libraries and unknown formats abort before any temporary store is created; (3) the query input exists and is dispatchable — a direct vendor file/.d input aborts up-front, while vendor files inside a directory are announced at run start and keep the documented explicit per-file failure semantics. Missing optional extras that degrade instead of abort (consensus/cascade without [ml], cascade + hnsw_enabled: true without [hnsw]) are emitted as run-start warnings carrying the pip install massflow-msms[...] fix (MassFlow.workflow.optional_extra_warnings). db build rejects vendor/unloadable sources and db merge rejects missing or non-store inputs before the output database file is created (previously an empty .db was left behind). CLI failures now print a plain-English fix: hint line via MassFlow.tui.diagnostics.suggest_fix (new HNSW branch) instead of a bare error; no failing run leaves output artifacts. Single-source-of-truth loadability helpers io.is_vendor_raw / io.is_loadable_spectral_input / io.is_store_input (with a canonical vendor error message) back both the loader and the pre-flight checks. Tests: tests/test_preflight.py; README gains a documented "happy path" (input → library build → annotation → export → inspect). Docs: docs/user-guide/annotation.md (Pre-flight validation + tightened vendor handling), docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md.
  • Adduct registry expansion & notation normalisation (issue #72): MassFlow.cheminformatics now recognises the adducts that dominate real library exports and resolves the many ways a file may spell them. New registry entries: positive mode [M+3H]3+, [M+2Na-H]+, [M+H-H2O]+, [M+CH3CN+H]+, [M+CH3OH+H]+; negative mode [M-2H]2-, [M+Br]-, [M+I]-, [M+TFA-H]-, [M+HCO3]-, [M+NO3]-. The new public cheminformatics.normalize_adduct canonicalises notation variants (M+H, M+Na, [M+H]1+, [M+H]+1, [m+h]+, interior whitespace, unbalanced brackets, and alias chemistry such as M+FA-H, M+OAc, M+ACN+H, M-H2O+H) onto the registry keys. Normalisation fails closed: a notation whose declared charge contradicts the chemistry ([M+H]2+), a charge-less ambiguous body (M), or chemistry outside the registry ([M+Weird]+) still resolves to None and is still rejected by the gate. compute_adduct_offset and calculate_theoretical_mass accept the same variants, and SpectrumMetadata stores the canonical spelling while metadata_processing canonicalises it during ingestion, so the physics gate, database columns, triage, and exports all agree on one form. Notably, normalisation cannot manufacture false positives — a resolved adduct must still clear the 5 ppm precursor gate. Tests: tests/test_adduct_registry.py; docs: docs/user-guide/validation.md, docs/user-guide/data-requirements.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Annotate input discovery includes .baf (vendor-format tightening): directory discovery now derives its vendor extension set from io.PROPRIETARY_FORMATS (which includes Bruker .baf), so a .baf file inside an input directory produces an explicit per-file failed result like every other vendor raw format instead of being silently ignored. Vendor handling is documented in docs/user-guide/annotation.md.
  • Strict configuration validation (config audit): all Pydantic configuration models now reject unknown keys (extra="forbid") — a misspelled key such as ms2_tolerence fails immediately with a human-readable error carrying the YAML line number, a spelling suggestion (when one is close), and the allowed keys. Relative paths (project.output_directory, input.input_path, input.library_path) now resolve relative to the YAML configuration file's directory instead of the caller's working directory, making runs deterministic regardless of the invocation CWD; the legacy CWD-relative behavior is available via the documented MASSFLOW_COMPAT_CWD_PATHS=1 environment variable. Invalid combinations now fail at validation time instead of silently doing nothing: hnsw_enabled requires algorithm='cascade', reduce_to_top_n_peaks requires a positive n_max, cascade_stages/consensus_weights must reference leaf engines with positive weights, and cascade_upper_bound >= cascade_lower_bound. The batch processing path now honors the documented filter_min_peaks / filter_by_mz toggles (it previously dropped spectra by min_peaks/precursor mz_max even when the toggles were off). A normalized configuration representation (schema version, source config path, full effective config with resolved paths, SHA-256 digest) is written into provenance: a run-level run_provenance.json in the output directory before expensive processing, plus a config: section in every per-file report sidecar. See docs/user-guide/configuration.md and tests/test_config_strictness.py.
  • Failure model (per-file execution results): every experimental input file now produces a structured FileExecutionResult (status success/degraded/failed, input path, spectra loaded, spectra rejected, hits produced, output path, warnings, fatal errors, degraded-mode flags). A file whose data could not be loaded, validated, or scored is reported as failed with an explicit <stem>_failed.report.yaml sidecar and no results CSV (an empty CSV can no longer be mistaken for a successful annotation). Batch runs continue across failed files, worker crashes are synthesized into failed results, and massflow annotate exits nonzero when any file failed. Spectrum-level rejections (I/O validation and processing drops) are counted and recorded in the provenance; engine fallbacks (classical, consensus, cascade, routing, HNSW) and uncalibrated FDR are surfaced as degraded_mode_flags. Unsupported vendor formats are now explicit per-file failures with a conversion hint instead of disappearing from the batch. Cascade mid-stage failures fall back to classical scoring instead of silently returning no results. See docs/user-guide/results.md (Failure Model) and tests/test_failure_model.py.
  • Per-query target-decoy FDR contract (statistical audit): the FDR competition unit is now the query spectrum — each query contributes its best target hit and its best decoy hit exactly once — instead of pooling every threshold-passing hit. Ties are ranked decoys-first (conservative). The empirical p-value is a per-query diagnostic column and is never used as a filter; the small-library Bonferroni branch was removed (it silently compared FWER-corrected p-values against fdr_threshold). The true reference-library size is now threaded through the single-file and streaming execution paths (previously derived from empty worker-local state, forcing every such run into the small-library branch). Decoy generation is chunk-invariant (content-hashed per-spectrum seeds) and honors processing.decoy_* in every execution mode. Cascade now scores decoys when include_decoys=True (previously it never did). The streaming gRPC path reports fdr_q_value = NaN (uncalibrated) instead of a placeholder 1.0. See docs/user-guide/scoring_logic.md for the full contract and tests/test_fdr_statistics.py for the regression suite.
  • Onboarding overhaul: Rewrote docs/user-guide/usage.md to use real, runnable tutorial file paths instead of hypothetical placeholders. Added Step 0 (Generate Tutorial Data) so a copy-paste follower can complete the full workflow without FileNotFoundError.
  • README and ARCHITECTURE docs: Added massflow tutorial to stable feature lists, CLI command references, and quickstart sections. Fixed a stray similarity: key in the README YAML example.
  • Config storage backends: input.storage_backend now accepts "hybrid" in addition to "sqlite" and "zarr"; massflow db inspect auto-detects hybrid databases by their sibling .zarr store.
  • Worker-owned library backends (multiprocessing redesign): the annotation engine no longer serializes the full processed reference library (and its decoys) into every ProcessPoolExecutor worker. MassFlow.library.prepare_library normalizes raw-format libraries into a worker-openable store in the parent (store inputs such as .db/.zarr are used directly), and only a compact LibrarySpec (path/kind/backend, ~185 B pickled) crosses the process boundary. Workers open the store themselves and stream processed spectra in bounded 10k-spectrum chunks, so per-worker RSS is bounded by one chunk and parent RSS is flat regardless of library size or worker count. Measured on macOS/Python 3.13 (spawn): 8-worker spawn wall time drops from 33–54 s to ~0.02 s at 100k spectra, with byte-identical results locked by golden CSVs asserted in tests/test_library.py (decoy generation remains chunk-invariant). The memory model and reproduction steps are documented in docs/multiprocessing.md (scripts/benchmark_multiprocessing.py).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Missing precursor values remain missing: batch processing preserves absent, malformed, and non-finite precursor m/z as float64 NaN rather than a fabricated zero. The configured m/z filter applies to fragment peaks and does not make precursor availability an eligibility gate.
  • Modified-cosine recall: combine direct-fragment and neutral-loss prefilter counts so mixed-frame matches survive the default three-peak gate. Full matchms greedy scoring still enforces one-to-one peak use. See the synthetic experiment.
  • Normalize retention times to seconds with source-unit evidence, preserve that metadata through SQLite/Zarr/hybrid reconstruction, and compare against explicit similarity.rt_tolerance_unit (seconds or minutes). Legacy unitless tolerances retain actual seconds behavior with a migration warning. Managed raw-library caches rebuild; explicit legacy stores require a rebuild from source. CSV exports add explicit time-unit/provenance columns. See issue #122 and the migration guidance.
  • Golden CSV tests made platform-portable (they failed on Linux): the byte-exact CSV-digest assertions in tests/test_library.py::TestGoldenDeterminism and tests/test_scientific_validation.py::TestGoldenPipelineRuns failed on Linux because scores are exported at full float64 precision and macOS (Accelerate) and Linux (OpenBLAS) round the low-order bits differently — identical scientific results, different bytes. Comparison is now by value: column order, row counts, categorical/integer fields and matched-peak counts are compared exactly, numeric fields within a tight tolerance (~1e-9), and within a query the exported rows are compared as a set ordered by score then reference (score-tie order is not part of the contract). The SQLite/Zarr equivalence test runs both backends on the same platform (a portable byte-for-byte check). No production output or scientific contract changed; the manifest still records csv_sha256 for provenance. Docs updated (docs/multiprocessing.md, docs/user-guide/scientific_validation.md).
  • Worker pool no longer forks (fixes a Linux hang in CI and a latent production risk): run_annotation_pipeline built its ProcessPoolExecutor without an explicit start method, so Linux used fork while macOS already used spawn. Forking a multi-threaded process copies the other threads' lock state into the child while dropping the threads themselves, so a child that needs a lock held at fork time deadlocks forever. That is reachable in practice: under pytest the process accumulates threads (an asyncio event loop and thread-pool workers) from earlier tests — which hung the Ubuntu CI job in tests/test_provenance.py for hours — and the streaming server carries a live event loop by design. The pool now pins multiprocessing.get_context("spawn") explicitly (MassFlow.workflow._WORKER_MP_CONTEXT), matching the benchmarked configuration, with a regression test asserting the start method. See docs/multiprocessing.md.
  • Ionisation-mode gate misread adduct notation (found reviewing #72): the compatibility gate in SimilarityEngine.search classified a candidate pair as "opposite ionisation modes" whenever the two adduct strings each contained both a + and a - character, so [M+HCOO]- vs [M-H]- (both negative) and [M+H-H2O]+ vs [M+H]+ (both positive) were silently discarded before scoring. The #72 registry expansion grew the dual-sign population from 3 to 7 of 22 entries, making the latent defect substantially more reachable. Ionisation mode is now read from the resolved adduct charge via the new MassFlow.cheminformatics.adduct_charge; notation the registry cannot resolve falls back to its trailing charge token and otherwise still means "no opinion", so only genuinely opposite-mode pairs are dropped. Tests: tests/test_similarity_internals.py, tests/test_adduct_registry.py.
  • Adduct-notation rejections at ingestion (issue #72) — a registry-coverage gap, not a mass error: real .msp/.mgf libraries write the same ion in many ways, and every spelling the strict 5 ppm gate could not resolve flagged an otherwise correct spectrum is_physically_valid = False, quarantining it at ingestion. Canonical strings such as [M+H]+ already resolved; M+H, M+Na, [M+H]1+, [m+h]+, and alias chemistry such as [M+FA-H]- / M+OAc did not, and adducts common in public libraries ([M+2Na-H]+, [M+TFA-H]-, [M+H-H2O]+, [M-2H]2-, …) were absent from the registry entirely. Notation is now canonicalised before lookup and the registry covers those adducts (the legacy [M+FA-H]- spelling resolves to its canonical [M+HCOO]- key). Gate semantics are unchanged: an unresolvable adduct still fails closed and the 5 ppm tolerance is untouched. Tests: tests/test_adduct_registry.py.
  • Zero decoy hits on real-world runs (fdr_uncalibrated) — root cause, diagnostics, and honest labeling (issue #68): an investigation on the MASSBANK benchmark store showed that the decoy null is empty by geometry, not because a decoy is lost: generate_decoys displaces every fragment by ±processing.decoy_mz_shift_da (1.0 Da default), i.e. 50× the 0.02 Da MS2 scoring tolerance, so decoys can never satisfy the positional min_matched_peaks/min_score gates (measured: 0 decoy rows out of 195,737 scored decoy pairs vs 16,264 target rows in the recorded modified-cosine run). The 5 ppm/MS1 precursor gate is not involved — decoys preserve precursor_mz bit-for-bit and pass the same window as their targets (verified in Da and 5 ppm modes). Decoys are now faithful null objects (they keep their source's complete peak list — the baseline filter only selects which intensities are permuted — so a decoy is never systematically less matchable than the library spectrum it stands in for), and the empty-null state is diagnosable and honest: SimilarityEngine.decoy_diagnostics reports n_decoy_pairs_scored, best_decoy_score, n_decoy_scores_above_min_score/above_gates, n_decoy_hits and decoy_null_empty for the whole (chunk-aggregated) search; the engine flags decoy_null_empty, the workflow flags fdr_uncalibrated and its warning now carries the measured best decoy score; the engine warns when decoy_mz_shift_da is below the MS2 tolerance (near-copy decoys inflate the null and reject genuine annotations); and rows of an uncalibrated run are exported with Annotation_Status: Uncalibrated instead of Matched/Putative, so a score-filtered candidate list can never be read as an FDR-controlled result. No production threshold, precursor gate, or q-value formula was changed. Tests: tests/test_decoy_competition_path.py; docs: docs/user-guide/scoring_logic.md (§5.1), docs/user-guide/results.md.
  • Unified storage backend interface (storage audit): MassFlow.storage.SpectralStore is now the single backend interface consumed by every workflow — annotation workers, CLI database commands, and the streaming server. It supports everything the annotation engine needs: metadata lookup (metadata_query, now also implemented on the SQLite backend), precursor-range filtering (get_precursor_mz_range, precursor_mz metadata queries), sequential iteration (get_spectra/iter_spectra), batched access (batch_get_arrays, iter_processed_chunks), spectrum count, and backend_provenance(). The duplicate LibraryBackend protocol and StoreLibraryBackend wrapper were removed; open_library returns a SpectralStore; the raw-file fallback is now RawFileLibraryStore, a read-only SpectralStore adapter (writes rejected explicitly); the streaming server loads its reference library through the same interface. storage_backend now has one unambiguous meaning: prepare_library builds the library store in the configured backend (<stem>_library.db for sqlite/hybrid, <stem>_library.zarr for zarr), the store cache key includes the backend, and run provenance records the EFFECTIVE backend actually used. Contract tests (tests/test_storage_contract.py) run the same search against SQLite, Zarr, and hybrid libraries and assert identical spectrum IDs, precursor metadata, peak arrays, similarity scores, and ranking order.
  • Pytest discovery & test groups (repo audit): explicit discovery is configured (testpaths = ["tests"]) so scratch/exploratory tests under scripts/experiments/ are never collected, and the default pytest selection runs exactly the release suite (unit + integration + scientific-validation) while excluding benchmark, slow, and optional tests unless requested. Markers are registered and --strict-markers is enforced; tests/benchmarks/ is benchmark-marked via conftest; scientific-validation files carry a module-level scientific marker; optional-dependency tests (hnswlib-backed HNSW) are marked optional and properly skip when the extra is missing (the previously failing test_hnsw_parameters_flow_to_index no longer breaks local runs). CI now verifies formatting (ruff format --check), linting, type checking, the release suite with coverage, the scientific group explicitly, and the optional group explicitly, on the declared supported matrix (Python 3.13 × Linux/macOS, declared via trove classifiers). Benchmarks and slow tests never run in CI and cannot block ordinary runs. See CONTRIBUTING.md (Tests) and .github/workflows/ci.yml.
  • Reproducible packaging (release audit): uv.lock is now explicitly committed (it was tracked but listed in .gitignore). The supported Python version is explicit (requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14", .python-version = 3.13); the stale [project.optional-dependencies] dev extra was removed (the dev tooling lives in [dependency-groups] dev); CI installs strictly from the lockfile (uv sync --frozen) and fails when the lockfile is out of date (uv lock --check). Two people checking out the same commit can recreate the same environment with uv sync --frozen. See docs/getting-started/installation.md (Reproducible Environments).
  • First-class run provenance: every completed annotation run now writes run_provenance.json (counter-suffixed per run) recording: MassFlow version, git SHA + dirty flag, Python version/implementation/platform, resolved dependency versions, the committed lockfile SHA-256, the normalized configuration with its digest, engine/processing configuration, storage backend, decoy seed and parameters, per-input-file SHA-256 hashes, the reference-library digest, run start/completion timestamps, and the completion summary (per-status counts, aggregated warnings, degraded-mode flags, failed files). The record is written before per-file processing begins and finalized afterwards; it is deterministic except for the explicitly time-varying fields (run_started_at, completed_at). See docs/user-guide/results.md (Run-Level Provenance) and tests/test_provenance.py.
  • Zarr peak fidelity (storage audit): storing a spectrum can no longer silently change its scientific data. The tensor layout previously truncated over-capacity spectra to the first max_peaks_per_spectrum peaks with no warning or record. Now: (1) over-capacity spectra raise PeakCapacityError by default (peak_reduction="none"), rejecting the batch atomically; (2) an explicit peak_reduction="topN" policy retains the N most intense peaks deterministically and records the reduction in per-spectrum provenance (extra_metadata.peak_reduction), which round-trips into reconstructed spectra; (3) the layout, capacity, and reduction policy are persisted in a store manifest and validated on every open, so a store reopened with mismatched parameters fails loudly instead of misreading its data; (4) legacy pre-manifest stores are inferred from their arrays and may only be opened with the strict policy. The flat layout (and the hybrid ZarrPeakArrayStore) store every peak exactly with no capacity. See tests/test_zarr_store.py (TestPeakFidelity, TestTopNReduction, TestStoreManifest, TestSimilarityEquivalenceAcrossStorage).
  • Streaming server security (audit): the gRPC streaming server previously bound [::] (all interfaces) with plaintext transport and an unauthenticated control plane that could replace the configuration and load arbitrary server-side library paths mid-stream. Now: (1) the default bind is loopback-only (127.0.0.1); (2) non-loopback binds require TLS (--tls-cert/--tls-key) or an explicit --allow-insecure-remote override that emits a prominent warning and an audit-log entry; (3) TLS is supported via grpc.ssl_server_credentials; (4) every control-plane operation requires the admin token (--admin-token / MASSFLOW_ADMIN_TOKEN, authorization: Bearer <token> metadata, constant-time comparison) and the control plane is disabled entirely when no token is configured; (5) SET_CONFIG/LOAD_LIBRARY additionally require --allow-remote-control and apply transactionally (a failed reload leaves the running state intact); (6) every administrative action is audit-logged to massflow.streaming.security with peer, command, and outcome; (7) message size, control-payload (1 MiB), and per-packet peak-count limits are enforced, and queue-rejected spectra always receive an explicit error response (no silent drops); (8) a single shared consumer routes responses strictly back to the owning connection — annotations can no longer leak across concurrent clients (the previous per-connection consumers crossed responses between clients). See docs/api/queue.md and tests/test_streaming_security.py.
  • Tooling deprecation & supply-chain hygiene: asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function" is now set explicitly in pyproject.toml, silencing the pytest-asyncio deprecation warning about the future default change (all async fixtures in the suite are function-scoped, so behavior is unchanged). The docs site no longer loads polyfill.io (mkdocs.yml) — the CDN changed ownership in 2024 and is a known supply-chain risk, and MathJax 3 requires no polyfills on supported browsers.
  • Docs accuracy (capability-audit follow-up): serve is documented as the deprecated alias of stream-server in the CLI/server guides (examples now use stream-server); the README quickstart YAML no longer enables hnsw_enabled under modified_cosine (an invalid combination under strict config validation); the unimplemented FBMN export and GraphML/massflow visualize workflows are explicitly marked as not shipped in docs/user-guide/results.md, docs/user-guide/annotation.md, docs/user-guide/configuration.md, and .github/copilot-instructions.md (matching docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md C-4/C-5); MassFlow.library and MassFlow.ml_client were added to docs/api_reference.md; the workflow config section no longer claims unimplemented toggles; the ML satellite example README warns that its reference servers are unauthenticated demos (loopback or TLS-terminated reverse proxy recommended).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Formal Data Model: Implemented Pydantic-based validation for all spectral metadata.
  • SQLite Backend: Added massflow db build to compile .msp/.mgf libraries into high-performance relational databases.
  • Flexible Validation: Added graceful fallbacks for in-house libraries lacking structural (SMILES) data.
  • Small Library Support: Introduced empirical p-value calculations as an alternative to target-decoy FDR for small datasets.
  • CLI Suite: Finalized init, db, and annotate command structure.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Refactored SimilarityEngine to use a factory pattern for easier algorithm swapping.
  • Optimized isotopic envelope generation to use vectorized NumPy operations.
  • Updated matchms filtering pipeline for stricter precursor mass consistency.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Resolved memory exhaustion when loading large (>2GB) MSP files.
  • Fixed floating-point precision errors in cosine similarity scoring.

docs.title: Complexity Audit & Subsystem Classification
docs.text:
STATUS: authoritative (2026-08-25). Companion to CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md: the capability matrix says what is in the product; this document says where the complexity lives, which tier each subsystem belongs to, and how the package boundary keeps experimental machinery from silently altering stable scientific behavior.

Classification legend:

Tier Meaning Change discipline Required (stable) Part of the v0.1 product contract. Removing or changing it is a product decision Must not regress; full test gate + coverage Optional but supported Installed/available by default, contract-tested, but not the default path Must keep contract tests green Experimental Implemented and tested, outside the support promise; must be visibly flagged and never silently alter stable behavior May evolve freely; guards/fallbacks required Deprecated Kept only for compatibility with existing configs/CLI invocations; warns on use Remove only at a schema/CLI bump Remove Dead, duplicated, or superseded; deleted in this pass —

docs.title: 1.1 src/MassFlow — core package
docs.text: Module Lines Tier Classification / rationale Boundary config.py 1140 Required (stable schema) + deprecated legacy fields Strict Pydantic schema (extra="forbid", line-numbered errors, relative-path resolution). Contains the deprecated SimilarityConfig.tolerance alias, ProcessingConfig.precursor_mz/retention_time legacy fields, SolventConfig (validated but not consumed by the pipeline), WorkflowConfig (empty placeholder kept for workflow: YAML compat), and MassFlowConfig.output_directory legacy property Deprecated fields warn or are inert; tolerance warns and maps onto ms2_tolerance; removal deferred to a schema bump io.py 520 Required File-system boundary: loaders (mzML/mzXML/MGF/MSP), validation layer, CSV exporter and experimental mzTab-shaped exporter, YAML reports, vendor-format rejection — processing.py ~500 Required matchms-based metadata/peak pipeline + the strict 5 ppm physical-integrity gate (physical_integrity_reason), which consumes the MassFlow.models contracts on spectra with declared structural claims Gate rejections are reported via the optional rejection_reporter and the quarantine logger; see CAPABILITY_MATRIX D-8 similarity.py 3135 Required (classical core) + experimental (meta/ML engines) Required: SimilarityEngine (cosine/modified_cosine), MS1 prefilter, generate_decoys, calculate_fdr, calibrate_query_level_fdr, calculate_empirical_p_values, spectral_entropy, SearchResult, get_similarity_engine factory. Experimental: ConsensusEngine, CascadeEngine, Spec2VecEngine, MS2DeepScoreEngine, MLRouter, entry-point discovery, remote-endpoint routing Experimental engines are flagged by workflow.experimental_surface_flags at the run boundary; ML engines raise RuntimeError when dependencies are missing (no silent swap); consensus/cascade degrade to classical only with explicit warnings + degraded-mode flags workflow.py ~1300 Required Orchestration, per-file failure model (FileExecutionResult), provenance, TDC block, worker-owned library backends, library-lineage sidecar payload (_build_library_provenance) Lineage payload attaches to every per-file result and is written into the YAML sidecar (library: section); LibrarySpec mechanism unchanged library.py ~530 Required Library normalization (prepare_library), worker-openable LibrarySpec, RawFileLibraryStore, public processing_fingerprint Fresh raw-library builds record a library_builds row (best-effort, sqlite/hybrid stores only) storage.py 382 Required SpectralStore — the single backend interface (metadata query, iteration, batched access, provenance) + factory — database.py ~2600 Required SpectralDatabase (SQLite/hybrid store), spectra + library-provenance schema (store_meta, library_builds, PRAGMA user_version >= 1), migrations, lineage queries (record_library_build, get_library_builds, get_latest_library_build, get_store_created_at, get_schema_version). Contains legacy-schema migration helpers (migrate_legacy_peaks_database, _decode_legacy_peaks_payload, LegacyDatabaseSchemaError) Provenance schema is additive raw SQL (no ORM/migration framework); recording is explicit (never on plain add_spectra), so scientific payload bytes are unaffected; legacy helpers are deprecated tooling for pre-array-schema DBs zarr_store.py 2463 Optional but supported ZarrSpectralStore/ZarrPeakArrayStore — supported alternative backend (storage_backend: zarr|hybrid), peak-fidelity contract (no silent truncation), storage-contract tests zarr is a core dependency (no extra); backend selected explicitly in config; default remains sqlite models.py, cheminformatics.py 386+727 Required 5 ppm precursor validation, adduct registry, isotopic envelopes Enforced as a processing gate on spectra with declared structural claims in the classical annotate/db build paths (D-8 executed; see CAPABILITY_MATRIX C-11/D-8) plus the streaming gate; processing.py hosts the gate (physical_integrity_reason) protocols.py 134 Experimental MLEngineProtocol — contract for the ML satellite boundary Only consumed by ML engines ml_client.py 573 Experimental Remote ML engines (REST/gRPC) + circuit breaker Only active when similarity.ml_endpoints is configured (flagged) hnsw.py 585 Experimental HNSW two-channel candidate index ([hnsw] extra) Only active inside cascade with hnsw_enabled=true (config-validated); flagged acceleration.py 521 Experimental Numba peak/neutral-loss prefilter: opt-in for modified_cosine; disabled by default until exact candidate-domain equivalence is qualified. HNSW spectral binning: experimental approximate retrieval with no recall guarantee Full scoring is the default; prefilter remains an explicitly experimental path convert.py 104 Experimental Thin wrapper around external ProteoWizard msconvert; the annotate pipeline rejects vendor formats CLI help marks it EXPERIMENTAL log_config.py 103 Required Structured logging setup — streaming/ (server 1189, engine 734, queue 542) 2465 Experimental gRPC streaming server (loopback default, TLS/auth, bounded queue); stream-server CLI command CLI help marks it EXPERIMENTAL; safe-by-default binds/auth tui/ (8 modules) 2114 Experimental Textual interactive console ([tui] extra) Extra-gated; CLI help marks it EXPERIMENTAL generated/ + streaming/generated/ 439 Experimental Compiled protobuf/gRPC stubs (ml + streaming) Excluded from lint; regenerated via scripts/protoc_gen.sh __init__.py 90 Required Public package surface; lazy submodule accessors Fixed in this pass: removed the dead try/except PackageNotFoundError version probe

docs.title: 1.2 CLI commands (cli.py)
