1. Independent scientific validation: authenticate source labels/acquisition independence and collect independent batches, matrices, modes, instruments and application-relevant truth. The frozen cohort is diagnostic only.
  2. Confidence calibration: nonempty or empty decoy nulls do not establish exchangeability, expected error control or candidate-specific probabilities. A calibrated-FDR claim remains unsupported.
  3. Legacy persistent stores: externally supplied SQLite/Zarr/hybrid libraries are intentionally not rewritten. Rebuild from raw sources into new destinations, inspect IDs/records, and switch paths only after human review.
  4. Installed artifact and platform qualification: build/install the candidate wheel and sdist outside this checkout, inspect package resources/dependencies, and test the declared Python/OS matrix. This local macOS run alone does not qualify Linux or other platforms. RDKit is an upstream transitive dependency.
  5. Manual release approval: tag/publication workflows still require a human approval gate and exact source/artifact hashes. This branch creates neither.

Calibration research is a blocker to a calibrated-FDR claim, not an excuse to ship misleading confidence or an unavoidable prerequisite to a transparent candidate-ranking tool with explicit unvalidated estimates. If a desired product claim exceeds the evidence, defer that claim instead of inventing an accuracy cutoff.

docs.title: Human-review handoff sequence
docs.text:
1. Review the single stabilization PR and its integration commit history, including the deliberately resolved #101/#105 fragment-window contract and processing semantics revision 4. Require hosted CI on Linux and macOS for this exact head.
  2. Review the frozen cohort comparison and its per-query/artifact hashes. The result is unchanged on this panel; the synthetic prefilter tests remain separate and do not establish measured-data recall or identification accuracy.
  3. Independently review source identity/provenance, confidence states, external-store migration instructions, package dependencies and clean-installed artifact checks.
  4. Retain the restricted candidate-retrieval contract; do not promote calibrated FDR, confirmed identity, or universal platform/adduct/matrix claims without new evidence.
  5. A separate explicit human release decision is required before any version bump, tag, merge, publication, or deployment. This work authorizes none of those actions.

The combined cache fingerprint is processing-semantics revision 4. Externally supplied native stores remain untouched. Rebuild from raw sources into a new destination, inspect record counts/IDs/metadata and only then switch library_path. Do not append corrected records into an old invalid store and call that migration.

docs.title: Scientific terminology and applicability
docs.text:
• Spectral similarity: agreement under a stated peak assignment/tolerance.
  • Candidate ranking: ordering possible library structures; repeated acquisition records must not fill a distinct-structure top-five metric.
  • Putative annotation: a candidate supported by the stated evidence and known limitations, not a confirmed identity.
  • Confirmed identification: requires application-appropriate independent experimental confirmation; a library score/q column alone is insufficient.

The initial measured benchmark addresses deposited positive-mode, singly protonated ESI MS2 standards under fixed preprocessing/tolerances. Full-key and connectivity endpoints are distinct. It does not establish stereo selectivity, matrix unknown identification, extraction recovery, negative/multiple-charge/adduct performance, concentration, detection limits or calibrated FDR. Original standard labels and acquisition independence must retain their actual evidence tier. Numerical tests prove software invariants; measured retrieval results support only their frozen cohort and conditions.

docs.title: Conservative Confidence and Release Preparation Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: execute inline with test-first changes and one independent final review. The user has explicitly authorized implementation and dedicated PRs; do not request another scope approval.

Goal: Make confidence reporting explicit and empirically honest, execute a real-data benchmark through the existing pipeline, and prepare a narrow 1.0 release decision.

Architecture: Independent benchmark scripts do not change scientific production scoring. Confidence semantics wrap the existing numerical estimator with nullable estimate/state/method/limitations; invalid numerical inputs fail explicitly. Preserve legacy numerical columns/filtering for compatibility and identify them as diagnostics when unavailable. Release documentation separates supported engineering behavior from empirical scientific validation.

Spec: The scientific validation program in the attached scientific-validation-program worktree; current user benchmark, FDR-audit and release-management instructions.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Preserve primary dirty/concurrent work; use managed worktrees and codex branches.
  • No synthetic data presented as experimental evidence; real fixtures carry original source/license/hash/accession.
  • No automatic merge, protected-branch mutation, package publication or official release.
  • Float64, fixed seeds, missing confidence distinct from zero, real chemistry validators and existing annotation pipeline.
  • Full mandatory coverage >=80%, lint/typing and meaningful adversarial tests.

docs.title: Task 1 — Confidence semantics
docs.text:
• [x] Add failing tests for explicit unavailable/estimated_uncalibrated/invalid states and independent numerical invariants.
  • [x] Reject nonfinite/invalid confidence inputs before ranking; keep legitimate numerical zero distinct from missing.
  • [x] Add per-file and per-row machine-readable method, scope, nullable estimate and limitations without asserting calibration or changing valid score ordering.
  • [x] Correct README/scoring/results claims, document legacy fields and prove output serialization.
  • [ ] Run full gates, review, commit and open dedicated draft PR.

docs.title: Task 2 — Experimental benchmark
docs.text:
• [ ] Inventory frozen MassBank release and predeclare data eligibility/selection before scoring.
  • [ ] Add failing metrics/manifests/integration tests; implement isolated runner and transparent pipeline observation.
  • [ ] Fetch/hash outside Git; document original ground truth and acquisition/duplicate limitations.
  • [ ] Execute present/absent libraries and both classical engines, saving every query and failure.
  • [ ] Publish small machine-readable results/report, verify gates and open dedicated draft PR.

docs.title: Task 3 — Release scope and gates
docs.text:
• [ ] Refresh exact PR heads/CI, packaging/optional-dependency and installation evidence.
  • [ ] Classify major features A–E, rank blockers and specify manual PR integration/migration sequence.
  • [ ] Make narrowly scoped documentation corrections and create only nonduplicate implementation issues.
  • [ ] Verify docs/artifacts, review and open release-preparation draft PR without version/release actions.

docs.title: Review focus
docs.text: Empty decoy null is not empirical calibration; few observations are reported as counts, not a magic sufficiency threshold. Query maxima are not candidate-specific confidence. Invalid/nonfinite inputs cannot silently disappear. Query/file partition and library redundancy can affect estimates. Real-data labels and source independence must not be upgraded by code or unit tests.

docs.title: Execution record
docs.text: A partial independent review demonstrated a valid finite tied-decoy undercount. The complete equal-score block correction is justified by an independent 1,156-vector-pair oracle; threshold selection may change for affected ties. Final frozen full suite: 1,393 passed, coverage 82.53%. The real-data benchmark executes in its separate worktree on clean commit 4dab3c2; all four metric dictionaries reproduce the earlier diagnostic. PR creation and release handoff remain the final delivery tasks, with no merging or publication.

docs.title: CLI Workflows
docs.text: The core of MassFlow v0.1 is the config-driven CLI. These workflows are designed to be fully reproducible, predictable, and simple enough to execute in an automated shell script or CI/CD pipeline.

docs.title: Standard Annotation
docs.text:
The annotate subcommand requires a single argument: the path to your validated YAML configuration file.

uv run massflow annotate --config massflow_config.yaml

docs.title: How It Works Under the Hood
docs.text:
When you execute this command, MassFlow orchestrates the following pipeline:

  1. Configuration Parsing (config.py): The YAML file is loaded and strictly validated against Pydantic schemas. If a path doesn't exist, or an invalid tolerance is provided, the pipeline fails fast before consuming heavy resources.
  2. Library Loading (io.py, database.py): MassFlow reads your reference library (e.g., library.msp or an optimized SQLite library.db).
  3. Reference Processing (processing.py): Every spectrum in the library is passed through the configured metadata harmonization and peak-filtering pipeline. Small libraries may trigger a configured-count warning. This is a diagnostic heuristic, not a validated minimum library size or evidence that a target/decoy estimate is calibrated.
  4. Experimental Input Discovery (workflow.py): The pipeline looks for your experimental data in the configured input_path. If it's a directory, MassFlow recursively discovers all supported open formats (mzML, MGF, etc.).
  5. Per-File Multiprocessing (workflow.py): Each experimental file is handed off to a separate worker process. MassFlow utilizes a Zero-I/O shared memory architecture, loading the reference library into RAM once, preventing redundant parsing across CPU cores.
  6. Query Processing (processing.py): The experimental queries are cleaned and filtered using the exact same configured pipeline as the reference library, ensuring parity for scoring.
  7. Chunked Searching (similarity.py): To avoid memory exhaustion, the worker searches the processed queries against the reference library in chunks using the configured engine (e.g., cosine).
  8. Confidence diagnostics (similarity.py): Decoys are scored and query-level numerical estimates are reported with estimated_uncalibrated, unavailable, or invalid states. The legacy fdr_threshold still filters candidates, but it does not provide calibrated FDR control.
  9. Reporting (io.py): Finally, MassFlow exports a clean result table for each experimental file, accompanied by a YAML sidecar file detailing the exact provenance of that run.

docs.title: Pre-flight validation (fail fast, before anything expensive)
docs.text:
Before any library store is built and before any file is searched, the workflow runs strict pre-flight sanity checks (MassFlow.workflow.preflight_annotation_run), so a misconfigured run fails in milliseconds — with a clear, actionable error — instead of after minutes of preparation, and never leaves partial store files behind:

  • Similarity surface availability: the configured engine (and ML router, when enabled) is constructed once in the parent process, using the same factory the workers use. A pure ML engine (e.g. spec2vec) requested without the [ml] extra aborts here with the plain-English install fix — it would otherwise crash every worker after the library store was built, surfacing as an opaque BrokenProcessPool.
  • Reference library: must be configured, must exist, and must be a loadable input (open-format .msp/.mgf/.mzML/.mzXML file or a MassFlow .db/.sqlite/.zarr store). Vendor raw libraries and unknown formats abort before any temporary store is created.
  • Query inputs: the configured input_path must exist. A direct single-file (or .d directory) vendor input aborts the run up-front; a directory must contain at least one dispatchable file. Vendor raw files inside a directory are announced at run start (with the conversion hint) and then keep the documented batch semantics below.

Warnings (never errors) are emitted for optional extras whose absence degrades results instead of aborting them — consensus/cascade without [ml] (classical sub-engines only) and cascade + hnsw_enabled: true without [hnsw] (exact scoring instead of HNSW candidate retrieval) — each carrying its pip install massflow-msms[...] fix. The CLI prints these before the run starts and prints a fix: hint line for every pre-flight failure (via MassFlow.tui.diagnostics), never a raw traceback.

docs.title: Interactive Live Reloading (watch)
docs.text:
If you are actively optimizing your data processing thresholds (e.g., tweaking noise_threshold or min_score), repeatedly running the full annotate pipeline can be tedious. MassFlow provides an interactive, live-reloading terminal UI:

uv run massflow watch --config massflow_config.yaml

Features: * Real-time Previews: Displays a live Rich table of the top 15 results directly in your terminal. * Hot-Reloading: The pipeline automatically re-triggers the moment you save changes to your massflow_config.yaml or any files in your input_path. * Silent Error Handling: If you make a typo in your config, watch mode will catch the error, display it, and wait for your next save without crashing.

docs.title: Vendor File Conversion (convert)
docs.text:
MassFlow is intentionally conservative at the I/O boundary. The core annotate pipeline explicitly supports only open spectral formats:

  • .mzML / .mzXML
  • .MGF / .MSP
  • .db / .sqlite / .zarr (MassFlow native libraries)

docs.title: Unsupported vendor raw formats
docs.text:
Vendor raw formats are never auto-converted and are never silently ignored. The following extensions are rejected with an explicit UnsupportedVendorFormatError when handed to the loader (.raw Thermo, .d Agilent/Bruker directories, .wiff AB Sciex, .lcd Shimadzu, .t2d Bruker, .baf Bruker):

  • .raw
  • .d
  • .wiff
  • .lcd
  • .t2d
  • .baf

How rejection surfaces depends on how the file reaches the pipeline:

  • Reference library / db build input: a vendor raw library (e.g. library.raw as input.library_path, or massflow db build --input on a vendor file) aborts pre-flight with the conversion error — before any temporary store or output database is created (previously an empty store file was left behind by the late loader failure).
  • Single file input (input_path → one vendor file, or a .d directory): the annotate run fails at pre-flight with the conversion error, before the library store is built.
  • Directory input: vendor files inside the scanned directory are announced up-front (pre-flight warning with the conversion hint) and dispatched like any other input; each produces an explicit per-file failed result with the conversion hint and a <stem>_failed.report.yaml sidecar. The remaining open-format files are still processed (batch robustness), and the CLI exits nonzero. Vendor files are not silently skipped during discovery.
  • The quarantine log is not involved — rejection happens before parsing, because the format itself is unsupported.
  • massflow db merge rejects missing or non-store inputs before the output database is created.

To use vendor data, convert it to an open format first. MassFlow provides a wrapper command around ProteoWizard's msconvert:

uv run massflow convert --input data/raw_files/ --output data/mzml_files/

Note: You must have ProteoWizard installed on your system and available in your PATH for this command to work. convert is an experimental convenience wrapper; the core pipeline itself never performs vendor conversion.

docs.title: Network Visualization (not shipped)
docs.text:
Not implemented

Molecular networking / GraphML export and the massflow visualize command are planned, not implemented in the current release. The configuration key and this workflow do not exist yet — do not rely on them. See docs/index.md (Stable vs. Experimental) and docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md for the authoritative capability list.

docs.title: Benchmarking reference-library retrieval
docs.text: scripts/benchmark_real_corpus.py evaluates cross-instrument retrieval: spectra from one acquisition are searched against a known spectral library, and a retrieved reference is called correct when its InChIKey connectivity block matches the known query label. This is a retrieval benchmark. It does not measure identification of compounds in an unknown sample.

docs.title: Metric contract
docs.text:
The report uses query-level units. “Selected” means every labeled query chosen for the benchmark, including queries that the preprocessing peak-count gate rejects before scoring. “Searched” means selected queries that pass that gate. An accepted call is a query with at least one candidate at the stated score, matched-peak, and (when enabled) q-value operating point.

Report field Numerator Denominator Meaning end_to_end_top1_accuracy Correct top-ranked compound calls All selected queries Headline retrieval accuracy, including preprocessing rejections and no-candidate queries as failures conditional_top1_accuracy Correct top-ranked compound calls Searched queries Ranking/retrieval performance conditional on passing preprocessing call_coverage_selected Queries with an accepted candidate All selected queries Fraction of the selected set receiving an accepted call call_coverage_searched Queries with an accepted candidate Searched queries Fraction of searched queries receiving an accepted call accepted_call_accuracy Correct top-ranked compound calls Queries with an accepted candidate Accuracy among accepted calls; undefined (null) when there are no calls true_compound_retrieval_rate_selected Queries with the true compound anywhere among retained candidates All selected queries Candidate-generation reachability across the selected set rank1_of_reachable Correct top-ranked compound calls Queries with the true compound among retained candidates Ranking success conditional on candidate reachability candidate_rows_exported Candidate rows in the saved result table Not a rate; this is a count Export volume, not a query metric

For a headline, use end_to_end_top1_accuracy and print its correct-call and selected-query counts beside it, along with preprocessing-rejected and searched counts. Label it cross-instrument reference-library retrieval and state that it is not unknown-sample identification. Report instrument-specific values as well as the pooled result when the query set spans instruments. A pooled metric can conceal a source-specific failure; investigate and disclose large coverage differences or a source with zero calls before presenting the pooled result as representative.

The candidate-row ratio for a paired report is current candidate_rows_exported / baseline candidate_rows_exported. It is a row-volume ratio, not a multiplicative change in candidates per query or an accuracy change. The report also gives the percent wall-time change. A zero baseline row count makes the ratio undefined (null). The paired comparison also flags operating-system, CPU architecture, and Python-version differences; interpret wall-time changes cautiously when any of these differ.

docs.title: Reproducing and comparing runs
docs.text:
Run the benchmark from the repository root with a fresh work directory. For 300 selected queries per input instrument, pass --max-queries 300; the selection can be smaller if the source corpus has fewer eligible records. The default preprocessing gate is --min-query-peaks 3. Its rejected queries remain in the end-to-end denominator. The October 18 cross-instrument cohort is recreated with seed 20260921, 300 queries per QTOF/LTQ file, QExactive as the library, cosine, min_score=0.4, min_matched_peaks=3, fdr_threshold=1.0, and matched MS1/MS2 tolerances of 0.01/0.01 Da (narrow) or 0.02/0.02 Da (wide). These settings are not defaults; keep them explicit when reproducing that experiment. Example:

uv run python scripts/benchmark_real_corpus.py \
  --corpus /path/to/msp \
  --workdir /tmp/massflow-benchmark-baseline \
  --max-queries 300 \
  --run-tag _baseline

Keep the resulting report.json, stats.json, normalized library.msp, queries.mgf, labels.json, and run CSVs together. Schema-v2 report metadata records SHA-256 hashes for normalized inputs and selected query IDs, git revision and dirty state, Python and platform, run configuration, exported candidate-row counts, and wall time. --keep-data verifies schema, labels, and the input fingerprint; older or changed prepared data must be rebuilt.

To compare a new run, use a separate work directory and point --compare-to at the baseline report:

uv run python scripts/benchmark_real_corpus.py \
  --corpus /path/to/msp \
  --workdir /tmp/massflow-benchmark-current \
  --max-queries 300 \
  --run-tag _current \
  --compare-to /tmp/massflow-benchmark-baseline/report.json

The selection seed and exact normalized library/query inputs must match; the report comparison refuses different dataset fingerprints. If both MS1 and MS2 tolerances changed, describe the comparison as a joint configuration change. It cannot establish the causal effect of either tolerance separately. To attribute effects, hold other settings fixed and vary one tolerance at a time, or run a 2×2 MS1/MS2 tolerance design. The score and q-value sweeps evaluate only candidates retained and exported by the actual run gates; they cannot recover rows filtered out during annotation.

docs.title: FDR wording for benchmark reports
docs.text:
When the decoy null is empty at a gate, state:

The decoy null was empty at this gate; the reported q/FDR column is an uncalibrated rank bound and does not establish FDR control.

Do not describe the rank-bound column as a measured or calibrated FDR, claim that the run controls FDR at the selected threshold, or say that accepted candidates have a verified false-match rate at or below that threshold.

At the permissive fixture operating point with 400 target and 375 decoy competitions and 3,780 rows at q <= 0.05, state:

At the permissive gate, 400 target and 375 decoy competitions produced 3,780 rows with q <= 0.05 under the implemented ranking procedure; this is a fixture-specific rank-based result and is not evidence of calibrated FDR control.

Do not state that 3,780 compounds were identified, that 5% of those rows are known false, or that the observed counts prove empirical control of the true false-discovery rate. The q-value is query-level under the target-decoy contract; repeated candidate rows from one query are not independent discoveries. See Scoring Logic for assumptions and degraded-mode behavior.

docs.title: Saved-output accounting check
docs.text: Before quoting a metric, reconcile every selected query into exactly one of three states: preprocessing-rejected, searched with no accepted candidate, or searched with an accepted candidate. Then check that correct top-1 calls do not exceed calls, calls do not exceed searched queries, and searched queries plus preprocessing rejections equal selected queries. Recompute the metric numerators and denominators from the query partition and saved candidate rows; never derive accepted-call accuracy from classification metrics over invented labels for wrong predictions.

docs.title: Retrieval-funnel diagnostics
docs.text:
Set similarity.collect_retrieval_diagnostics: true to write a versioned <results-stem>.diagnostics.json beside the normal YAML report. It contains input/library fingerprints when available, the effective configuration and run SHA/dirty state, bounded typed preprocessing-rejection samples, per-query terminal outcomes, and cumulative target/decoy pair counts at candidate prefilter, score, matched-fragment, polarity, RT, top-N, and confidence stages. The JSON sidecar is referenced from the YAML provenance report. Collection is opt-in and does not alter scores or result ordering.

The search.pair_stages counts are query-reference pairs, not query counts. Each stage is a cumulative survivor count; rejection_counts records disjoint differences between adjacent stages. Query terminal outcomes are mutually exclusive. unknown_or_unattributable is reported separately and must not be added as a second terminal state. no_precursor_candidates means no reference passed the configured cosine precursor window; it does not mean the query compound is absent from the library. An empty candidate list alone never establishes missing chemical coverage.

Benchmark-only truth_attribution is kept separate from production annotations. It replays each labelled query against only its declared truth records using the same effective processing and search gates, then compares that reachability with the full-library ranking. It can distinguish records not retained in the prepared store, precursor/prefilter loss, score or fragment threshold loss, polarity/RT loss, confidence filtering, and ranking among returned candidates. Any reason not directly observed is recorded as unknown; truth labels are not passed into the annotation pipeline.

The real-corpus harness currently normalizes every query with IONMODE=Positive and CHARGE=1 and does not emit source precursor-type metadata as an adduct. Its source metadata audit records the original polarity/adduct values separately and warns that these normalized cross-instrument runs do not test the original source polarity/adduct gates. Do not interpret them as evidence that LTQ/QTOF polarity metadata were compatible.

When a search configuration allows zero-score/zero-match rows (min_score <= 0 and min_matched_peaks == 0), the legacy sparse-cosine output can contain a zero-valued row for a pair that was not submitted to scoring. The diagnostic marks such stage arithmetic with stage_accounting_consistent: false and unattributable_pairs; it does not invent a score- or prefilter-rejection cause. This edge behavior is preserved for compatibility, and is not exercised by the cross-instrument benchmark's 0.4 score / 3 matched-peak gates.

Each pair-stage class also includes score_distribution, a fixed 0.1-wide histogram of finite scores submitted to scoring and before the configured score cutoff. The final bin includes score 1.0; below-range, above-range, and non-finite values are counted separately. Histogram counts plus those three exception counts equal scored_pairs; prefilter-excluded pairs are not included in the distribution. This bounded summary is sufficient to distinguish “scored but below threshold” from “never reached scoring” without retaining a full query-reference score matrix.

The benchmark report adds retrieval_diagnostics_by_source: per-instrument selected/preprocessing-rejected/searched/no-call counts, target/decoy pair funnel totals, score histograms, confidence states, and terminal outcomes. Its preprocessing-rejected denominator is derived from benchmark peak-count labels and checked against the production query-ID funnel; unobserved non-preprocessing records are kept as unknown rather than silently classified.

truth_precursor_eligibility_audit compares the serialized query precursor masses to the serialized precursor masses of the benchmark-labelled truth records at the reported MS1 windows. It reports pair- and query-level window coverage with selected and searched denominators, and labels the quantile method. This post-hoc calculation characterizes a configured eligibility gate; it does not widen that gate, change a candidate result, or establish that an MS/MS match would pass fragment or score thresholds.

docs.title: Confidence estimates and evidence states
docs.text: MassFlow's similarity score and its statistical estimate are different quantities. A cosine or modified-cosine score measures spectral agreement under a particular preprocessing, peak-assignment and tolerance policy. It is not an identification probability. A numerical q estimate does not establish experimentally demonstrated FDR control or confirmed chemical identity.

docs.title: Machine-readable contract
docs.text:
Field/state Meaning score, matched_peaks Numerical spectral matching outputs, unchanged by this confidence reporting layer confidence_state=estimated_uncalibrated At least one qualifying target and decoy query maximum permits the implemented calculation; empirical calibration is pending confidence_state=unavailable No target observations or no surviving decoy observations; no statistical estimate is available confidence_state=invalid An unattributable candidate, nonfinite/nonnumeric score or malformed numerical input invalidates the family; the workflow fails explicitly confidence_q_value Nullable numerical estimate for a query with a target when the family is estimated_uncalibrated; null otherwise confidence_method pooled_query_maxima_plus_one_v1 confidence_scope query_best_target; every candidate of that query inherits the query assessment, not candidate-specific confidence confidence_limitations JSON array in tabular exports; machine-readable reasons and unvalidated assumptions Sidecar confidence Versioned method, formula, discovery unit, family, counts, tie policy, limitations and empirical_calibration: pending

There is no calibrated state produced by this implementation. A nonempty null is necessary for this numerical estimate and is insufficient to establish calibration. One observed decoy is explicitly reported as single_decoy_observation; no magic sample size or library size converts an estimate into a validated one. Missing estimates serialize as null/empty cells, never as zero. A supplied or computed zero must never be interpreted as certainty.

docs.title: Compatibility and filtering
docs.text:
The historical q_value/p_value columns and existing fdr_threshold filtering retain their API names. A proven partial-tie undercount is corrected, so values and threshold selection can change for tied target/decoy scores. On an empty decoy null, historical q is 1/N_target and p is 1: these are arithmetic diagnostics, not an estimated false discovery rate or a conservative error bound. Use confidence_state and confidence_q_value to determine estimate availability. Changing query-file partitioning changes N and can change the historical filter. Do not use the legacy column without checking the explicit state.

Newly assessed candidate rows are labelled Uncalibrated even when a decoy survived. No-hit queries remain Unknown with unavailable confidence. Existing direct export callers without assessments retain legacy score-status behavior for compatibility; those labels cannot be interpreted as a validated confidence level.

docs.title: Exact method
docs.text:
For each query, retain the maximum target and maximum decoy score after configured candidate eligibility, score and matched-peak gates. Pool these two sets; this is not one target-or-decoy winner per query. At score threshold t:

T(t) = number of finite best target scores >= t
D(t) = number of finite best decoy scores >= t
FDR_hat(t) = min(1, (1 + D(t))/T(t))      [1 when T(t)=0]
q(s) = min_{t<=s} FDR_hat(t)
p(s) = (1 + number of best decoy scores >= s)/(1 + N_decoy)

The arrays are ranked by descending score, decoys first on ties, followed by a reverse cumulative minimum over complete equal-score blocks. Partial tie ranks are never treated as attainable thresholds. Equal best target scores share q. The p column is a diagnostic and is not used for FDR thresholding. The calculation family is one input file. Arrays must be one-dimensional, real and finite; invalid values cannot silently disappear. Candidate scoring remains independent of this validation.

docs.title: Assumptions and pending calibration
docs.text:
Incorrect target matches and generated decoys must be comparable after every gate. Precursor windows, adduct/polarity restrictions, shifted-fragment candidates, library composition, repeated spectra, query dependence and instrument/CE changes can alter those populations. Preserving entropy or precursor m/z does not prove exchangeability; uniform fragment jitter can also leave some peaks within scoring tolerance. Scores from routed engines are not automatically on comparable scales.

Synthetic arithmetic tests verify formulas, ties, monotonicity and invalid-input behavior. They do not verify chemical error rates. Existing saved cross-instrument MoNA results include empty-decoy regimes; they cannot establish FDR calibration. Independent known-truth present/absent experiments, group-level uncertainty and frozen query/file/library definitions are required. Calibration remains pending. See Scheubert et al., 10.1038/s41467-017-01318-5, for a distinct published decoy-method evaluation; it does not validate MassFlow's generator. Li et al., 10.1038/s41592-021-01331-z, addresses entropy similarity and discusses limitations of computational decoys.

docs.title: YAML Configuration
docs.text:
MassFlow operates on a Config-First principle. Instead of writing custom Python scripts for every analysis, all operational parameters—from file paths to noise thresholds—are defined in a single YAML file.

This ensures your MS/MS annotation workflows are completely reproducible.

docs.title: Generating a Template
docs.text:
The easiest way to start is by letting the CLI generate a canonical configuration file for you:

uv run massflow init --output massflow_config.yaml

This creates a massflow_config.yaml file with sensible defaults for a classical similarity search.

docs.title: The Configuration Schema
docs.text: The YAML configuration is broken down into modular sections. Under the hood, MassFlow uses Pydantic to strictly validate these fields before any processing begins.

docs.title: project
docs.text:
Defines high-level run metadata.

project:
  name: "Standard_Annotation_Project"
  output_directory: "results/standard_analysis"
* name: A descriptive string for your run. * output_directory: The folder where the resulting CSVs and YAML sidecar reports will be saved.

docs.title: input
docs.text:
Defines where MassFlow should look for your experimental data and your reference library.

input:
  input_path: "data/experiments/experiment.mzML"
  # input_path: "data/experiments/" # Use this to process a whole folder
  library_path: "data/libraries/library.msp"
  format: "mzml"
  storage_backend: "sqlite"
* input_path: The experimental file or directory to process. A directory is recursively scanned for supported spectral files. * library_path: The file path to your reference library (e.g., an .msp file or a MassFlow .db SQLite file). * format: (Optional) An explicit format hint. If omitted, MassFlow infers the format from the file extension. * storage_backend: (Optional) How the reference library is stored: "sqlite" (default, BLOB peak arrays), "zarr" (pure Zarr), or "hybrid" (SQLite metadata + chunked Zarr peak arrays). The setting has one unambiguous meaning everywhere: it selects the backend of the library store built for the run — massflow db build, the annotation pipeline (prepare_library), and the streaming server all honor it. Pre-existing store inputs (.db/.sqlite/.zarr) are opened directly in their own backend. The annotation layer consumes every backend through the single SpectralStore interface, so SQLite, Zarr, and hybrid libraries produce identical results (verified by tests/test_storage_contract.py).

docs.title: processing
docs.text:
Controls how spectra are cleaned and filtered before they are scored. See the Processing & Filtering guide for deep dives into these toggles.

processing:
  clean_metadata: true
  filter_by_intensity: true
  noise_threshold: 1000.0
  min_intensity: 0.0
  filter_min_peaks: true
  min_peaks: 5

docs.title: similarity
docs.text:
Defines the scoring algorithm and the strict chemical constraints required for a valid match. See the Classical Similarity guide.

similarity:
  algorithm: "cosine"
  ms1_tolerance: 0.02
  ms2_tolerance: 0.02
  min_score: 0.6
  min_matched_peaks: 3
  fdr_threshold: 0.05
* algorithm: The core engine. Stable choices are "cosine" and "modified_cosine"; "spec2vec" and "ms2deepscore" require the ml extra; "consensus" and "cascade" combine multiple engines (see the Similarity API). * ms1_tolerance: Precursor mass tolerance (in Da). * resolution_ppm: Optional: Precursor mass resolution (in ppm). Overrides ms1_tolerance if set. * ms2_tolerance: Fragment mass tolerance (typically in Da). * min_score: The absolute minimum score required to keep a hit. * min_matched_peaks: Minimum number of matched fragment peaks. * fdr_threshold: Legacy cutoff for numerical query-level target/decoy estimates. Those estimates are uncalibrated; the cutoff is not a controlled FDR guarantee.

Advanced similarity keys include analog_search, the consensus_* / cascade_* engine settings, the hnsw_* approximate-candidate retrieval knobs (requires the hnsw extra), and ml_endpoints for routing Spec2Vec/MS2DeepScore scoring to a remote REST/gRPC service with automatic fallback to the classical engines.

docs.title: export
docs.text:
Defines the output format.

export:
  format: "csv"
* format: "csv" (default, stable) or "mztab" (experimental, non-conformant mzTab-shaped table). Only CSV is in the stable v0.1 export contract. mztab does not claim mzTab-M standards conformance. (Other formats such as fbmn are documented in places but not implemented; see the Results guide and docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md.)

docs.title: workflow
docs.text: Reserved for future pipeline stages (peak picking, retention-time alignment, networking). It currently has no active fields — all orchestration is handled directly by the workflow module, and the stable annotation path runs on the processing + similarity sections alone.

docs.title: Configuration Validation
docs.text: MassFlow validates the entire configuration before any expensive processing begins, and rejects invalid configuration with human-readable errors that include the YAML line number.

docs.title: Unknown keys are errors, never silent
docs.text:
Configuration models are strict: any key that is not part of the schema fails validation immediately. A misspelled key such as

similarity:
  ms2_tolerence: 0.02   # typo

produces:

Configuration validation failed:
Line 3, Key 'similarity -> ms2_tolerence': Unknown configuration key
'ms2_tolerence' under 'similarity'. Did you mean 'ms2_tolerance'?

No typo is silently ignored and no default is silently substituted.

docs.title: Invalid combinations fail at validation time
docs.text:
• hnsw_enabled: true requires algorithm: "cascade" (HNSW candidate retrieval only exists inside the cascade engine).
  • reduce_to_top_n_peaks: true requires a positive n_max (otherwise the toggle would silently do nothing).
  • cascade_stages must be a non-empty list of leaf engines (cosine, modified_cosine, spec2vec, ms2deepscore).
  • consensus_weights keys must be leaf engines with positive weights.
  • fdr_threshold and min_score must lie in [0, 1].
  • ms2_tolerance / ms1_tolerance / rt_tolerance must be non-negative.

docs.title: Relative paths resolve against the config file
docs.text:
All relative paths (project.output_directory, input.input_path, input.library_path) are resolved relative to the YAML file's directory, not the caller's current working directory. The same configuration therefore behaves identically regardless of where the massflow command is invoked from.

Legacy CWD-relative resolution can be restored explicitly with the compatibility environment variable:

MASSFLOW_COMPAT_CWD_PATHS=1 massflow annotate --config massflow_config.yaml

Programmatically constructed configurations (no YAML file) keep their paths untouched; relative paths then resolve against the process working directory at use time.

docs.title: Normalized configuration in provenance
docs.text:
Every run writes the normalized configuration representation into provenance:

  • a run-level file run_provenance.json (counter-suffixed when a run shares an output directory) in the project output directory, written before any expensive processing begins;
  • a config: section in every per-file *.report.yaml sidecar.

The representation contains the schema version, the absolute source config path, the full effective configuration (all paths resolved), and a config_digest_sha256 over the canonical JSON, so any result can be verified to have been produced by exactly the configuration it claims.

docs.title: Retention-time units and migration
docs.text:
Spectrum retention_time is always seconds. The tolerance has an explicit unit; these settings accept a difference of at most 12 seconds (inclusive):

similarity:
  rt_tolerance: 0.2
  rt_tolerance_unit: minutes

rt_tolerance_unit: seconds with rt_tolerance: 12 is equivalent. A missing tolerance disables the gate. Both values must have an interpretable retention time for the gate to apply; missing, invalid, or conflicting times remain missing.

Existing configurations that set rt_tolerance without a unit retain the actual legacy seconds behavior and log a migration warning. Earlier documentation incorrectly called those values minutes. Set the unit explicitly after reviewing the intended window; no automatic factor-of-60 change is made to saved settings. The per-file report records the original tolerance and its effective seconds value.

Unit-aware normalization changes prepared-library metadata. MassFlow-managed raw file caches rebuild once. Existing explicit SQLite/Zarr libraries are not rewritten; rebuild legacy libraries from the original files into new destinations before relying on retention-time filtering. A unit lost before storage cannot be recovered from its plain numeric value. Retention-time comparison also requires comparable chromatographic methods; matching numeric units does not establish method transfer.

The combined stabilization and retention-time implementation uses processing semantics revision 5. It includes the precursor, fragment-window, charge/adduct, and record-identity corrections from revision 4 plus canonical seconds and source-unit evidence. Managed caches from either predecessor rebuild once; the next unchanged run reuses the replacement. Explicit persistent stores retain the manual-rebuild requirement above.

docs.title: MassFlow Data Requirements & Metadata Contract
docs.text: MassFlow employs a rigid Pydantic validation layer to ensure scientific accuracy during spectral annotation. This document outlines the exact metadata requirements for user-provided spectral files (e.g., .msp, .mgf) and explains how MassFlow processes, repairs, and validates these fields.

docs.title: Supported File Formats
docs.text:
MassFlow requires open, vendor-neutral data formats for both query spectra and reference libraries:

  • Supported: .mzML, .mzXML, .mgf, .msp
  • Unsupported: Proprietary vendor formats (.raw, .d, .wiff, .lcd, .t2d). These must be converted to an open format (like .mzML) using tools like ProteoWizard MSConvert prior to ingestion.

docs.title: Required Metadata Fields
docs.text:
To successfully pass the SpectrumMetadata and MolecularStructure validation contracts, the following fields are strictly required for every spectrum:

Field Description Type / Format precursor_mz The measured m/z of the precursor ion. Float (e.g., 195.088) charge The integer charge state of the ion. Integer (e.g., 1, 2, -1). Note: If missing, MassFlow will attempt to impute it. mz_array Array of fragment m/z values. List of floats. Must be monotonically increasing. intensity_array Array of fragment intensities. List of floats. Must match the length of mz_array.

docs.title: Charge Imputation
docs.text: If the charge is missing, the matchms filtering sequence (make_charge_int) will attempt to derive it. If the charge cannot be determined, the strict 5 ppm mass comparison is skipped for that spectrum (an unknown charge disables the check per the SpectrumMetadata contract); the spectrum remains analyzable through classical cosine scoring.

docs.title: Optional & Conditionally Required Metadata
docs.text: While not strictly required for basic ingestion, the following fields unlock advanced validation, structural verification, and Machine Learning capabilities.

docs.title: 1. adduct and ionmode
docs.text:
MassFlow rigorously validates the relationship between precursor_mz, charge, exact mass, and the ionization adduct.

  • adduct: Must be an ionization adduct whose chemistry MassFlow recognises. The registry covers the common LC-MS adducts ([M+H]+, [M-H]-, [M+Na]+, [M+NH4]+, [M+K]+, [M+Cl]-, [M+HCOO]-, [M+CH3COO]-, multiply-charged and solvent/water-loss variants — see docs/user-guide/validation.md for the full table and offsets).
    • Notation is canonicalised, so library spellings are accepted: M+H, [M+H]1+, [M+H]+1, [m+h]+, interior whitespace, and unbalanced brackets all resolve to [M+H]+; alias chemistry such as M+FA-H / M+HCOOH-H (formate), M+OAc / M+Ac-H (acetate), M+ACN+H, and M-H2O+H resolves too. The stored value is rewritten to the canonical spelling.
    • Prose descriptions (e.g. "sodium adduct") and adducts outside the registry cannot be resolved, so strict validation fails for those spectra; normalisation never guesses, and a resolved adduct must still clear the 5 ppm tolerance.
  • ionmode: Must be exactly "positive", "negative", or "neutral".

Imputation Behavior: * If adduct is missing but ionmode is provided, MassFlow defaults to [M+H]+ for positive mode and [M-H]- for negative mode. * The matchms filter derive_adduct_from_name will attempt to parse the adduct from the compound name if possible.

docs.title: 2. Structural Identifiers (smiles, inchi, inchikey)
docs.text: Structural identifiers are optional, but their presence fundamentally alters how MassFlow validates the spectrum.

docs.title: The 5 ppm Strict Mass Validation
docs.text:
If a smiles, inchi, or formula is provided, MassFlow triggers rigorous structural validation:

  1. Parsing: The structure is parsed using RDKit (when a formula is not already declared). If the SMILES/InChI is syntactically invalid and the matchms repair filters could not fix it, the spectrum is flagged as physically invalid.
  2. Theoretical Calculation: The theoretical monoisotopic exact mass of the molecule is calculated (pyteomics from the declared formula; RDKit + pyteomics from the structure otherwise).
  3. Conflict Checking: If your library provides an exact_mass field alongside the structure, MassFlow checks for conflicts. If the provided mass deviates from the calculated mass by > 5.0 ppm, the spectrum is flagged as physically invalid, assuming a corrupted library entry.
  4. Adduct Validation: If the exact mass is known and the adduct is standard, MassFlow calculates the theoretical m/z of the precursor ion. If the experimental precursor_mz deviates from this theoretical m/z by > 5.0 ppm, the spectrum is flagged as physically invalid.

Enforcement in the pipeline — "physically invalid" spectra are rejected by the processing gate in the classical annotate/db build paths (see docs/user-guide/validation.md): query spectra are rejected and counted per file (an all-rejected file is an explicit failure), raw reference-library entries abort the annotate run, and db build quarantines them. Spectra without structural claims are exempt from the gate.

docs.title: Isotopic Envelope Generation
docs.text: When a valid smiles is present, MassFlow automatically calculates a theoretical MS1 isotopic envelope (M, M+1, M+2, etc., normalized to the base peak). This theoretical envelope acts as a ground-truth signature, used by advanced ML routing and the ConsensusEngine to break ties between competing MS2 fragmentation annotations. If smiles is missing, this advanced credibility check cannot be performed.

docs.title: 3. General Metadata
docs.text: Field Description Type / Format retention_time Chromatographic retention time. Float (seconds). Known source units are converted; missing or ambiguous values stay missing. Original time evidence is retained in retention_time_source. exact_mass Provided monoisotopic mass. Float. Will be auto-calculated if SMILES is present. formula Chemical formula. String (e.g., C8H10N4O2). Will be auto-calculated if SMILES is present.

docs.title: Metadata Harmonization Pipeline
docs.text:
During ingestion, MassFlow runs a series of matchms filters (configurable via ProcessingConfig) designed to repair common library issues before strict Pydantic validation:

  1. default_filters: Normalizes common keys (e.g., mz -> precursor_mz).
  2. repair_inchi_inchikey_smiles: Attempts to fix broken formatting in structural identifiers.
  3. harmonize_undefined_*: Cleans up undefined strings (e.g., "N/A", "null") in structural fields.
  4. derive_formula_from_name & derive_adduct_from_name: Attempts to extract missing data from the compound_name string.

If these filters cannot repair a non-standard entry, and it lacks the critical fields (or violates the 5 ppm physics check when structural identifiers are present), the spectrum is rejected by the strict processing gate: counted per query file (see the failure model), fatal for raw reference libraries during annotate, and quarantined during db build.

docs.title: SQLite Library Management
docs.text:
MassFlow v0.1 natively supports persistent, reusable local spectral libraries backed by SQLite.

If you run massflow annotate against large, raw text-based formats (like .msp or .mgf), MassFlow must parse those massive files into Python objects every single time you launch the CLI.

By building a SQLite database, you preprocess the spectra, serialize their mass arrays into optimized binary blobs, and dramatically speed up subsequent annotation runs while reducing memory overhead.

docs.title: Why Use SQLite Databases?
docs.text:
1. Speed: SQLite blobs bypass the slow string-parsing required for MGF/MSP files.
  2. Memory: SQLite allows MassFlow to lazily stream spectra into the scoring engine instead of materializing an entire 10GB .msp into RAM at once.
  3. Organization: You can merge multiple project-specific libraries together and query them by category.
  4. Triage Scanning (Core Feature): During database construction, MassFlow automatically scans spectra for key chemical features (like the Tyrosine immonium ion at 136.076 Da) and flags them in a triage_flags bitmask. This allows the workflow to intelligently route structurally significant spectra to advanced machine learning engines downstream without having to re-parse the raw peak arrays.

docs.title: The Database Workflow
docs.text: The typical pattern for a local bioinformatics lab is to maintain curated, in-house databases.

docs.title: 1. Build a Database
docs.text:
Convert a raw open-format library (like .msp) into a MassFlow SQLite .db file.

This command streams the input file through the matchms filters defined in your configuration file, ensuring the database only stores clean, processed spectra.

uv run massflow db build \
    --input data/libraries/example_library.msp \
    --output results/user_library.db \
    --config massflow_config.yaml \
    --category personal
  • --input: The raw file to ingest.
  • --output: The destination .db file.
  • --config: The YAML config dictating how the spectra should be cleaned before storage.
  • --category: An optional tag (e.g., personal, standards, gnps) to organize the spectra internally.

If the input file is malformed or yields zero valid spectra after processing, the build will explicitly fail and alert you.

docs.title: 2. Inspect a Database
docs.text:
Quickly verify the contents and health of a built database without loading the full spectrum objects.

uv run massflow db inspect results/user_library.db

Every SQLite-backed database records its own build lineage at creation time: the input file(s) used (with content SHA-256), the effective config hash (config_digest_sha256), the processing parameters (including decoy-generation settings), the similarity / target-decoy configuration, the MassFlow version, and an exact UTC build timestamp. db inspect acts as the query surface for that history:

Example Output: 

DATABASE INSPECTION: results/user_library.db
Total Spectra: 15420
Precursor m/z Range: 50.0211 to 1400.9822

Categories:
  - personal: 15420 spectra

Store Metadata
  Backend          sqlite
  Schema Version   1
  Created At (UTC) 2026-09-06T10:00:00+00:00

Library Build History
  #  Built At (UTC)            Category  Spectra  Backend  Source                  Config Digest (sha256)
  1  2026-09-06T10:00:00+00:00 personal  15420    sqlite   data/libraries/lib.msp  5c7725e3d5e77f5b…

Processing Parameters
  min_peaks                   5
  decoy_min_relative_intensity 0.01
  decoy_mz_shift_da           1.0
  ...

Target-Decoy Configuration
  algorithm    cosine
  fdr_threshold 0.05
  ...

  • db build records one history row per build; rebuilding over changed input or configuration appends a new row, so the table reads as a version history.
  • db merge records the exact input databases and per-input spectrum counts (details.merged_sources).
  • Databases created before the provenance schema existed (user_version 0) are upgraded in place on their next MassFlow open; their spectra are untouched and their history starts at the first recorded build.
  • The same history is queryable programmatically via SpectralDatabase.get_library_builds() / get_latest_library_build() (all JSON fields parsed), and annotation result sidecars link back to these rows (see docs/user-guide/results.md).

docs.title: 3. Merge Databases
docs.text:
Combine multiple specialized databases into a single, master search library.

For example, you might maintain one database for authenticated in-house standards, and another for a downloaded GNPS library.

uv run massflow db merge \
    --inputs results/user_library.db results/standards.db \
    --output results/master_library.db

The merged database will retain all the processed spectra and metadata from the inputs.

docs.title: Using the Database in Annotation
docs.text:
Once your .db file is built, simply point your massflow_config.yaml to it instead of the raw .msp file:

massflow_config.yaml
input:
  file_path: "data/experiments/experiment.mzML"
  library_path: "results/master_library.db"
  format: "sqlite" # 'db' or 'sqlite'

Run massflow annotate as normal. The workflow will automatically detect the database and stream the binary spectra directly into the similarity engine.

docs.title: Processing & Filtering
docs.text:
The processing section of the MassFlow YAML configuration defines how raw spectral data is transformed before it is scored by a similarity engine. MassFlow acts as a declarative facade for the matchms library, applying a standardized two-stage pipeline: Metadata Processing and Peak Processing.

To ensure that query spectra and reference libraries are scored fairly, MassFlow strictly applies the exact same processing configuration to both sets of data.

docs.title: Metadata Processing
docs.text:
Metadata filters repair, harmonize, and standardize the annotations attached to a matchms.Spectrum object (e.g., InChIKeys, SMILES, charge state, adducts).

processing:
  clean_metadata: true
  add_retention_time: true
  repair_inchi_inchikey_smiles: true
  derive_adduct_from_name: true
  derive_formula_from_name: true
  clean_compound_name: true
  derive_ionmode: true
  make_charge_int: true
  • clean_metadata: Applies the default_filters from matchms to correct common metadata formatting issues (e.g., stripping whitespace, harmonizing keys).
  • add_retention_time: Extracts supported retention-time aliases into canonical seconds, preserving the original value and unit in retention_time_source. Explicit minute/second MGF fields, unit-bearing MSP values, and mzML/mzXML unit metadata are converted before storage. Disabling alias extraction still normalizes an existing canonical retention_time field. Unlabelled canonical/MSP numeric times follow the seconds contract; an unlabelled mzML scan time is left missing. Conflicting alias values are left missing. Metadata repairs operate on a clone of the source spectrum.
  • repair_inchi_inchikey_smiles: Attempts to fix broken or malformed structural identifiers. Crucial if you plan to use structure-aware experimental engines later.
  • derive_adduct_from_name & derive_formula_from_name: Parses the compound name string to extract adduct and chemical formula information if it is not explicitly provided in the metadata fields.
  • clean_compound_name: Standardizes compound names for consistent downstream reporting.
  • derive_ionmode: Infers the ionization mode (positive/negative) from other metadata fields if it is missing.
  • make_charge_int: Ensures the charge state is represented as a clean integer.

docs.title: Contextual Metadata Injection
docs.text:
You can also inject project-specific or instrument-specific metadata into all processed spectra by defining them in the configuration:

processing:
  instrument: "Orbitrap"
  mode: "positive"

docs.title: Peak Processing
docs.text:
Peak filters physically alter the mass-to-charge (m/z) and intensity arrays of the spectra. They are critical for removing noise, ensuring comparability between different instruments, and optimizing the speed of the similarity search.

These filters are applied sequentially in a specific order:

docs.title: 1. Intensity Filtering (Noise Removal)
docs.text:
Removes all peaks below a certain absolute intensity threshold.

processing:
  filter_by_intensity: true
  noise_threshold: 1000.0
* filter_by_intensity: Master toggle for noise removal. * noise_threshold: The absolute minimum intensity a peak must have to be retained. (If set to 0.0, MassFlow will fall back to checking the min_intensity field).

docs.title: 2. Minimum Peak Count
docs.text:
Drops the entire spectrum from the analysis if it contains too few peaks to be statistically meaningful.

processing:
  filter_min_peaks: true
  min_peaks: 5
* filter_min_peaks: Master toggle for peak count enforcement. * min_peaks: The minimum number of peaks a spectrum must contain after noise filtering to survive. If a spectrum has fewer peaks than this, it is silently dropped.

docs.title: 3. M/Z Range Truncation
docs.text:
Discards peaks that fall outside a biologically or chemically relevant mass window.

processing:
  filter_by_mz: true
  mz_min: 0.0
  mz_max: 1000.0
* filter_by_mz: Master toggle for fragment-peak m/z truncation. It does not filter the precursor m/z or decide precursor candidacy. * mz_min & mz_max: The allowed m/z window. Peaks outside this range are deleted. (Note: mz_max must be strictly greater than mz_min).

docs.title: 4. Top-N Peak Reduction
docs.text:
A highly aggressive filter that retains only the most intense peaks in the spectrum, discarding the rest. This can drastically speed up classical similarity scoring on noisy data.

processing:
  reduce_to_top_n_peaks: true
  n_max: 100
* reduce_to_top_n_peaks: Master toggle for Top-N reduction. * n_max: The maximum number of peaks to retain.

docs.title: 5. Intensity Normalization
docs.text:
Scales the intensity array of the spectrum so the maximum peak has an intensity of 1.0.

processing:
  normalize_intensity: true
* normalize_intensity: Required for almost all classical similarity engines (like cosine) to function correctly, as they expect intensities to be on a consistent scale.

docs.title: Filter order and empty spectra
docs.text:
The batch path may reject an input already below the enabled minimum peak count. Metadata repair and the strict 5 ppm physical-integrity gate then run before peak processing. Intensity filtering precedes minimum-count filtering; fragment truncation, top-N reduction and normalization follow in that order. The minimum count is not reapplied after truncation. An empty spectrum created by truncation can therefore survive processing; this correction preserves that existing policy rather than introducing a new empty-spectrum filter.

For example, a spectrum with precursor m/z 800 and fragments at 49, 50, 100, 500 and 501 survives a 50–500 fragment window with peaks 50, 100 and 500. Precursor candidacy is a separate scoring setting. The physical-integrity gate still rejects a declared formula/adduct whose precursor exceeds the fixed 5 ppm tolerance.

docs.title: Processing fingerprints and cache migration
docs.text:
MassFlow.library.processing_fingerprint() hashes canonical JSON containing processing_semantics_revision and the JSON processing configuration, with sorted keys and compact separators. The explicit revision changes when an algorithm change alters processing even if the configuration stays identical; it is independent of package versions and Git SHAs. It is also recorded in library-build provenance.

The integrated candidate uses processing-semantics revision 4. It covers missing-precursor normalization, fragment-only m/z windows, charge/adduct consistency and per-acquisition source identity. Earlier config-only and standalone revisions invalidate managed SQLite, Zarr and hybrid caches built from raw files. Staged replacement rebuilds without mixing old/new rows, then reuses a compatible rebuilt cache.

Explicit .db, .sqlite and .zarr input libraries are opened directly and are not rebuilt or rewritten automatically. Previously generated persistent stores may retain rows discarded or altered under old processing. Rebuild from raw source into a new destination when corrected processing is required; appending to an existing store does not remove its old rows.

Do not reuse the standalone revision numbers described in individual PR evidence reports; the combined revision is the cache contract for this candidate.

docs.title: Result Export & Confidence States
docs.text:
MassFlow writes per-file candidate-search results in CSV with YAML provenance reports. CSV is the stable supported export. The mztab option writes an experimental, non-conformant mzTab-shaped table (see below). Scores and confidence states are evidence for review, not confirmed identities or calibrated error bounds.

GNPS FBMN export is not shipped

The fbmn export format and consensus_spectra.mgf are documented in places but not implemented in this release (export.format accepts only csv and mztab). Do not rely on them. See docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md for the authoritative capability list.

docs.title: Output Structure
docs.text: If you process a single experimental file (e.g., experiment.mzML), MassFlow will generate standard output files in your configured project.output_directory depending on your export.format:

docs.title: CSV Export (csv)
docs.text: The simplest and most common format. 1. experiment_results.csv: The main tabular annotation report. 2. experiment_results.report.yaml: The provenance sidecar containing the runtime context.

docs.title: Experimental mzTab-shaped Export (mztab)
docs.text: This option is not mzTab-M and is not standards-conformant. It is retained only for backward-compatible diagnostic interchange. It writes MassFlow-specific MTD/SMH/SML sections, omits the mandatory mzTab-M controlled vocabulary and table structure, and does not use the required null missing-value encoding. The file deliberately omits mzTab-version, because emitting it would assert conformance. Use CSV for the supported release export. 1. experiment_results.mztab: Contains MassFlow experimental metadata (MTD) and MassFlow-specific SMH/SML rows in an experimental schema. 2. experiment_results.report.yaml: The provenance sidecar.

docs.title: GNPS FBMN Export (fbmn) — not shipped
docs.text: Not implemented in this release. export.format accepts only csv and mztab; there is no consensus_spectra.mgf output. (Planned/aspirational only — see docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md §2.4.)

docs.title: The Result Table
docs.text:
The table contains retained candidate matches, including score, matched_peaks, and a legacy Annotation_Status category. A candidate score is not an identification probability.

Each candidate row also contains reference_metadata, a compact JSON object that preserves the source record ID, original accession/identifier, source path and SHA-256/ordinal locator when available, plus the acquisition metadata carried by the library record (for example collision energy, instrument, adduct and charge). This acquisition identity is distinct from chemical identity such as InChIKey.

Annotation_Status values:

Status Meaning Matched Legacy score category (score ≥ 0.9); never a confirmed identity. Assessed unvalidated rows use Uncalibrated. Putative Legacy score category (score < 0.9); not a validated confidence level. Uncalibrated The query confidence state is estimated_uncalibrated, unavailable, or invalid. Its legacy q_value may remain for compatibility, but neither a non-empty nor empty decoy null establishes FDR control. See confidence semantics. Unknown No hit for this query (base row).

Example: experiment_results.csv

query_id query_precursor_mz reference_id reference_name score matched_peaks Annotation_Status query_0 195.0 ref_12 Caffeine 0.98 5 Matched query_1 304.0 Unknown query_2 150.0 ref_8 Unknown_Metabolite 0.75 3 Putative

Unmatched Queries

The CSV includes matched and unmatched query spectra. A query with no retained candidate still has a row with reference-specific columns left blank. Historical q-value filtering may affect candidate retention, but it is not validated FDR control.

The retained query_retention_time column is in seconds. New query_retention_time_seconds and query_retention_time_unit columns make this explicit; query_retention_time_source contains JSON with the original input field, value, unit, and normalization status. A missing time is a blank numeric cell, never a fabricated zero. These additive fields are also emitted by the current mzTab-shaped exporter; they do not establish mzTab-M conformance (see issue #123).

docs.title: The Provenance Sidecar Report
docs.text:
The sidecar report (.report.yaml) acts as a hard link between your CSV results and the run conditions that produced it. It captures:

  • When the analysis was run (report_created_at).
  • Which query file and library file were used (query_file, library_path).
  • The path to the original massflow_config.yaml.
  • The exact parsed configurations (processing, similarity, workflow) that were applied.
  • The normalized configuration representation (config) with its SHA-256 digest.
  • The number of query spectra processed and the number of retained results.
  • A library lineage block that links the results to the exact database that was searched (see below).

docs.title: Library lineage (library)
docs.text:
When the reference library is a MassFlow database (built by massflow db build or prepared from a raw file during annotate), the sidecar records where the results came from and which build produced that database:

library:
  configured_library_path: results/master_library.db   # what the config pointed at
  store:
    path: results/master_library.db                    # the store actually searched
    kind: store
    storage_backend: sqlite
    spectrum_count: 15420
    schema_version: 1
    created_at: 2026-09-06T10:00:00+00:00
  build:                                               # the library_builds row
    id: 3
    built_at: 2026-09-06T10:00:00+00:00
    source_path: data/libraries/example_library.msp    # input file used to build it
    category: personal
    spectrum_count: 15420
    config_digest_sha256: 5c7725e3…                     # config hash recorded at build
    processing_fingerprint: 9f4a…
    massflow_version: 0.1.0

Comparing the sidecar's own config.config_digest_sha256 (this run) with library.build.config_digest_sha256 (the database build) tells you at a glance whether the database was built with the exact configuration this run used. When the store has no recorded history (e.g. a pre-provenance database), build is null rather than guessed. The same lineage is queryable per database with massflow db inspect.

This ensures you can always reproduce how a specific CSV was generated months later, meeting the standards of scientific reproducibility.

docs.title: Run-Level Provenance (run_provenance.json)
docs.text:
Every annotation run writes a first-class run-provenance record into the output directory (run_provenance.json, counter-suffixed when runs share an output directory). It is written before any per-file processing begins and finalized with the completion summary afterwards. The record contains:

Field Meaning massflow_version The MassFlow package version git_sha / git_dirty The exact checkout commit (and whether it was dirty) python_version / python_implementation / platform The interpreter and OS dependencies Resolved versions of every direct dependency lockfile_digest_sha256 SHA-256 of the committed uv.lock effective_config / config_digest_sha256 The normalized configuration and its digest engine / processing The similarity-engine and processing configuration backend The storage backend (sqlite / zarr / hybrid) decoy_seed / decoy_config The decoy-generation seed and parameters input_file_hashes SHA-256 of every experimental input file reference_library_sha256 / reference_library_kind The reference-library digest run_started_at / completed_at Explicitly time-varying timestamps (UTC ISO-8601) results Completion summary: per-status counts, aggregated warnings, degraded-mode flags, failed files

Provenance is deterministic: two runs from the same checkout and lockfile over the same inputs produce identical records except for the explicitly time-varying fields (run_started_at, completed_at).

docs.title: Per-File Execution Status (Failure Model)
docs.text:
Every experimental input file produces exactly one structured execution outcome (MassFlow.workflow.FileExecutionResult) with the following contract:

Field Meaning status success | degraded | failed input_path The experimental input file spectra_loaded Spectra that passed I/O validation and entered processing spectra_rejected Spectra dropped by validation or processing (reported explicitly, never silently) hits_produced Annotation hits exported for the file output_path Written results file (None for failed files) warnings Non-fatal caveats (e.g. small-library FDR) fatal_errors Non-empty iff the file failed degraded_mode_flags Machine-readable degradation markers (engine_fallback:<algo>, consensus_*, cascade_*, routing_*, decoy_null_empty, fdr_uncalibrated)

The status is recorded in the provenance sidecar, so a degraded or partially failed run is never indistinguishable from a clean one:

  • success — the file was fully processed with the configured pipeline.
  • degraded — results were produced, but part of the configured pipeline fell back (engine fallback, uncalibrated FDR); the flags explain what changed.
  • failed — the file's data were not processed. No results CSV is written for a failed file (an empty CSV would be mistaken for a successful annotation); instead an explicit <stem>_failed.report.yaml records the fatal errors.

Batch runs continue across files: one bad file does not stop the others, but the CLI exits nonzero when any file failed, and the per-file summary printed by massflow annotate accounts for every input. Unsupported vendor formats (.raw, .d, .wiff, ...) are never silently ignored: a vendor raw library or a direct single-file/.d query input aborts at pre-flight (before any store is built, with the conversion hint), while vendor files inside a scanned input directory are announced at run start and reported as explicit per-file failures with a conversion hint — they never silently disappear from a batch. See the annotation guide (Pre-flight validation) for the full contract.

docs.title: False Discovery Rate (FDR)
docs.text:
MassFlow calculates a numerical query-maxima estimate, not empirically demonstrated FDR control. See confidence semantics for the exact formula, explicit states, nullable estimate, family, inherited-row limitations and historical column/filter compatibility. Both populated and empty nulls remain scientifically uncalibrated; no nominal q threshold proves an observed error rate.

Increasing fdr_threshold only changes selection; it does not cure a sparse or unrepresentative decoy null. Inspect counts, methodology and limitations before interpreting any confidence column.

docs.title: Numerical confidence diagnostics
docs.text:
The implemented target/decoy procedure reports a query-level numerical estimate; its empirical calibration is pending. Decoys are synthetic altered spectra intended to provide a null comparison, but exchangeability with incorrect chemical matches has not been established.

  1. Decoys are generated from reference records and searched using the configured engine and candidate gates.
  2. Each query contributes at most its best target score and best surviving decoy score to the numerical competition.
  3. The implementation computes a monotone q-like estimate. estimated_uncalibrated means the calculation had target and decoy observations, not that its error rate has been validated. An empty decoy null is unavailable; the historical 1/N value is a rank diagnostic, not an error bound.
  4. Candidate rows inherit the query-level assessment; it is not candidate-specific.
  5. fdr_threshold remains a compatibility filter on the numerical value. It does not establish controlled FDR or confirm the retained structures.

The exported p_value remains a diagnostic only. See confidence semantics for the method, scope, explicit states, limitations and migration details.

docs.title: Decoy-count warnings
docs.text: The workflow may warn when a library is below its configured count heuristic. That warning is not a scientifically validated minimum size, and no decoy count threshold establishes FDR control. A sparse or unrepresentative decoy null should be reported with its confidence state and limitations; relaxing fdr_threshold changes which candidates are retained, not the validity of the estimate.

docs.title: Scientific-Validation Suite (Golden Tests)
docs.text: STATUS: authoritative. This is the "golden" known-answer test suite that detects changes in scientific meaning, not merely changes in code output. It is part of the default release test selection (marker: scientific) and runs in CI on every PR.

docs.title: What the suite asserts
docs.text:
The suite (tests/test_scientific_validation.py, fixtures in tests/scientific_validation/) locks down the scientific contract end-to-end:

Fixture category What is asserted Perfect spectral match cosine / modified-cosine score = 1.0, all peaks matched, Matched status Near match hand-computed cosine (3 of 4 fragments), matched-peak count, ranking Precursor-mass violation cosine MS1 gate (0.0 sentinel); modified cosine still matches in the exact frame Adduct violation [M-H]- vs [M+H]+ rejected by both engines Missing precursor (query) rejected by the I/O validation layer, counted in spectra_rejected, never silently analyzed Missing RT (query) bypasses the RT filter when it is configured RT filtering rt_tolerance removes exactly the RT-violating reference Modified-cosine behavior precursor-shift alignment (Watrous 2012), both-frame matching, |shift| <= tolerance → plain cosine Decoy generation determinism, entropy preservation (Li et al. 2021), precursor preservation, decoy ≠ source, decoy matches tagged is_decoy for TDC Confidence diagnostics per-query competition unit; q is traceable to the query-best target; empty-null 1/N is a rank diagnostic, not an error bound; p-value is diagnostic; historical fdr_threshold filtering is not calibrated FDR control Unmatched queries exported as Unknown with unavailable confidence; no identification claim Duplicate scores identical scores → identical q-values; equal-score references both exported Large peak counts 60-peak round trip, no peak loss, self-match counts all 60 Multiple engines cosine / modified_cosine / consensus / cascade known answers, including consensus's 0.5 dilution of MS1-gated pairs and cascade's stage semantics Storage equivalence SQLite and Zarr runs produce byte-identical result CSVs

docs.title: How expectations are derived
docs.text:
Every expected value is a known answer computed from the published formulas — cosine / modified cosine (Watrous et al., PNAS 2012), target-decoy competition (Elias & Gygi, Nat. Methods 2007), spectral-entropy decoys (Li et al., Nat. Methods 2021) — not captured from the implementation.

The fixture spectra are anchored to the well-documented caffeine [M+H]+ fragment series (m/z 195.0877 → 138.0662, loss of C2H3NO; → 110.0717, loss of CO; → 83.0608, loss of HCN; plus the characteristic 42.0344 fragment), as reported in public MS/MS libraries (MassBank / GNPS) and the caffeine metabolism literature. The remaining fixture spectra are explicitly synthetic with hand-computed expectations.

docs.title: The ground-truth manifest
docs.text:
tests/scientific_validation/ground_truth_results.json records, for every engine run (cosine, modified_cosine, consensus, cascade, cosine+RT, and the Zarr-backend equivalence run):

  • the exact configuration used;
  • per-query best target/decoy scores, q-values, and p-values;
  • every exported row (reference, score, matched peaks, q, p, annotation status, score breakdown);
  • the FDR summary (competition counts, true library size), warnings, degraded flags, and the SHA-256 of the result CSV (recorded for provenance).

The suite re-runs the pipeline and asserts the recorded rows are reproduced: column order, row counts, categorical fields, matched peak counts, and annotation statuses exactly; numeric fields (scores, q/p values) within a tight tolerance. The comparison is by value rather than CSV digest because scores are exported at full float64 precision, so identical results can serialize to different bytes across platforms.

docs.title: Regeneration policy
docs.text:
The fixtures change only when the scientific contract intentionally changes. Regenerate with:

uv run python tests/scientific_validation/generate_ground_truth.py

The generator re-verifies the current pipeline against its independent reference implementation of the published formulas before writing the manifest — if the pipeline diverges from the formulas, it fails loudly and the recorded ground truth is left untouched. A divergence that "passes" by updating the manifest is a deliberate scientific decision and must be reviewed as such.

docs.title: Relationship to the other suites
docs.text:
• tests/test_fdr_statistics.py — synthetic statistical tests of the FDR contract (degenerate inputs, ties, duplicates, execution-mode equivalence).
  • tests/test_similarity.py, tests/test_mathematical_proof.py — unit-level scoring correctness.
  • tests/test_library.py::TestGoldenDeterminism — row-for-row determinism of the worker-path outputs against the pre-refactor in-memory design (numeric fields within round-off tolerance; see docs/multiprocessing.md).
  • The suite here is the integration layer: real engines, real files, real store round-trips, real exports — the whole pipeline against known answers.

docs.title: Scoring and numerical FDR contract
docs.text:
Classical cosine and modified cosine use matchms greedy one-to-one peak assignment with configured fragment tolerance. Modified cosine also considers precursor-shifted matches and can retrieve different structures. Spectral agreement is not structural identity, and a score is not a probability.

The exact query-maxima formula, tie policy, empty-null behavior, explicit confidence states, machine-readable limitations and compatibility rules are documented in Confidence estimates and evidence states.

docs.title: Statistical scope
docs.text:
