MassFlow retains one best qualifying target score and one best qualifying decoy score per query, pools both sets, computes (1+D)/T, and applies a reverse minimum to obtain q-like numerical estimates. This is not a paired winner-take-all contest. Every exported candidate inherits the statistic determined by its query's best target, so additional rows are not independently calibrated discoveries.

Both candidate generation and configured gates condition the target/decoy samples. A surviving decoy permits a numerical estimate, not a claim that the null models incorrect chemical matches. Empty-null legacy values are rank diagnostics, not statistical bounds. Increasing a library or relaxing a threshold does not repair missing calibration evidence. Empirical p-values remain diagnostics only.

docs.title: Tests and interpretation
docs.text:
test_fdr.py, test_fdr_statistics.py, test_fdr_invariants.py and test_confidence_semantics.py verify arithmetic and reporting contracts, including independent complete-threshold enumeration, ties, sparse/empty/null cases and nonfinite input rejection. Golden integration fixtures verify repeatable numerical outputs. None is a chemical-identification calibration experiment.

The current procedure has no registered empirically calibrated domain. Confidence reporting therefore uses estimated_uncalibrated, unavailable or invalid. No code path promotes confidence to calibrated based on a score threshold, library size, nonempty null or passing software tests.

docs.title: Classical Similarity Scoring
docs.text:
The restricted candidate-retrieval scope centers on cosine and modified_cosine from matchms. These engines score spectra under configured peak and precursor domains; their outputs do not confirm identities.

These engines compare experimental and reference m/z/intensity arrays to retrieve and rank candidate library records. Similarity alone does not confirm chemical identity.

docs.title: Supported Stable Engines
docs.text: The similarity.algorithm field in your massflow_config.yaml determines which scoring engine is used for the annotation workflow.

docs.title: cosine
docs.text:
The classic Cosine Greedy algorithm. It computes the normalized dot product of the aligned fragment peaks between two spectra.

similarity:
  algorithm: "cosine"
  ms1_tolerance: 0.02
  ms2_tolerance: 0.02
  tolerance_unit: "Da"
  min_score: 0.6
  min_matched_peaks: 3
  fdr_threshold: 0.05

When to use: This is the standard choice for comparing identical MS/MS spectra (e.g., standardizing against an authenticated reference library). The precursor m/z of the query and reference must match within the configured ms1_tolerance.

docs.title: modified_cosine
docs.text:
An extension of the classic cosine algorithm designed to account for mass shifts (neutral losses) between a query and a reference. It aligns peaks by calculating the difference between the precursor masses (\(\Delta M\)) and shifting the query fragments by that amount.

similarity:
  algorithm: "modified_cosine"
  ms2_tolerance: 0.02
  tolerance_unit: "Da"
  min_score: 0.6
  min_matched_peaks: 3
  fdr_threshold: 0.05

When to use: Search for spectra with precursor-shifted fragment patterns, such as possible structural analogues. A modified-cosine match alone does not confirm an analogue or molecular identity.

docs.title: Configuration Parameters
docs.text:
The legacy fdr_threshold is a numerical candidate filter, not a calibrated false-discovery guarantee. Consult confidence semantics before interpreting q-like values.

The similarity section controls candidate scoring and retention. Structural metadata checks are described separately; a retained candidate is not a validated identification.

docs.title: ms1_tolerance
docs.text:
• Type: float
  • Default: 10.0
  • Description: The maximum allowable difference between the query precursor m/z and the reference precursor m/z.
  • Note: This is only strictly enforced by the standard cosine engine. The modified_cosine engine intentionally ignores this to allow for mass-shifted analog searching.

docs.title: ms2_tolerance
docs.text:
• Type: float
  • Default: 0.02
  • Description: The maximum allowable m/z difference for two fragment peaks to be considered an alignment match during scoring.

docs.title: tolerance_unit
docs.text:
• Type: string ("Da" or "ppm")
  • Default: "Da"
  • Description: The unit of measurement applied to the tolerances.

docs.title: min_score
docs.text:
• Type: float
  • Default: 0.6
  • Description: The absolute minimum similarity score (0.0 to 1.0) required to retain a candidate before configured confidence filtering.

docs.title: min_matched_peaks
docs.text:
• Type: int
  • Default: 3
  • Description: The minimum number of aligned fragment peaks required. Even if two spectra share a single extremely intense peak that yields a high cosine score, the hit will be rejected if it does not meet this physical evidence threshold.

docs.title: fdr_threshold
docs.text:
• Type: float
  • Default: 0.05
  • Description: Legacy threshold applied to the numerical query-level target/decoy estimate. Estimates are explicitly uncalibrated; changing this value changes candidate selection, not the evidence for FDR control. See confidence semantics.

docs.title: Experimental Engines
docs.text:
MassFlow contains several advanced machine learning models and orchestration logic (like spec2vec, ms2deepscore, consensus, and cascade).

Because these engines require external model weights, complex validation, or specific tie-breaking logic, they are not currently part of the stable v0.1 pipeline contract.

For documentation on how to configure and run these engines at your own risk, see the Similarity Engine API reference.

docs.title: MassFlow CLI Usage Guide
docs.text: This guide walks you through a complete, self-contained MassFlow workflow — from generating synthetic tutorial data through to annotation results — using nothing but the commands listed below. Every file path in this guide is real; copy and paste each command in order and everything will work.

docs.title: 0. Generate Tutorial Data
docs.text:
Before running any annotation commands, generate a synthetic dataset that includes a reference library, experimental queries, and a pre-configured YAML config file.

# Source checkout only: the synthetic generator is a repository script,
# not an installed CLI command.
uv run python scripts/generate_tutorial_data.py

The generator is not bundled in the wheel or sdist. Installed users should start with massflow init and their own data.

This creates a tutorial/ directory containing:

File Description tutorial/tutorial_library.msp Reference library with 3 steroid standards (Testosterone, Progesterone, Cortisol) tutorial/tutorial_experimental.mgf 4 experimental query spectra (matches, analogues, and noise) tutorial/tutorial_config.yaml Pre-configured analysis parameters (cosine similarity, 0.02 Da tolerance)

docs.title: 1. Build a Reference Database
docs.text:
Compile the raw MSP library into a high-performance SQLite database for rapid, memory-aware annotation workflows.

uv run massflow db build \
    --input tutorial/tutorial_library.msp \
    --output tutorial/results/compiled_library.db \
    --config tutorial/tutorial_config.yaml \
    --category library

Expected output: ✓ Successfully processed and added 3 spectra to tutorial/results/compiled_library.db.

docs.title: 2. Inspect the Database (Optional)
docs.text:
Verify the compiled database contents:

uv run massflow db inspect tutorial/results/compiled_library.db

docs.title: 3. Initialize a Custom Workspace (Optional)
docs.text:
If you want to generate a fresh configuration file for your own data rather than using the tutorial config:

# Generate configuration file in the current directory
uv run massflow init --output massflow_config.yaml

# Overwrite an existing configuration file
uv run massflow init --output massflow_config.yaml --force

docs.title: 4. Run an Annotation
docs.text:
Annotate experimental spectra against the compiled SQLite reference library.

If you're using the tutorial config (generated in Step 0), first update it to point to the SQLite database instead of the raw MSP file:

# In tutorial/tutorial_config.yaml, change:
input:
  library_path: "tutorial/results/compiled_library.db"

Execute the pipeline:

uv run massflow annotate --config tutorial/tutorial_config.yaml

Expected output: ✓ Annotation complete! Results saved to tutorial/results

Results are exported as defined in the configuration (tutorial/results/tutorial_experimental_results.csv).

docs.title: 5. Check the Results
docs.text:
The CSV results file contains annotation hits with computed scores, matched peaks, and automated Annotation_Status tags (Matched, Putative, or Unknown).

# Quick peek at results:
head -n 5 tutorial/results/tutorial_experimental_results.csv

docs.title: Convert Vendor Files
docs.text:
Convert vendor raw files (.raw, .d) to open formats (.mzML) using ProteoWizard msconvert:

uv run massflow convert --input data/raw/ --output data/experiments/

docs.title: Watch Mode
docs.text:
Interactive live-reloading that re-runs the pipeline whenever files or config change:

uv run massflow watch --config tutorial/tutorial_config.yaml

docs.title: Scientific Validation & Data Integrity
docs.text: MassFlow applies explicit checks to declared molecular metadata and reports processing rejections. These checks can detect inconsistencies under the registered chemistry and fixed tolerances; they do not prove a structure or establish universal instrument, matrix, or adduct validity.

docs.title: Precursor Mass Validation (5 ppm)
docs.text:
A cornerstone of MassFlow's data integrity is the 5.0 ppm precursor tolerance check.

In high-resolution mass spectrometry, the experimental precursor m/z must align with the theoretical monoisotopic mass of the candidate molecule, adjusted for its ionization adduct and charge state.

When the MassFlow.models layer processes a candidate structure (via a chemical formula, SMILES, or InChI), it automatically:

  1. Calculates the exact monoisotopic mass of the neutral molecule (formula-first, pyteomics; structure parsing via RDKit when no formula is declared).
  2. Identifies the adduct offset (e.g., +1.007276 Da for [M+H]+).
  3. Requires the declared signed charge to agree with the registered adduct (for example, [M+2H]2+ requires +2). Contradictory charge magnitude or sign sets is_physically_valid = False.
  4. Computes the theoretical m/z: \((ExactMass + AdductOffset) / |Charge|\).
  5. Compares this to your experimental precursor_mz.

If the deviation is greater than 5.0 ppm, the declared metadata fails this fixed software check. This prevents a candidate row from passing on contradictory declared precursor/structure metadata; it does not confirm candidates that pass.

docs.title: Where the check is enforced
docs.text:
• Model layer — the two Pydantic contracts above always compute the verdict (is_physically_valid); this is the stable core implementation, and both streaming and classical paths consume it.
  • Streaming ingestion gate (experimental stream-server) — incoming packets that violate the contracts are rejected with a structured StreamingValidationError before scoring.
  • Classical annotate / db build processing gate — during metadata processing (MassFlow.processing), explicitly declared recognized adduct/charge pairs are checked after matchms harmonization; spectra with structural claims also receive structural and 5 ppm mass checks:
  • a query spectrum that fails the gate (malformed claim, unsupported adduct with a complete context, or a >5 ppm precursor deviation) is rejected and counted (spectra_rejected) with a human-readable reason in the quarantine log; a file whose spectra are all rejected is an explicit failed result with the reasons in <stem>_failed.report.yaml;
  • a raw reference library entry that fails the gate aborts the annotate run with a PhysicalIntegrityError listing the offending spectra, because silently changing the candidate library would change every query's search results and legacy numerical estimates. massflow db build is the curation workflow: it quarantines such entries (they are never stored) and reports the stored count.
  • spectra without structural claims skip the structural/5 ppm mass checks, but an explicitly declared supported adduct/charge pair is still validated.

An adduct is required for the precursor-mass comparison: it may be declared explicitly or imputed from ionmode (positive → [M+H]+, negative → [M-H]-). When a recognized adduct and charge are both explicitly declared, their signed-charge consistency is checked independently of precursor availability. The 5 ppm mass comparison still requires a structural claim and usable precursor mass. Missing adduct/charge context skips the corresponding check.

docs.title: Applying validation changes to stored libraries
docs.text:
Managed prepared caches are fingerprinted with canonical processing configuration plus processing-semantics revision 4, which covers missing-precursor normalization, fragment-only m/z windows, charge/adduct consistency, and source-record identity. Older managed caches rebuild once from raw sources using staged replacement. A raw library with contradictory structural metadata aborts preparation with the rejection reason.

User-supplied .db, .sqlite, and .zarr libraries are used directly and are not revalidated or rewritten automatically. Rebuild from the original raw sources with massflow db build into a new output path that does not already exist: the command appends to an existing store, so reusing the old output preserves invalid entries. Inspect the new store and review quarantine messages/counts, then update input.library_path to the new store. See the charge/adduct experiment for evidence and limitations.

docs.title: Supported Adducts & Offsets
docs.text:
MassFlow maintains a high-precision internal registry of monoisotopic offsets for common LC-MS adducts:

Adduct Mode Offset (Da) Description [M+H]+ Pos +1.007276 Protonated [M+NH4]+ Pos +18.033826 Ammonium [M+Na]+ Pos +22.989221 Sodium [M+K]+ Pos +38.963158 Potassium [M]+ Pos -0.000549 Radical Cation [M+2H]2+ Pos +2.014553 Doubly protonated [M+3H]3+ Pos +3.021829 Triply protonated [M+2Na-H]+ Pos +44.971165 Disodium salt [M+H-H2O]+ Pos -17.003288 Protonation with water loss [M+CH3CN+H]+ Pos +42.033826 Acetonitrile adduct [M+CH3OH+H]+ Pos +33.033491 Methanol adduct [M-H]- Neg -1.007276 Deprotonated [M-2H]2- Neg -2.014553 Doubly deprotonated [M+Cl]- Neg +34.969401 Chlorine [M+Br]- Neg +78.918886 Bromine [M+I]- Neg +126.905022 Iodine [M+HCOO]- Neg +44.998203 Formate [M+CH3COO]- Neg +59.013853 Acetate [M+TFA-H]- Neg +112.985587 Trifluoroacetate [M+HCO3]- Neg +60.993117 Bicarbonate [M+NO3]- Neg +61.988366 Nitrate [M]- Neg +0.000549 Radical Anion

docs.title: Notation is normalised, not guessed
docs.text:
Library files spell the same ion in many ways, and a spelling the registry could not resolve used to quarantine an otherwise correct spectrum. Adduct notation is therefore canonicalised before lookup (see MassFlow.cheminformatics.normalize_adduct):

  • Brackets and charge position: M+H, [M+H]1+, [M+H]+1, and [M+H]+ are equivalent; interior whitespace and unbalanced brackets are tolerated.
  • Letter case: [m+h]+ and M+NA resolve to [M+H]+ and [M+Na]+.
  • Alias chemistry: formate written as M+FA-H/M+HCOOH-H, acetate as M+OAc/M+Ac-H, trifluoroacetate as M+CF3COO, acetonitrile as M+ACN+H, and M-H2O+H all resolve to their canonical keys.

Normalisation fails closed: notation that declares a charge contradicting the chemistry (e.g. [M+H]2+), a charge-less ambiguous body (M), or chemistry outside the registry (e.g. [M+Weird]+) still resolves to nothing and is still rejected by the gate. Crucially, normalisation cannot manufacture a false positive — the resolved adduct must still clear the 5 ppm precursor tolerance.

docs.title: Theoretical Isotopic Envelopes
docs.text:
For advanced structural verification, MassFlow automatically generates Theoretical Isotopic Envelopes for every reference compound with a valid SMILES string.

Using high-precision calculations (via pyteomics and RDKit), the pipeline determines the relative abundance and centroid masses of the M, M+1, M+2, and M+3 isotopologues.

  • MS1 Verification: This envelope establishes a ground-truth signature that can be compared against experimental MS1 data.
  • Tie-Breaking: If two candidates share similar MS2 fragmentation scores, the ConsensusEngine can use the isotopic pattern fit as an orthogonal tie-breaker to select the most likely structure.

docs.title: Spectral Integrity Checks
docs.text:
Beyond chemical structures, MassFlow validates the physical properties of the mass spectra themselves:

  1. Monotonicity: The mz_array must be strictly increasing. Out-of-order peaks (common in malformed open formats) are detected and blocked.
  2. Array Parity: The m/z and intensity arrays must have identical lengths.
  3. Positive Intensity: All intensities are validated to ensure they are non-negative.
  4. Minimum Peak Counts: Configurable thresholds (default: 5 peaks) ensure that "empty" or noise-only spectra do not consume CPU cycles in the similarity engine.

docs.title: Triage Bitmasking
docs.text:
During the library ingestion phase (massflow db build), MassFlow performs a fast NumPy-based scan of every spectrum to identify diagnostic fragments.

These fragments (e.g., the Tyrosine immonium ion at 136.076 Da) are stored in a triage_flags bitmask in the SQLite database, so downstream stages can route specific spectra toward specialized ML models without re-scanning the raw peak data.

docs.title: Scientific red-team experiment: charge/adduct contradictions
docs.text:
Integration note: this report documents standalone processing-semantics revision 1. The combined candidate uses revision 4 for missing-precursor normalization, fragment-only windows, charge/adduct consistency, and acquisition-record identity; the historical standalone revision is not the current managed-cache contract.

Run date: 2026-10-17 (America/Vancouver). Baseline: 5b847c0c45af32f2a2286371b4893c2af5481903.

docs.title: Finding
docs.text:
Demonstrated implementation defect: a structurally annotated spectrum could pass precursor validation with a charge that contradicted its registered adduct. For synthetic caffeine, [M+2H]2+ plus charge +1 passed at m/z 196.094928513, twice the correct m/z 98.047464256. That is a 1,000,000 ppm error relative to the declared adduct, despite the 5 ppm validation contract. The retained row could then yield cosine 1.0 with three matched fragments.

This is evidence of an invalid library claim entering scoring, not a measured false-identification rate or evidence of how frequently real libraries contain such metadata. No FDR calibration claim follows from this experiment.

docs.title: Target selection and hypothesis
docs.text:
Reviewed current issues, open PRs, recent commits, existing physics/adduct tests, and the golden validation manifest/documentation before choosing this target. Issue #95 already records the fragment-range bug; issue #91 records the decoy-null investigation. Neither is this experiment's target. PR #76 added canonical adduct handling and signed registry charges, but the precursor validator did not compare that charge with the separate charge metadata field. Existing adduct tests reject contradictory notation within one string; they did not exercise a contradiction between those two metadata fields.

Hypothesis: the validator uses the adduct's atom/electron offset but divides by the separately declared abs(charge). A mass calculated with a contradictory charge can therefore pass; abs() also hides polarity contradictions.

Recent baseline changes were the prepared-cache replacement (#99), SciPy compatibility (#98), and build-only library workflow (#96). No claim is made about the historical introducing commit; a bisect was not performed.

docs.title: Discriminating experiment and data
docs.text:
All spectra are explicitly synthetic. No experimental acquisition, instrument mass accuracy, real caffeine fragmentation abundance, or public reference-spectrum identity is asserted.

  • Neutral formula: caffeine, C8H10N4O2; matching SMILES: CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C.
  • Neutral/proton masses come directly from pyteomics, independently of MassFlow's adduct-offset and theoretical-mass helpers. Expected m/z is (neutral_mass + n * proton_mass) / abs(z), with n fixed by the adduct. See the Pyteomics mass API.
  • Synthetic fragment m/z values: [42.033826, 67.029075, 69.044725]; intensities [0.4, 1.0, 0.6], all float64. These are rounded ion masses for the caffeine-compatible subformulas C2H4N+, C3H3N2+, C3H5N2+, including subtraction of the electron mass from each neutral formula mass. They are chosen to give an exact, hand-computable cosine of 1 for identical peak vectors, not to simulate a measured spectrum.
  • Change only the metadata charge/precursor relationship. Test both formula and SMILES resolution, correct-charge controls, and 4.75/5.25 ppm boundaries.
  • Exercise the real Pydantic validators, matchms harmonisation, batch quarantine, ordinary cosine MS1 filtering, and actual SQLite/Zarr/hybrid prepared stores. Chemistry, mass validation, and scoring are not mocked.
Adduct Declared charge Input m/z Baseline verdict Corrected verdict [M+H]+ +1 195.087652046 valid valid [M+2H]2+ +2 98.047464256 valid valid [M-H]- -1 193.073099112 valid valid [M+2H]2+ +1 196.094928513 valid invalid [M+H]+ +2 97.543826023 valid invalid [M+H]+ -1 195.087652046 valid invalid [M-H]- +1 193.073099112 valid invalid

For the scoring experiment, the unknown synthetic query has precursor m/z 196.094928513, [M+H]+, charge +1, no structural claim, and the three fragments above. Search uses cosine, MS1/MS2 tolerance 0.02 Da, minimum score 0.7, minimum matched peaks 3, decoys disabled. The malformed caffeine row survived processing and produced score 1.0 / three matched peaks on the baseline. After correction it is quarantined and produces no hit. The correctly labelled double-charge control survives processing at 98.047464256 but produces no hit against that query because it is outside the cosine MS1 window. This isolates the metadata defect from intended modified-cosine analogue matching and from statistical calibration.

docs.title: Root cause and correction
docs.text:
SpectrumMetadata.validate_precursor_mass_logic() combined the registered adduct offset with the independent, unchecked charge denominator. It now requires exact agreement with the registry's signed charge before applying the existing m/z formula and unchanged 5 ppm threshold. The processing rejection reason identifies the contradictory charge/adduct rather than reporting a misleading zero ppm error. The ingestion guarantee applies to metadata after matchms harmonisation. Existing matchms behaviour can repair an original charge-sign contradiction when explicit ionmode supplies the intended polarity: [M+H]+/charge -1/positive becomes charge +1, and [M-H]-/charge +1/negative becomes charge -1. Those repaired records still pass if their masses are consistent; original-sign auditing is not implemented here. The model itself rejects either original contradiction.

Managed prepared stores previously fingerprinted configuration alone. Correcting the validator without changing that fingerprint left old invalid entries reusable; seven additional tests demonstrated this bypass before the fingerprint correction. The fingerprint now includes canonical configuration plus processing-semantics revision 1. Old managed caches are reprocessed once through the existing staged replacement code. Tests cover all three backends, no old/new mixing, reuse after successful rebuilding, and aborting a raw library with contradictory entries. This introduces the revision mechanism anticipated by #95; its fragment-filter correction remains outstanding and must increment the revision when implemented.

Migration limit: externally supplied .db, .sqlite, and .zarr libraries continue to be trusted direct inputs. They are not retrospectively revalidated or modified. Rebuild them from original raw sources with massflow db build into a new output path that does not already exist. Building into an existing store appends spectra and would preserve its invalid entries. Inspect the new store and review quarantine messages/counts before switching input.library_path to it. Missing structural context/charge keeps its documented exemption. Direct similarity calls that bypass preprocessing also bypass this ingestion gate. The experimental streaming transport is outside this test's validated scope.

docs.title: Reproduction and verification
docs.text:
From the review branch, run:

uv sync --locked --extra chem
uv run pytest tests/test_charge_adduct_consistency.py -v
uv run --isolated --locked --no-extra chem pytest tests/test_charge_adduct_consistency.py -v
uv run pytest --cov=src/MassFlow --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=80 -v
uv lock --check
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy .

Before the validator fix, the initial 30-case experiment produced 11 failures, 19 passes, including formula and SMILES contradictions; valid-ion/boundary controls passed. After fixing validation, all 30 passed. The seven cache/revision tests then failed for the expected stale-cache reuse or unchanged-fingerprint reason, and all 37 cases passed after adding the revision.

After correcting the synthetic fragments for electron mass during review, the final fixture was copied to a separate, pristine checkout of the exact baseline commit and retested: 11 failed, 19 passed, 7 deselected. The standalone scoring probe again retained the contradictory row and returned cosine 1.0 / three matches; the valid double-charge control remained unmatched. Import provenance confirmed that this repetition used the baseline checkout's source. Final quality gates below use the corrected fixture.

The untouched baseline full suite passed: 1,355 passed, 7 skipped, 35 deselected; 82.39% coverage. Baseline lint, formatting and mypy also passed.

Corrected-tree quality gates on the same macOS environment:

Gate Result Full mandatory coverage command above 1,392 passed, 7 skipped, 35 deselected; 82.42% coverage, exit 0 Focused charge/adduct and cache regressions 37 passed, exit 0 Lockfile consistency passed Repository lint and formatting passed Repository mypy passed, 146 source files Golden scientific fixtures unchanged; included in passing full suite

The full suite emitted 81 non-fatal warnings (the baseline emitted 79). Hosted Linux/macOS PR checks are separate from these local results.

The isolated run without the chem extra passed all 37 cases. Its environment still installed RDKit transitively through matchms; this run does not verify an environment in which RDKit cannot be imported. Formula-based cases always run and use pyteomics; the SMILES cases have the established optional-dependency skip.

Environment: macOS 27.0.1 arm64, CPython 3.13.12, matchms 0.33.1, SciPy 1.16.3, NumPy 2.2.6, pyteomics 4.7.5, Pydantic 2.13.4, RDKit 2026.3.1, committed lockfile. The imported MassFlow.__file__ was verified inside the isolated review worktree. Golden scientific fixtures were not regenerated.

Repository governance mismatch: AGENTS.md requests a core pytest marker, but the strict marker registry currently has no core entry and existing tests do not use it. These regressions follow the registered scientific convention and run in the full mandatory release suite; no separate comprehensive core-marker gate is claimed.

Passing regression tests establishes the specified software correction. It does not establish identification specificity, real-library prevalence, exchangeable decoys, empirical FDR control, or independent scientific validation.

docs.title: FDR and confidence-reporting audit
docs.text: Baseline: main ffef50bff913fcf400cb3de72595dab50e4f3fd8. Review date: 2026-10-22. This change corrects inspectability and proven numerical-input/ serialization defects; it does not supply missing empirical calibration.

docs.title: Findings and correction
docs.text:
1. Main computes a pooled best-target/best-decoy query-maxima ratio with a +1 numerator and reverse-minimum closure. Both sides may include the same query; it is not paired winner-take-all TDC. Independent review reproduced a tied-score undercount: targets [0.6,0.9,0.9,0.9], decoys [0.6,0.6] gave q(0.6)=2/3; the complete-threshold formula gives 3/4. Partial ranks inside a tie were allowed into reverse-minimum closure and the per-score lookup selected the first descending occurrence. Counts now include each entire tie block before closure. Both q fields and threshold selection can change for affected ties. An independent enumeration covers all 1,156 pairs of nonempty sorted vectors of length 1–4 over three score levels, in addition to named counterexamples.
  2. Nonfinite values could silently disappear from query maxima or enter array ranking. Arrays now require one-dimensional finite real scores; invalid candidate families get an explicit invalid assessment and workflow failure.
  3. Empty-null values q=1/N_target, p=1 were described as conservative bounds. They are retained only as historical numerical diagnostics; the statistical estimate is null with state unavailable. No empirical bound follows from them.
  4. A nonempty decoy null was being described as calibrated. A new assessment reports estimated_uncalibrated, never calibrated; it records method/version, family, unit, sample counts, nullable estimate and unvalidated assumptions. All newly assessed unvalidated hits use Annotation_Status=Uncalibrated.
  5. Candidate rows inherit the best-target query statistic. The new metadata says candidate_specific=false and query_best_target; extra rows are not discoveries independently supported by that q value.
  6. Streaming serialization converted a numerical q of 0 to NaN through truthiness, and an absent response q defaulted to zero. Explicit presence checks preserve numerical zero and use NaN for missing experimental streaming confidence. This does not make per-packet FDR available or validate the experimental API.
  7. README and scoring/results guidance overstated identity, exchangeability and calibration, and encouraged threshold relaxation as a remedy. Those claims are corrected. Numerical ranking, chemical plausibility, putative annotation and empirical confirmation remain distinct.

docs.title: Assumptions not established
docs.text:
The source retains target precursor/adduct/other metadata, permutes selected intensities and jitters fragments uniformly by +/-1 Da by default. The jitter includes displacements smaller than the scoring tolerance. Entropy preservation alone does not establish a chemically credible false-match population. Degenerate intensities can be tapered, so entropy preservation is not universal either.

Candidate eligibility, precursor and fragment tolerances, shifted matching, minimum-score/peak gates and adduct/RT filters condition which target and decoy maxima survive. Duplicate acquisitions, repeated structures, query dependence, per-file partitioning, library composition and routed engine scales can change numerical estimates. None is repaired by a universal library-size threshold or by adding a pseudo-count. The new method metadata preserves these limitations.

docs.title: Evidence and tests
docs.text:
The initial new assessment/input/serialization test run on unchanged baseline failed 27 cases and passed one valid numerical-array control. After correction, the new suite passes; separate red/green tests reproduce zero-to-missing streaming coercion and absent-to-zero response coercion. Tests include empty/no-target/null cases, one surviving decoy, score ties, nonmonotonic raw ratios, redundant candidate rows, target-absent labels and NaN/infinity/non-vector/complex/boolean inputs.

The independent oracle enumerates complete score cutoffs and computes tail counts; it does not reproduce the implementation's sorting/cumulative-sum steps. Constructed caffeine integration inputs exercise real files, formula/adduct/5-ppm validation, SQLite preparation, workflow estimation and native CSV/YAML output. These are software tests, not measured fragmentation validation.

Golden changes are deliberate reporting semantics: annotation_status values change from Matched/Putative to Uncalibrated and unsupported warning claims are corrected in the scientific manifest. Scores, q/p numbers, matched peaks, ranks, FDR counts and input spectra are unchanged. The older multiprocessing CSV anchor is still compared on all its original numerical columns, with an explicit five-column confidence extension and the specified status migration. The independent fixture generator now checks the same reporting policy; it was not used to regenerate numerical expectations.

Final frozen verification: 1,393 passed, 7 skipped, 35 deselected; 82.53% coverage with the mandatory full command. The focused FDR/workflow selection has 98 passing cases, including all 37 new confidence tests. Ruff, formatting, mypy, strict MkDocs and wheel/sdist build pass. The independent review found the tie, no-hit export and warning defects but exhausted quota before its final full review; that review remains required before merging. Verification metadata records log hashes and the excluded intermediate coverage measurement.

docs.title: Experimental calibration remains pending
docs.text: Historical 600-query cross-instrument MoNA outputs have empty-decoy regimes, zero LTQ calls and unresolved dirty/environment/source-lineage limitations. They do not validate this null generator or a nominal error bound. A separate frozen MassBank benchmark is being prepared using measured standard records and known present/absent structures; its retrieval results must not be treated as FDR control. A single surviving decoy permits the arithmetic but is sparse evidence, explicitly recorded as single_decoy_observation. Known-truth independent-batch calibration and uncertainty remain required before a calibrated state can be justified.

docs.title: Compatibility / remaining risks
docs.text:
• Historical empty-null q_value/p_value and fdr_threshold behavior remain for compatibility; tied-score estimates are corrected. Consumers must check confidence_state and confidence_q_value. Empty-null legacy filtering remains query-count dependent and must not be used to claim error control.
  • Direct similarity APIs and older manually exported rows can lack assessments; their legacy score labels are not evidence of calibration.
  • Invalid input now fails explicitly; callers relying on silent NaN/inf omission must correct their input rather than infer confidence from the remaining rows.
  • Other source-record, charge, fragment-filter and prefilter corrections are separate PRs #101/#103–#107. This change does not integrate them or repair legacy libraries.
  • Streaming is experimental, has no per-packet calibration, and uses NaN for unavailable protobuf confidence. Full explicit-state protocol migration is deferred.

See confidence semantics for the exact machine-readable contract and primary literature references. No merge or release.

docs.title: Executable MassBank diagnostic
docs.text:
An isolated benchmark now runs deposited experimental standard spectra through MassFlow.workflow.run_annotation_pipeline. The source, dataset selection and configuration are frozen. This does not change the historical audit/specification or complete every experiment in the scientific validation program.

The executable specification and reproduction command are in benchmarks/massbank-v1/README.md. It uses positive ESI [M+H]+ records from Athens queries and Eawag references, retains every query outcome, audits duplicates and reports exact-structure retrieval separately from confidence calibration. Source labels are depositor assertions of standard compounds, not independently authenticated identity. Limited contributor, adduct and polarity coverage precludes a general identification-accuracy claim.

Four arms compare cosine and modified cosine with all truths present, then with 50 connectivity groups removed from the library. Numerical q estimates are uncalibrated; no nominal FDR is accepted as empirical error control. Known unmerged correctness fixes remain a condition of interpretation. The measured results and remaining observability limits are documented in the benchmark directory.

docs.title: Finding
docs.text:
On main ffef50bff913fcf400cb3de72595dab50e4f3fd8, the default Numba prefilter silently removes some pairs that pass full modified-cosine scoring. With the default min_matched_peaks=3, two direct-fragment matches plus one precursor-shifted match yield score 1.0, three matched peaks, but no search result with acceleration enabled. The same input returns a hit with enable_numba_prefilter=False. Both the JIT kernel and its Python mirror have the incorrect gate; the engine activates the gate when Numba is available.

This is a demonstrated false negative and a reproducibility defect, since enabling the prefilter changes the accepted search results. Its frequency in measured data is unknown.

docs.title: Discriminating experiment
docs.text:
All spectra below are explicitly synthetic. They do not represent measured caffeine or theobromine fragmentation, authentic standards, or confirmed identifications. The precursor formulas and illustrative fragment formulas provide plausible small-molecule mass ranges while isolating the algorithm. Masses use real pyteomics.mass.calculate_mass(..., charge=1) calculations; the fixtures exercise the real formula/adduct/5-ppm integrity gate.

  • Reference precursor: C7H8N4O2, [M+H]+, charge +1, m/z 181.07200198165003.
  • Query precursor: C8H10N4O2, [M+H]+, charge +1, m/z 195.08765204578998.
  • Precursor difference: 14.015650064139948 Da.
  • Reference peaks: 67.02907454051, 97.03963922421, 109.03963922420998, derived from C3H2N2, C4H4N2O, C5H4N2O with charge +1.
  • Query peaks: add the precursor difference to the final one or two peaks. All intensities are 1.0; arrays are float64.
  • Scoring: modified_cosine, MS2 tolerance 0.02 Da, minimum score 0.7, minimum matched peaks 3. No decoys are used: this experiment isolates candidate recall, not confidence estimation.

For three disjoint matched pairs with unit intensities, the expected cosine is 3 / (sqrt(3) * sqrt(3)) = 1. The installed matchms 0.33.1 scorer independently returns that value and three matched peaks.

Synthetic query Direct matches Shifted matches Full score / peaks Main: prefilter off Main: prefilter on Corrected: prefilter on All direct 3 0 1.0 / 3 Hit Hit Hit All shifted 0 3 1.0 / 3 Hit Hit Hit Two direct, one shifted 2 1 1.0 / 3 Hit No hit Hit One direct, two shifted 1 2 1.0 / 3 Hit No hit Hit One direct, one shifted, one unmatched 1 1 2/3 / 2 No hit No hit No hit

The last control displaces the second query peak by 3 Da rather than preserving it. Regression tests also reverse query/reference roles, exercise the inclusive tolerance boundary with exactly representable masses, and verify that overlapping frames cannot inflate the final one-to-one match count.

docs.title: Root cause and correction
docs.text:
_prefilter_pairs_numba and _prefilter_pairs_python previously required max(direct_count, loss_count) >= min_matches, in both their allocation and emission passes. Modified cosine assigns peaks over the union of direct and shifted candidate edges, as documented in the matchms scorer. MassFlow's independent golden-fixture reference scorer also uses this union.

For each sorted frame, the two-pointer count is a maximum-cardinality matching. Partition the scorer's selected edges by frame; each subset is bounded by its frame's maximum count. Thus their sum is an upper bound on the combined selected count, while their maximum is not. The correction uses the sum in all four gate sites, keeping the existing early exit when direct matches suffice. Cross-frame double counting can admit extra candidates, but full scoring still resolves peak reuse and applies the final matched-peak and score thresholds. This is a conservative pruning bound, not a replacement score or a scientific heuristic. The cosine-only gate is unchanged.

Here, full scoring means the existing matchms ModifiedCosineGreedy scorer, which uses greedy peak assignment, rather than an optimal Hungarian assignment. The count bound assumes that counters and scorer recognize the same tolerance-compatible peak pairs. Floating-point differences in how they compare masses at a tolerance boundary remain a separate, pre-existing limitation; this correction does not establish recall equivalence for every float64 input. The regression boundary fixtures use exactly representable masses to isolate the mixed-frame counting defect.

docs.title: Reproduction and scope
docs.text:
Run the committed experiment/regression tests:

uv sync --locked --all-extras
uv run pytest tests/test_mixed_frame_prefilter.py -v

Copy that test file onto the stated main revision to reproduce the before state: 18 failures, 8 passes. On the correction all 26 pass. The baseline full suite passed 1356 tests, with 7 skipped, 35 deselected, and 82.33% coverage, demonstrating the existing coverage gap. The corrected full suite passed 1382 tests, with 7 skipped, 35 deselected, and 82.46% coverage using the mandatory command:

uv run pytest --cov=src/MassFlow --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=80 -v

These results were freshly reproduced on 2026-10-21 UTC, on macOS arm64, Python 3.13.12, matchms 0.33.1, NumPy 2.2.6, Numba 0.61.2. Lockfile validation, Ruff lint/format, mypy, all pre-commit hooks, and strict MkDocs build passed. An independent read-only review checked all four gate sites and the matching bound; its documentation findings are reflected in the limitations above. Hosted Linux/macOS CI remains a separate check on the resulting PR head.

This correction restores the demonstrated candidate recall. Additional candidates can affect downstream rankings and target-decoy estimates; the experiment does not establish identification accuracy, empirical FDR calibration, or the scientific reliability of analogue annotations. No golden expected values were regenerated, and no confidence estimator was changed.

docs.title: Spectral-record provenance review
docs.text: Integration note: this report documents standalone processing-semantics revision 3. The combined candidate uses revision 4 for all processing-affecting corrections; the historical standalone revision is not the current managed-cache contract.

docs.title: What was reproduced
docs.text:
Reviewed main ffef50bff913fcf400cb3de72595dab50e4f3fd8, active worktrees, recent PRs/issues, the experimental network branch 73deedf, matchms 0.33.1 metadata repair, and existing storage/lineage/search/export tests. No dedicated InChIKey metadata-cache implementation was found in those inspected paths.

Two constructed caffeine records with the same InChIKey and distinct record IDs retained their different source files, library accessions, collision energies, adducts, instruments and instrument types. Reversing processing order did not produce crossover. The reported InChIKey-keyed metadata inheritance was therefore not reproduced on current main.

Two related provenance failures were reproduced:

  1. Stable library ingestion/search/export: raw libraries without id keep that absence through preparation. Two different acquisitions then both produce reference_id="None", including two modified-cosine hits scoring 1.0 with three matched peaks. Repeated explicit IDs similarly fail to distinguish records. The store retains acquisition metadata, but annotation IDs cannot unambiguously link back to it.
  2. Experimental consensus: results aggregate by (query_id, reference_id). Colliding IDs combine evidence from different acquisitions under a single metadata template. In the discriminating fixture, the protonated record scores 0.9622504486493763 in both engines; the sodiated record scores 0 in precursor-gated cosine and 1 in modified cosine. They must produce two consensus rows scoring approximately 0.96225 and 0.5, not one blended row. This collision does not require matching InChIKeys; sharing a structure does not make the acquisitions interchangeable.

Explicit None structural identifiers also caused matchms repair to raise and the batch pipeline to discard otherwise usable records. An absent InChIKey is not a reason to discard a valid measured spectrum or copy another record's key.

docs.title: Identity contract and correction
docs.text:
InChIKey represents chemical identity. id represents a spectral record in the library being searched. library_id names a library and is not a record key.

Raw library ingestion now opts into load_spectra(..., assign_record_ids=True):

  • Clone each loader record before adding provenance; acquisition metadata and float64 peak arrays stay with that record.
  • Preserve the first nonempty supplied id. Replace missing, empty or repeated IDs with massflow:sha256:<source-file-digest>:spectrum:<loader-index>.
  • Preserve the supplied ID in massflow_original_id, including explicit missingness. Record massflow_source_path, massflow_source_sha256 and massflow_source_index independently of chemical identifiers.
  • Count zero-based loader records before validation/filtering. A rejected record does not renumber subsequent acquisitions. This is the importer's record ordinal, not an assertion about vendor scan numbering or text lines.
  • Fail rather than reuse a generated ID if it collides with an earlier ID.

Managed annotation preparation, the direct raw-library adapter and db build enable this policy. Generic/query loading retains its existing behavior. Native store inputs are read without assigning new IDs or rewriting stored provenance. The source digest is content-based: moving identical bytes preserves generated IDs; changing source bytes changes them. The path/ordinal fields describe the file ingested on this call; declared upstream acquisition metadata is retained.

Consensus and cascade now reject missing, empty or duplicate reference IDs at their public search boundary. They also reject a supplied target ID that would collide with another record's generated <id>_decoy ID when decoys are enabled. Direct API callers and legacy-store users get an actionable error instead of silent record aggregation/routing. Classical scorers and confidence formulas are unchanged. Missing primary structural strings are normalized on a clone before repair, without supplying chemistry.

Annotations retain the existing reference_id column. Its value can be used to retrieve the complete stored acquisition record, then its source digest and ordinal. CSV and the experimental mzTab-shaped output do not add collision-energy or instrument columns; those fields remain in the referenced native-store record. MSP/MGF spectrum exports retain the acquisition fields and IDs as well.

docs.title: Cache and compatibility
docs.text:
Processing fingerprint revision 3 invalidates config-only managed caches. They rebuild using the existing staged replacement, then are reused. Tests demonstrate replacement rather than append for SQLite, Zarr and hybrid caches. This standalone revision does not incorporate PR #103 or #105. Combining their processing changes requires another revision, rather than aliasing revision 3.

Three historical multiprocessing CSV fixtures previously expected None as every reference ID. Only their reference_id cells are intentionally updated, using the fixture file's SHA-256 and independently enumerated NAME records. Every other cell, including scores, matched peaks, q-values and p-values, is unchanged. The scientific-validation manifest is not regenerated. An existing mock loader accepts the added keyword; its FDR assertions are unchanged.

docs.title: Reproducible tests
docs.text:
Fixtures are deliberately synthetic caffeine acquisitions, not measured spectra or confirmed identities. They use formula C8H10N4O2, real pyteomics adduct arithmetic and the actual formula/5-ppm validators. Three hypothetical fragments are at m/z 42.033826, 83.060374 and 138.066188. Acquisition A declares [M+H]+, collision_energy=20, QTOF-A, LIBRARY-A and ACCESSION-A; B declares [M+Na]+, collision_energy=45, Orbitrap-B, LIBRARY-B and ACCESSION-B. accession is canonicalized to spectrum_id by matchms; its value remains record-specific. No physical validator, isotope calculation or scoring algorithm is mocked.

uv sync --frozen
uv run pytest tests/test_spectral_record_provenance.py tests/test_record_identity_consensus.py -v
uv run pytest --cov=src/MassFlow --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=80 -v
uv run ruff check .
uv run mypy .
uv lock --check

To reproduce the failures, copy only the two regression files into a separate clean checkout at the base revision and verify MassFlow.__file__ points there. On the unchanged base the final 38 regressions produce 31 failed, 7 passed. The passing cases include the shared-structure preservation controls: this is not evidence of a structure-keyed metadata cache defect.

Independent review reproduced a further target/decoy collision: IDs x and x_decoy produced a consensus row with decoy-of-x precursor metadata but the sodiated target's score. Two additional regressions failed before adding the generated-namespace check. Decoy generation and confidence formulas are unchanged.

Coverage includes duplicate structures, absent/empty/repeated IDs (including InChIKey strings misused as record IDs), conflicting and missing acquisition fields, reversed input order, exact source ordinals after quarantine, generated ID stability, SQLite/Zarr/hybrid reopen and individual lookup, MSP/MGF spectrum round-trips, both classical scorers, CSV and experimental mzTab-shaped reference traceability, legacy cache replacement/reuse, experimental meta-engine ambiguity rejection, and target/generated-decoy ID collisions. Consensus/cascade tests are not marked core.

Validation on macOS arm64 / Python 3.13.12 with the unchanged lockfile:

  • Unchanged main full suite: 1,356 passed, 7 skipped, 35 deselected; 82.39% coverage.
  • Corrected final full suite: 1,394 passed, 7 skipped, 35 deselected; 82.44% coverage, including all 38 new regressions.
  • Focused ingestion/search/FDR/equivalence tests: 110 passed before adding the final three duplicate-InChIKey-ID variants; the full suite includes those.
  • Ruff lint, mypy, uv lock --check and strict MkDocs build pass. Full-suite warnings include unclosed SQLite resources; execution is not warning-free.
  • Independent read-only review found the target/decoy collision, verified its correction, independently passed all initial 36 cases and the final nine meta-engine cases, and found no remaining blocking code issues. It verified that all 12 changed golden rows differ only in reference_id.

docs.title: Remaining limits
docs.text:
• Existing external stores are not repaired automatically. Rebuild from raw sources into a new destination when IDs are absent or nonunique. Old exports containing None cannot be repaired from the export alone.
  • Supplied IDs remain scoped to a library. Appending/merging independently curated stores can introduce duplicate supplied IDs; the meta engines now reject these, but classical direct API callers must ensure uniqueness. This change does not migrate all store lookup or merge APIs.
  • Direct classical calls with manually constructed, unidentified Spectrum objects retain their old scoring behavior; callers must supply record IDs for traceable annotations. Use the library ingestion policy for raw files.
  • Source files must stay unchanged while hashing/parsing. The extra digest pass and ID set have not been performance-benchmarked. Parser-level records skipped before yielding cannot receive a loader ordinal from MassFlow.
  • Explicit configuration overrides (for example processing.instrument) still follow the existing contract; this patch does not reinterpret those settings.
  • Synthetic software tests do not measure real-library prevalence, identification accuracy, chemical identity validity or FDR calibration.

docs.title: Finding
docs.text:
On main ffef50bff913fcf400cb3de72595dab50e4f3fd8, a capped classical search can lose an eligible near-match because an ineligible higher-scoring reference consumes the result budget. The same search with top_n=None returns the eligible result. Both cosine and modified cosine are affected.

This is a reproducible candidate-recall defect in the search API. It does not establish how often this happens in measured data, compound identification accuracy, or FDR calibration. Default annotate and normal consensus sub-engine searches request unlimited candidates and do not exercise this defect. Consensus fallback can forward a caller's cap to the classical engine. That call site establishes reachability, not an end-to-end reproduction of every consuming workflow. Classical batch_score supplies only one reference per search, so it has no competing reference to trigger this defect.

docs.title: Hypothesis and decision rule
docs.text:
Before executing the new tests, the run protocol fixed this hypothesis: top_n is applied before polarity and retention-time eligibility checks. For each query, capped search must return the first N eligible, score-ordered results of unlimited search with the same parameters. A higher-scoring ineligible reference must not change that result.

The experiment varies the eligibility gate, algorithm, result cap, and reference delivery mode. No scoring algorithm, scientific threshold, confidence estimator, or golden fixture is changed to obtain a result.

docs.title: Explicit synthetic data
docs.text:
All spectra are deliberately constructed caffeine ions (C8H10N4O2). Neutral formula masses come from real pyteomics.mass.calculate_mass; precursor m/z uses registered [M+H]+ or [M-H]- offsets. Every constructed spectrum exercises the real MolecularStructure and SpectrumMetadata formula and 5-ppm validators. Nothing in those validators is mocked. RDKit is unnecessary.

The three ascending fragment atom inventories are C2H4N, C4H7N2, and C6H8N3O. Their masses are computed with pyteomics and corrected by minus one electron mass for positive fragments, plus one electron mass for negative fragments. Arrays are float64. These are hypothetical fragments, not measured caffeine MS/MS or a claim about a validated fragmentation pathway. Opposite fragment charges differ by two electron masses, within the 0.02 Da fragment window; the real polarity gate must still reject their pairing.

Spectrum Intensities RT in seconds Polarity Query (1, 1, 1) 60 positive Ineligible reference, RT arm (1, 1, 1) 600 positive Ineligible reference, polarity arm (1, 1, 1) 60 negative Eligible first (1, 1, 0.5) 61 positive Eligible second (1, 0.5, 0.5) 64 positive

RT tolerance is 5 seconds. Fragment tolerance is 0.02 Da; minimum matched peaks is 3; minimum score is 0.9. The RT arm uses a 0.02 Da precursor window. The polarity arm deliberately widens cosine's precursor window to 3 Da so the downstream polarity gate, rather than precursor separation, discriminates the negative reference. Modified cosine does not impose that precursor window. The experiment assumes comparable RT units and conditions; it does not validate cross-method use of retention time.

With isolated one-to-one fragment edges, both algorithms reduce to normalized dot products, independently derived as:

  • Ineligible reference: 3 / (sqrt(3) * sqrt(3)) = 1.
  • Eligible first: 2.5 / (sqrt(3) * sqrt(2.25)) = 0.9622504486493763.
  • Eligible second: 2 / (sqrt(3) * sqrt(1.5)) = 0.9428090415820634.

Each has three matched peaks. Tests assert those values using actual matchms pair scoring before testing MassFlow's result selection. See the matchms CosineGreedy definition for the matching tolerance and default intensity/mass powers. No ambiguous peak assignment or greedy-versus-optimal comparison is involved here.

docs.title: Reproduction and results
docs.text:
Environment: macOS arm64, Python 3.13.12, matchms 0.33.1, dependencies from the unchanged uv.lock.

uv sync --frozen
uv run pytest tests/test_top_n_eligibility.py -v

To reproduce the pre-fix failure, use a clean checkout of the base revision and copy only tests/test_top_n_eligibility.py into it. Verify MassFlow.__file__ points into that checkout before running. Do not revert a shared checkout.

Experiment Unchanged base Corrected Unlimited search, each arm/algorithm eligible first, eligible second same top_n=1, each arm/algorithm empty eligible first top_n=2, each arm/algorithm eligible first only both eligible references List / iterator / cached precursor-array modes same defect in all three eligible results preserved Two queries with mutually ineligible highest scorers both empty each gets its own eligible reference Missing RT, exact 5-second boundary, just outside boundary expected bypass/inclusion/rejection same Zero result budget empty empty

Before correction, the regression file yields 26 failed, 8 passed. Failures are assertions on missing eligible results; direct scoring, real chemistry validation, and unlimited-search assertions pass. After correction, all 34 regressions pass; the combined focused search/physics suite passes 120 tests. Iterator regressions use one library chunk; the existing wrapper remains responsible for combining and limiting results across chunks.

The mandatory full-suite command passes on both revisions:

uv run pytest --cov=src/MassFlow --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=80 -v
  • Unchanged base: 1,356 passed, 7 skipped, 35 deselected; 82.39% coverage.
  • Corrected: 1,390 passed, 7 skipped, 35 deselected; 82.39% coverage.
  • Ruff lint/format, mypy, uv lock --check, and strict MkDocs build pass.

Both full runs emit warnings, including unclosed SQLite resource warnings; passing the suite is not a claim of warning-free execution. Golden scientific fixtures and dependencies are unchanged.

docs.title: Root cause and minimal correction
docs.text:
SimilarityEngine.search sorted score/matched-peak survivors and sliced their indices to N. Only then did it evaluate adduct polarity and retention time. Rejecting a sliced candidate left a vacant slot without considering the next eligible reference.

The correction collects eligible results in the existing score order for each query, then slices that query's result list to N. None retains all results; zero remains empty. Scorers, physical validation, metadata gates, ordering, decoy generation and confidence formulas are unchanged. More metadata can be visited in capped searches because eligibility must precede truncation.

Decoys still share the existing result budget with targets. Changing that competition policy or calibrating top-N confidence is outside this correction. Software tests alone do not validate target-decoy assumptions. Existing active drafts #103, #104 and #105 address separate issues and are not incorporated here.

docs.title: Scientific validation program for core MS/MS annotation
docs.text:
Specification v1.0 — proposed experiments, not a validation certificate. Audit: 2026-10-21 America/Vancouver (2026-10-22 UTC). Implementation baseline: ffef50bff913fcf400cb3de72595dab50e4f3fd8, matching remote main when checked. No new experimental spectra were acquired and no new annotation benchmark was run for this specification. Existing saved outputs were recounted independently.

MassFlow has useful software correctness evidence and limited retrospective reference-library retrieval evidence. Chemical identification performance and empirical FDR control are not established for a declared deployment domain. A score, a passing test suite, or a nonempty decoy null cannot establish them.

Read the implementation/evidence audit, source assessment, manifest contract, and ordered GitHub-ready issue drafts alongside this protocol. The audit snapshot records source hashes and counts.

docs.title: 1. Intended decision and claim boundaries
docs.text:
The initial intended use is retrospective retrieval of a small-molecule library structure from centroided, experimental ESI-MS/MS reference spectra, with explicit abstention. This does not validate an LC/matrix workflow. Inlet types (LC, flow injection or direct infusion) are retained and reported separately for queries and references. The initial benchmark is positive-mode, singly protonated MS2; expansion to negative ions, other adducts, multiple charges, instruments, or matrices requires separate evidence. No quantitative concentration, recovery, LOD/LOQ, diagnostic, regulatory, peptide-search, or de novo structure-elucidation claim follows.

Three experiments answer different questions:

Experiment Library truth Decision being assessed Closed set At least one independent source acquisition of each query identity is present Can the true structure be retrieved and ranked? Open set Every reference equivalent to the query truth is removed Does the procedure abstain instead of assigning an incorrect structure? Confidence calibration A prespecified mixture of present and absent known truths Does the reported acceptance procedure achieve its claimed error behavior?

Modified cosine can retrieve analogues through precursor-shifted fragments. An analogue is incorrect for exact-structure retrieval even if chemically interesting; score analogue retrieval separately using independently curated relationships. Do not relabel incorrect identities as successes after inspection.

A library match supports a candidate annotation under tested conditions. It does not automatically confer a confirmed structure or a confidence level from an external framework. Confirmation needs independent evidence appropriate to that framework and use, including authentic standards and applicable orthogonal measurements [S1].

docs.title: 2. Freeze the study before scoring
docs.text:
1. Record the scientific question, intended domain, identity rules, error costs, acceptance criteria, primary endpoints, exclusions, candidate policy, configuration grid, and uncertainty method in a dated protocol. Freeze its SHA-256.
  2. Resolve the known affected-path software defects listed in the audit before a release-validation run. A run on baseline main is a diagnostic experiment with known limitations. Do not silently combine PRs or substitute their test results.
  3. Freeze the source release, asset hashes, record-level labels, acquisition groups, duplicate graph, all exclusions, development/test partitions, and two libraries (truth present / truth removed). Publish manifests where rights permit.
  4. Select settings on development structures only. Freeze the complete effective config, environment lock, clean application commit and harness commit. Any scientific change after unblinding creates a new version and a new independent confirmatory set; the old result stays in the record.
  5. Run the independent scorer baseline and MassFlow on identical frozen data. Save all candidates before q filtering, stage counters, best target/decoy scores, source-record mappings, failures, logs, final calls, and checksums.
  6. Unblind once, compute the prespecified tables, and retain all failed and negative results. All selected queries remain in the end-to-end denominator.

A repository change may be diagnostic and useful while still unsuitable for release validation. Capture git status, git diff digest, Python/OS/CPU, installed package versions using distribution names, lock hash, command line, seeds, backend, worker count, cache construction/reuse state, source hashes and run timestamps. A dirty SHA alone cannot reproduce uncommitted behavior. Existing provenance version fields containing requirement expressions must be checked against the actual installed versions; see the audit.

docs.title: Chemical identity
docs.text:
Primary endpoint: full standardized InChIKey agreement, with an archived structure, standardization policy/version, and independently reviewed mapping. This is a strict label comparison, not proof that MS/MS resolves stereochemistry. For stereochemically undefined references or insufficiently verified labels, report primary-endpoint ineligibility and a separate connectivity endpoint; do not invent stereochemical truth. Report stereo/isotope failures separately.

Secondary endpoint: first 14 InChIKey characters (connectivity block), explicitly named connectivity retrieval. Freeze salt/solvate stripping, neutralization, tautomer and isotope treatment before scoring; retain original structures and all alias mappings. Do not collapse unrelated ions by nominal mass, formula or name. Charged structures and mixtures require manual adjudication before inclusion. Evaluate correct ion/adduct/charge assignment separately from structure rank. A protonated and a sodiated spectrum may share chemical identity while being separate experimental records with different matching eligibility.

docs.title: Experimental record identity
docs.text: Use a source namespace + immutable accession/version + source-file SHA-256 and loader ordinal/native scan locator. A full InChIKey identifies a chemical label; it cannot identify an acquisition. Keep collision energy and its original units, instrument model/analyzer, polarity, adduct, charge, contributing laboratory, source experiment, raw file, processing lineage, and library accession per record. Preserve missing values. Every exported candidate must join to exactly one source spectrum. Aggregate structure ranks without discarding the contributing record IDs.

docs.title: Query eligibility
docs.text:
Select queries using label evidence and acquisition metadata before seeing MassFlow scores or whether its gates accept them. Primary reference-standard cohort: measured ESI MS2, verified centroided representation (or a documented, validated centroiding conversion), documented known standard identity, finite positive precursor, identified polarity/adduct/charge, interpretable acquisition lineage, and legal access. Records only labelled by another spectral search are a separate cohort. Exclude MS1, EI, MS3/pseudo-MS2/merged-stage spectra, simulated spectra, unverified suspects and ambiguous mixtures from the primary cohort. Record every exclusion.

Valid but sparse/noisy spectra remain selected; pipeline rejection is an outcome. Known metadata defects enter a labelled challenge cohort rather than quietly shrinking the primary denominator. Unknown truth cannot be counted correct or incorrect: report it separately, never treat it as a negative.

Keep the evaluator's structure/name/formula truth in a separate label table. Provide the search process only deployment-available query peaks, precursor, polarity, charge/adduct if measured/declared, instrument and CE. Remove query names, formula, SMILES, InChI/InChIKey, answer-bearing accessions and lookup routes from scoring input. Reference metadata may retain its legitimate library chemistry. Do not let query truth drive formula-derived filtering or metadata repair.

docs.title: Independence and leakage
docs.text:
Maintain separate IDs for chemical identity, vendor standard/sample lot, experiment/raw acquisition, scan, preprocessing derivative and spectral duplicate component. All scans, collision energies, consensus spectra, exports, and mirrored copies of one acquisition belong to the same group. Unknown lineage is unknown independence, not an independent replicate.

Development and test query structures and connectivity groups are disjoint; their acquisition and near-duplicate groups are disjoint too. This also prevents tuning exposure for the secondary connectivity endpoint. In a closed-set test the test structure must nevertheless exist in the searchable reference library: this is necessary, and differs from training/tuning exposure. Its query acquisition must be separate from reference acquisitions. For optional learned methods, additionally audit the actual model training structures/spectra; unavailable training data prevents an unseen-structure claim.

Audit across repositories using original accessions, raw-file/scan links, SPLASH, exact normalized peak hashes and near-duplicate comparisons. SPLASH alone does not certify independent acquisitions. Proposed conservative screening rule: flag pairs with equal polarity/adduct, precursor within 5 ppm, and direct cosine

=0.99 with >=90% of each spectrum's peaks matched within 0.005 Da. Also flag same-lineage pairs irrespective of score. These numbers are a study screening rule, not a chemical identity rule. Cluster linked derivatives; if independent lineage cannot resolve a flagged query/reference pair, exclude it from the strict independence cohort and retain it in the leakage sensitivity cohort. Audit the consequence of this exclusion; do not hide the loss of easy legitimate matches. Freeze the deduplication implementation and rule before evaluating retrieval.

docs.title: P0 — Software and provenance qualification
docs.text:
Run the required full coverage gate on the exact candidate release:

uv run pytest --cov=src/MassFlow --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=80 -v
uv run pytest -m core -v
uv run ruff check .
uv run mypy .
uv lock --check

These establish software evidence only. Add independent known-answer comparisons for greedy cosine, shifted matching, mixed frames, ppm boundaries, signed charge, missing metadata, ties, record collisions, source round-trips and rejected spectra. Compare the enabled prefilter with exhaustive exact scoring on every small-study query/reference pair. Compare in-memory, freshly built SQLite, warm managed cache, iterator/chunk and single/multiple-worker paths. Require identical eligible candidate identities, matched counts, rankings and q-values within declared float64 roundoff; numerical tolerance must never excuse changed threshold decisions. Inspect CSV and experimental mzTab-shaped joins and failed/rejected-query accounting. Legacy stores must be rebuilt into new paths; their lineage must identify the processing semantics.

docs.title: P1 — Closed-set acquisition-independent retrieval
docs.text:
Use one prespecified query acquisition per test structure for the primary analysis. Retain additional acquisitions for repeated-measurement/stratum analyses. Search against the entire frozen eligible background library plus independent references for the true structures, excluding all query acquisition groups and unresolved cross-set duplicates. Freeze the actual library size and spectrum multiplicity per structure; do not create a toy library containing only the correct answers.

Run cosine and modified cosine separately. Initial fixed operating configuration: ms1_tolerance=0.02 Da, resolution_ppm=null, ms2_tolerance=0.02 Da, min_score=0.6, min_matched_peaks=3, rt_tolerance=null, routing/HNSW off, top_n=None. Declare the modified-cosine default prefilter state and perform its exhaustive agreement control. Preserve processing defaults from the pinned version as complete JSON, with filter_by_mz=false; do not rely on changing defaults. These settings are a baseline, not an assertion of instrument suitability.

Use an analysis collection pass with fdr_threshold=1.0 to retain all score/match-gate-qualified targets and decoys; capture pre-q internal results as well, since normal exports omit decoys. Separately run the unchanged deployment config including its default q threshold. The collection pass is a benchmark instrumentation mode, not a recommendation to relax production confidence. For exhaustive candidate-loss diagnosis use the same processed spectra and scorer with score/match pruning disabled in the harness, and label that counterfactual.

Collapse eligible reference acquisitions to structures using maximum score, keeping all supporting record IDs. Rank distinct structures, not five repeated spectra of one compound. Deterministic tie order: descending score then standardized identity; also report pessimistic/optimistic rank bounds for exact-score ties, independent of correctness. Do not select the correct isomer to break ties. Report both strict and connectivity metrics, and record-level rank as a separate reproducibility check.

docs.title: P2 — Open-set rejection and paired removal
docs.text:
Starting from the same known-truth query panel, remove all reference records sharing the query connectivity block, including full-key variants, salts mapped by the identity policy, acquisition derivatives and mirrored copies. Verify removal against the independent label ledger, not only metadata parsed by MassFlow. This makes the open-set challenge unambiguously absent under both identity endpoints. Keep near-isobaric and related but different structures to make plausible false matches possible. List removal counts and changed library composition.

Use both (a) a mixed present/absent batch and (b) an all-absent challenge. Pair queries across present/removal arms; do not regard the two outputs as independent. At fixed score/match and q acceptance policies, count an accepted exact-structure assignment for any absent truth as a false positive. Correct rejection means searched and abstained. A preprocessing failure is an operational failure; report it separately, with an additional end-to-end no-false-call rate if useful. No-hit does not establish chemical absence in a sample. Top-k identity success is undefined as a retrieval objective for the absent set; all forced identity calls are wrong. Evaluate analogue usefulness only under its separate endpoint.

docs.title: P3 — Confidence calibration against experimental truth
docs.text:
Freeze test structure groups into acquisition-balanced batches before scoring. Create explicit present/absent fractions 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1 as proposed stress scenarios, not estimates of real sample prevalence. Keep total query count, query quality strata and library construction policy documented. Repeat batch allocations using stored seeds; reuse of compounds creates dependence, so repeated allocations quantify design sensitivity rather than new independent experiments. Include a separate laboratory/source holdout for transfer claims.

Evaluate the current procedure as implemented, including score/match truncation, best-target/best-decoy pooling, ties, per-file calibration, q lookup and target row inheritance. Do not replace it with winner-take-all TDC or a published decoy algorithm and claim to have validated MassFlow. Compare alternate procedures in separately named research arms only. The primary discovery unit is one top-ranked structure per query. Assess the risk of treating every exported row as a discovery as a separate endpoint; a query q-value is not candidate-specific evidence.

For each batch, retain best target and best decoy before and after each gate, including no-hit sentinels. Tabulate how often known incorrect target maxima and decoy maxima survive. On absent queries, compare their score distributions, matched counts, precursor eligibility, peak density and score tails within strata. This probes exchangeability; matching entropy alone cannot establish it. The published fragmentation-tree decoy work [S2] is relevant precedent, not validation of MassFlow's jitter/permutation generator. Li et al. [S3] also caution that computational decoys can underestimate errors.

Evaluate fixed q thresholds {0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1.0} and the deployment threshold, without choosing a favorable one after test inspection. Plot reported threshold versus observed FDP and number of accepted queries, including zero-call points. Plot raw decoy/target tail counts and empty-null frequency. A q-value is a set-level error measure, not the posterior probability that a particular structure is incorrect [S4]. Do not apply reliability-bin/Brier-score interpretation to it.

Every empty-null batch is labelled uncalibrated. Current code can give every target query q=1/N_target when decoys are absent; increasing query count can therefore make rows pass a fixed cutoff without adding null evidence. Test this explicitly by partitioning/recombining the same known-truth queries. This is a design sensitivity test, not extra independent sample size. Nonempty nulls still require empirical calibration. Never tune jitter, gates, or query batch size to manufacture nominally significant calls.

docs.title: P4 — Candidate and filter loss decomposition
docs.text:
For every selected query, retain truth-presence indicators at ordered checkpoints: raw frozen library; post-ingestion/physical-validation library; post-metadata eligibility; precursor candidacy; accelerator candidacy; exact scoring; score and matched-peak gates; adduct/RT gates; distinct-structure top-1/top-5; q acceptance. Match actual execution order in the pinned implementation and label counterfactual reordering as such. Assign a first-loss reason; retain overlapping reasons too.

Compare each accelerator to exhaustive scoring on the same input and eligibility rules. Precursor filtering loss is not synonymous with 5-ppm model validation: report separately query metadata rejection, reference chemistry rejection, and query-reference search window loss. Modified cosine lacks cosine's hard precursor window, so candidate expansion is expected and must be evaluated for both true retrieval and false calls. If raw-library validation aborts the run, record the abort before curation; any curated rerun is a separately versioned library.

docs.title: P5 — Strata and robustness
docs.text:
Prespecify instrument analyzer/model, ionization method, inlet type, source laboratory, acquisition family, polarity, adduct/charge, CE value/unit, precursor mass, usable peak count, entropy, structural class and library multiplicity. Report counts and uncertainty for every stratum, including unknown metadata and zero-call strata. Report same-instrument, independent acquisition and different-instrument results separately. Never convert NCE to eV or compare numeric energies across instruments without a validated mapping. The pilot does not support these expanded claims until adequate eligible records exist; empty strata remain unsupported.

Use development data to select instrument-appropriate MS1 and MS2 tolerance ranges independently. Then freeze a 2x2 factorial sensitivity comparison (for the pilot, MS1 {0.01,0.02} Da x MS2 {0.01,0.02} Da); do not attribute a paired change in both tolerances to either alone. The repository's 5-ppm metadata rule stays fixed; its empirical appropriateness is evaluated through rejection accounting, not silently weakened.

On the unchanged held-out queries, compare default preprocessing with a locked identity-preserving normalization-only analysis, 1% base-peak noise removal and top-50 peak reduction, each one factor at a time. Document exact operation order, renormalization and resulting empty spectra. Additional synthetic perturbations of real query spectra: fragment shifts {-10,-5,0,5,10} ppm; independent precursor shifts at the same values; remove {0,10,30,50}% of fragments; add {0,10,30}% background peaks sampled from a disjoint measured blank pool. Use five fixed seeds per stochastic condition (42–46), peak-count rounding down, no label-dependent selection, float64 arrays and stored original/perturbed hashes. Declare this grid as sensitivity analysis rather than a physical instrument-error model. If no measured blanks are available, defer that arm. Synthetic two-spectrum chimeras (10% and 50% intensity contribution, normalized component TIC) are stress controls, not measured co-isolation validation. Preserve the source groups for both parts.
