Confirm unexpected effects later using independent experimental acquisitions.

docs.title: 5. Metrics with explicit denominators
docs.text:
Let N be all prespecified labelled test queries, N_present those with truth in the frozen raw reference library, S successfully searched, C queries with any qualified target candidate, and A(t) queries making one accepted top-1 structure call under policy t. Let TP(t) be correct accepted calls and FP(t) incorrect accepted calls; an abstention is never a TP. Let H_k indicate that truth is among the first k distinct structures before confidence filtering. No numerical rate is reported with denominator zero: use null plus raw counts.

Metric Definition and interpretation Closed-set end-to-end top-k accuracy sum(H_k) / N_present, k=1,5; selected queries rejected or without candidates contribute zero Conditional top-k sum(H_k) / searched_present; report alongside the end-to-end result Candidate retrieval coverage Queries with any true structure among candidates / N_present; specify checkpoint Call coverage A(t)/N, also A(t)/S; candidate coverage C/N is a different measure Accepted-call precision TP/(TP+FP) for the declared strict/connectivity endpoint and mixed cohort Identification recall Correct accepted present-query calls / N_present; wrong or missing call is a miss False negatives N_present - correct accepted present calls; distinguish wrong assignment, abstention and operational failure Observed FDP FP/max(A,1) by convention 0 for A=0; show A=0 and precision undefined so no-call runs cannot pass utility criteria Estimated FDR at score cutoff Recompute MassFlow's (1+D_ge)/(T_ge), clipped to 1; show raw counts, gates and q closure Open-set false assignment rate Incorrect accepted absent-query calls / N_absent; additionally condition on successfully searched absent queries Open-set searched rejection rate Successfully searched absent queries with no accepted call / searched_absent; failures reported separately Specificity Same searched-absent rejection fraction, using the explicit detection-task convention Stage survival Queries retaining >=1 true reference at stage j / N_present; conditional loss at j = first lost at j / truth-surviving prior stage Ranking loss Truth retrievable but not top-k / truth retrievable; retain total selected denominator too Procedure FDR Expectation of FDP over the declared sampling/batch-generating process; estimated only with appropriately independent batches

A wrong call on a present query is both an FP assignment and an FN for the correct identity; explain this paired interpretation. Do not construct invented WRONG:<name> classes or use weighted multiclass accuracy as identification precision. Candidate-row counts measure computational output, not discoveries. Report acquisition-weighted metrics and a structure-macro average (mean of each structure's rate), with unique-compound counts; multiple CEs are not independent compounds. Report per-structure discovery FDR separately if deduplicating calls across queries; query-level q-values do not establish that error rate.

docs.title: 6. Uncertainty and statistical decisions
docs.text:
Report counts and 95% uncertainty intervals with each primary rate where the sampling model supports them. Wilson intervals for retrieval/coverage and exact binomial one-sided bounds for rare errors apply only to a fixed per-query decision rule under an explicitly justified independent Bernoulli sampling model, conditional on the fixed library. Unique structures alone do not justify this model, and it does not apply to file-level q-based acceptance: those decisions share a data-dependent threshold. If sampling assumptions are unsupported, report descriptive counts and design sensitivity rather than an inferential binomial bound.

For q-based pilot analyses as well as expanded repeated acquisitions, resample whole connectivity groups (all full-key variants and conditions together), 2,000 bootstrap replicates, seed 42. Where stratified resampling is used, assign each group to its prespecified primary query's source/polarity stratum; all paired acquisitions follow that group's draw. Record the anchor query and weights, so cross-stratum acquisitions cannot be independently resampled. Recompute acceptance sets and q-values from resampled best-target/decoy maxima, preserving resampling multiplicities as weights; resampling final accepted rows alone misses selection uncertainty. Within-query ranks come from the unchanged frozen library. Identical resampled acquisitions are weights, not new measurements or collapsed query IDs. Pilot bootstrap results are sensitivity analyses, not proof of control. Use batch/laboratory-level resampling for transfer and distinguish sensitivity intervals on reused data from independent validation intervals.

Observed FDP for one fixed batch is known conditional on its adjudicated labels. An interval concerns generalization to other sampled structures/batches, not uncertainty in counting that batch. Record disputed-label adjudications and give best/worst-case sensitivity bounds; a statistical interval does not repair bad truth. At zero accepted calls FDP=0 is bookkeeping, not evidence of useful control.

For a claimed operating error bound, set a scientifically justified allowable error and minimum useful retrieval/coverage before testing, based on the intended cost of false calls versus misses. Compare a one-sided upper uncertainty bound with that limit; also require a minimum useful number of calls. If precision is insufficient, conclude inconclusive rather than passing or moving the threshold. As a sample-size illustration under an ideal independent fixed-rule Bernoulli model only, zero errors among 50 independent accepted calls has a 95% one-sided binomial upper bound about 5.82%; 299 independent accepted calls with zero errors are needed to put that bound below 1% (1 - 0.05**(1/n)). This is not proof of FDR control or a universal sample-size requirement. Correlation, repeated compounds, label errors, batches and strata can require substantially more evidence.

Evaluate q calibration across all fixed thresholds with intervals and explicit multiplicity scope. Use a single prespecified primary operating point for a confirmatory claim; use a simultaneous band or prespecified multiplicity correction if claiming multiple strata/thresholds simultaneously. Do not declare calibration from a nonsignificant deviation or overlap of wide intervals. Report unresolved regions as unsupported. Paired algorithm comparisons use compound-level paired bootstrap differences, not independent-spectrum tests. Baselines are compared on identical eligible denominators and operating policies.

docs.title: 7. Required controls and baselines
docs.text:
Control/baseline Purpose and allowed interpretation Exact self-match, kept outside test accuracy Plumbing/serialization positive control; disclose inevitable leakage Independent standard acquisition, same structure Real retrieval positive control Truth removal plus isobaric/isomeric decoys from measured compounds Real open-set false-call challenge Wrong polarity, contradictory charge/adduct, missing precursor and metadata Failure/rejection/provenance behavior; constructed controls cannot establish prevalence Label permutation after scoring Evaluator sanity check only; not a physically realistic null or FDR estimate Measured blanks and held-out unrelated standards Operational false calls; no exhaustive chemical-negative truth inferred from a blank Library multiplicity: natural, one reference/structure, controlled duplicates Detect score/opportunity inflation and traceability failures; do not tune multiplicity on test outcomes Independent matchms 0.33.1 greedy exhaustive search Detect wrapper/prefilter/ranking differences with identical preprocessing and gates Maximum-weight one-to-one matching on a small subset Distinguish greedy assignment approximation from an implementation error; not assumed to be the production algorithm Precursor-only nearest eligible reference Measures information added by MS/MS beyond mass, with deterministic ties and no chemical label access Fixed-seed random eligible structure rank Checks candidate density and evaluator behavior; retain all failures Published decoy method, if fully reproduced Research comparator for error estimation [S2]; never borrowed calibration for the current generator

Fixed-count/shuffled-intensity/jittered spectra are software stress inputs, not real negative chemicals. No decoy generator is accepted solely because its entropy, peak count or precursor distribution matches the targets.

docs.title: 8. Smallest useful benchmark: MVB-1
docs.text:
Proposed, not executed: a MassBank frozen-release pilot with 20 development and 100 test structures from 120 distinct connectivity groups, one query per structure, each with a traceable independent reference acquisition. Select positive-mode [M+H]+ experimental MS2 with reference-standard label evidence, CC0/CC BY record rights, full-key identity, verified centroided representation, ESI ionization, known analyzer and CE units for both query and reference. Record inlet types and report cross-inlet retrieval separately; do not claim LC validation from flow-injection/direct-infusion data. Prefer different laboratories/instruments; a same-lab independent acquisition cohort must be reported separately. CE variants of one injection alone do not meet strict acquisition independence.

Freeze MassBank release 2026.03, resolved commit 705afb7bccc3b2c42410a744eef73674716a60ef (verified tag), plus every asset SHA-256. Inventory before asserting that the requested panel exists. First choose one eligible full-key truth per connectivity group by ascending SHA256("massflow-mvb1-truth-v1|" + full_inchikey). Then sort connectivity groups by SHA256("massflow-mvb1-v1|" + connectivity_key); choose the first 20 for development and next 100 for test, retaining the entire ordered eligible/reserve ledger and the within-group choices. Never split variants of one connectivity group across development/test or present/absent assignments. Within each selected structure choose query/reference groups by sorted immutable accession among qualifying independent pairs, using a frozen instrument-priority list (QTOF query / Orbitrap reference, then the reverse, then explicitly separate same-analyzer acquisitions). No fallback based on matching success.

Library L0 contains all rights/metadata-eligible positive protonated experimental MS2 records from that release except test/development query acquisition groups and unresolved cross-set duplicate components. Deduplicate mirrored acquisitions, retaining independent repeated references and their multiplicity. Preserve all background structures; report the resulting library size.

Library L50 removes all connectivity-equivalent records for the first 50 test groups in the frozen order. Because each test query has a different connectivity group, the other 50 remain present. Search the same 100 queries against L0 (all present) and L50 (50 present/50 absent), with both classical engines: four primary search runs. Construct development libraries using only development absence assignments so test labels do not tune settings. Save P4 funnels, top-1/top-5, precision/recall/coverage, paired truth-removal behavior, all target/decoy maxima, q/FDP tables and strata. A separate all-absent library is a required P2 extension, not one of these four minimal runs. P0 controls and the deployment-policy pass remain mandatory qualification checks.

This pilot is sufficient to exercise an honest retrieval/rejection evaluation and expose gross gate/calibration problems. It cannot validate a 1% FDR claim, comprehensive instrument performance or matrix generalization. If 120 qualifying structures/pairs do not exist, publish the inventory and the shortfall; reduce scope by a new protocol amendment or use a rights-cleared independent source, not synthetic replacement or relaxed undocumented independence. Expand calibration sample size only after observing pilot precision and predeclaring a new design.

docs.title: 9. Release evidence categories
docs.text:
Category Evidence required Current audit recommendation Validated stable functionality Exact version/domain/config/data identified; software qualification; independent held-out experimental results with adequate uncertainty; prespecified error and utility criteria met; provenance complete No broad chemical-identification or calibrated-FDR claim qualifies from the inspected evidence. Narrow arithmetic/I/O invariants can be called software-verified Functional but scientifically unvalidated Qualified software behavior, transparent limitations, no unsupported identity/FDR claims Classical library retrieval and numerical q/p outputs, subject to affected-path correctness fixes and explicit calibration warnings Experimental Explicit opt-in, isolated outputs, model/training or method evidence incomplete ML/meta-engine/routing/network/analogue inference and confidence transfer across untested strata Correction required before release of affected claims/paths Reproduced correctness/provenance defect, unreconciled metadata/units, materially misleading scientific claim, or inability to reproduce Review/integrate affected-path fixes #101/#103–#107; reconcile cache semantics; correct confidence/identity wording and RT units; repair benchmark/provenance deficiencies before evidentiary use

Release managers must decide whether an affected path is corrected or explicitly excluded/disabled and documented. A draft PR is not a correction on main. Green CI is necessary software evidence under repository policy, not a release approval. Do not advertise Matched at score >=0.9 as a confirmed identity, entropy preservation as calibrated FDR, or a 2,000-entry library as sufficient statistical power. Scope any future validation statement to the actual domain and frozen procedure. Human review is required for any merge or release; this program does neither.

docs.title: 10. Limitations and next work
docs.text: Public library labels may be wrong or incomplete; source mirroring and undocumented replicates limit independence. Full-key truth does not guarantee stereochemical selectivity. A standard-library pilot omits extraction losses, chromatographic coelution, ion suppression, endogenous concentration effects and real chimeras. Prospective blinded standard mixtures in relevant matrices, including blanks, spikes and independently acquired confirmatory spectra, are the next evidence layer after the retrospective pilot. Their composition, practical replicates and error limits must be designed for a stated application; they are not supplied by unit tests or this specification.

docs.title: Primary references
docs.text:
• S1: Schymanski et al. (2014), Identifying Small Molecules via High Resolution Mass Spectrometry: Communicating Confidence, DOI 10.1021/es5002105. Bibliographic identity verified through PubMed; publisher full text was inaccessible during this audit, so no detailed level assignment is inferred here.
  • S2: Scheubert et al. (2017), Significance estimation for large scale metabolomics annotations by spectral matching, DOI 10.1038/s41467-017-01318-5. Read through Europe PMC full-text XML, Results and Methods. Its algorithms and evaluations differ from MassFlow's.
  • S3: Li et al. (2021), Spectral entropy outperforms MS/MS dot product similarity for small-molecule compound identification, DOI 10.1038/s41592-021-01331-z, author-hosted full text, Discussion pp. 6–7. Similarity evidence does not validate entropy-preserving decoys.
  • S4: Storey and Tibshirani (2003), Statistical significance for genomewide studies, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1530509100, author-hosted paper. General q-value interpretation, not the estimator implemented by MassFlow.
  • S5: Huber et al. (2020), matchms — processing and similarity evaluation of mass spectrometry data, DOI 10.21105/joss.02411. Software reference; benchmark baseline must additionally pin the exact version.

docs.title: Experimental dataset assessment and freeze plan
docs.text: Source documentation checked 2026-10-21 America/Vancouver. Accessible documentation is verified; a complete experimental corpus has not been downloaded or curated for this program. All counts and eligible-pair feasibility must be established from frozen files. Proposed experiments are in the program.

docs.title: Candidate resources
docs.text:
Resource Ground truth and experimental diversity Rights and reproducibility Recommendation MassBank official records Record structures, accession, instrument, precursor/adduct, CE and provenance fields; record assertion is not independent identity verification. Select measured MS2 with standard evidence, preserving missing fields. Contributor/instrument diversity is useful; same-lab CE series may be one acquisition Record-level LICENSE can be CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC or CC BY-NC-SA. Check each record and its attribution; no blanket CC0 assumption. Versioned GitHub/Zenodo releases support freezes [D1,D2] Primary MVB-1 source: release 2026.03, tag resolves to 705afb7bccc3b2c42410a744eef73674716a60ef. Restrict initial redistributable panel to verified CC0/CC BY records; audit independent pairs before promising sample size MoNA / VF-NPL Hosts both measured and in-silico records; LC-MS/MS, polarity, instrument and named-library downloads. VF-NPL QTOF/LTQ/QExactive offers a practical cross-instrument panel already used locally, but shared source standards and repository mirrors need lineage checks [D3] Download endpoints are mutable. Freeze exact request/response, JSON plus MSP, timestamps, SHA-256, record IDs and original library links. The inspected license page concerns software; it does not establish blanket spectral-data redistribution rights [D4] Secondary/reconciliation cohort. Existing saved results are useful diagnostics. Do not redistribute VF-NPL derivatives until its original data rights and identity provenance are resolved GNPS directly contributed reference spectra Standards and community records with annotation histories and variable curation quality; separate measured standards from propagated/suspect/analogue hypotheses. Preserve accession, USI/raw scan where present and annotation revision [D5] Direct contributions default CC0; imported third-party libraries need their own rights checks. MGF/JSON download is possible; freeze content because live libraries change [D5] Independent source/laboratory holdout after cross-repository duplicate audit. Exclude propagated/suspect libraries as exact truth CASMI 2016 Known challenge solutions; category 1 and categories 2/3 are different cohorts. Original automated-method paper describes 208 category 2/3 peak lists and separate training data, and documents training overlap; historical challenges are not necessarily unseen today [D6] Official category-1 MassIVE MSV000079573 landing page identifies challenges 1–19 and CC0, with “Partial Public” status. This does not establish identical availability/license for categories 2/3, solution tables or every supplemental asset [D7] Small external challenge and label/provenance check. Resolve precise category, file access and identity solution provenance before freezing. Missing library truth belongs in open set, not closed-set failure inflation MSnLib (comparable reference resource) Measured Orbitrap ID-X flow-injection standards, both polarities and energy series, with raw/mzML and processing lineage. Export includes individual, merged-energy and pseudo-MS2 spectra; use only genuine single-stage MS2 with declared SPECTYPE for primary testing [D8,D9] Zenodo version record 21105617 inspected; API reports cc-by-4.0. Earlier concept record redirects to latest, so use a version DOI plus file hashes. Source lists raw-data records and checksum-bearing MGF/JSON assets [D8] Traceable expanded standard cohort, especially for pairing independent external references. Do not treat different energies, merged products or MSn derivatives as independent experiments Commercial NIST tandem libraries Potential high-quality comparator if properly licensed No open redistribution permission established here; published performance is not permission to ship data Optional locally licensed external comparison, excluded from an openly redistributed minimal benchmark

These are resource assessments, not declarations that every deposited chemical identity is correct. Require original contributor/standard evidence or classify the record as repository-asserted truth. Where an authentic-standard certificate, lot identity or orthogonal confirmation is unavailable, record that limitation. Evidence tier must never be upgraded merely because several repositories agree.

docs.title: Exact acquisition/freeze procedure
docs.text:
1. Archive release metadata and record-format documentation, capture access date, original publisher/laboratory, release DOI/tag and resolved commit. For MassBank, verify git rev-parse 2026.03^{commit} equals the pinned SHA after a clean clone; use that commit, not a moving default branch. Download the corresponding record archive and retain its byte length and SHA-256. Select source records directly from that commit; export to MSP/MGF using a separately pinned conversion step.
  2. Inventory records before selection. Extract native identity fields, source license/attribution, experimental/simulated/merged status, MS level, polarity, adduct/charge, instrument/analyzer, CE text/value/unit, precursor, peak count, sample and acquisition lineage. Keep original metadata JSON/text unmodified.
  3. Resolve structure labels in an evaluator-only table; record inconsistencies, missing stereo/isotope information and adjudication. Compute exact peak hashes and cross-source duplicate components. Do not use MassFlow acceptance or score to decide label eligibility. Retain the entire exclusion ledger.
  4. Apply the frozen eligibility and deterministic split/selection rules in MVB-1. Report the number of eligible structures, independent acquisition pairs, records and missing metadata by source/stratum. If sample-size/independence needs cannot be met, stop the confirmatory run and amend the design before scoring.
  5. Write an immutable manifest conforming to the contract. Store original assets, labels, scripts, mapping tables, input exports, checksums and the exact licensing/attribution evidence. For assets without redistribution permission, publish retrieval instructions and hashes only where permitted; access alone does not authorize repackaging. Resolve ambiguity before publishing.
  6. Fetch each frozen file twice to distinct local locations and verify identical SHA-256. Changing content requires a new dataset version. Rebuild search stores from these frozen files into new paths, save lineage, and verify record-count, structure-count and metadata round-trips. A live endpoint alone is not a freeze.

A possible MassBank source acquisition command (not executed as a corpus download in this task):

git clone --branch 2026.03 --single-branch https://github.com/MassBank/MassBank-data.git massbank-2026.03
git -C massbank-2026.03 rev-parse HEAD

Raw-source SHA-256 and lineage must supplement repository commit IDs. Do not use a mutable download filename as the dataset version. Collision energy numeric values with missing units stay unknown; polarity and adduct must not be inferred from the desired answer. Exclude computational libraries (e.g. LipidBlast) from the measured-reference primary cohort even when hosted alongside measured spectra.

docs.title: Original documentation and literature
docs.text:
• D1: MassBank official data repository and release 2026.03. Release metadata and remote tag checked; full data inventory deferred.
  • D2: MassBank Record Format 2.6.0, sections LICENSE, acquisition, focused-ion and peak metadata. Record-level licenses must be rechecked in the frozen dataset; this documentation URL can change.
  • D3: MoNA downloads and original query/API documentation.
  • D4: MoNA license documentation. Search-index text describes software licensing; rendered page did not expose a blanket data license in this audit. Dataset rights remain unresolved.
  • D5: GNPS reference-library documentation, annotation history, suspect libraries and License; GNPS2 library inventory.
  • D6: Schymanski et al. (2017), Critical Assessment of Small Molecule Identification 2016: automated methods, DOI 10.1186/s13321-017-0207-1, full text, Methods and training-overlap evaluation.
  • D7: MassIVE MSV000079573, original CASMI category-1 deposit.
  • D8: MSnLib versioned library deposit 21105617, SPECTYPE descriptions and raw-data links; API metadata inspected for metadata.license.id (cc-by-4.0). Do not rely on concept DOI redirects.
  • D9: Brungs et al. (2025), MSnLib: efficient generation of open multi-stage fragmentation mass spectral libraries, DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02813-0. Dataset-owner documentation, rather than the paper's aggregate performance claims, supplies the acquisition/export facts used here.

docs.title: Implementation and evidence audit
docs.text: Status: inspected source at ffef50bff913fcf400cb3de72595dab50e4f3fd8 on 2026-10-21 America/Vancouver; remote main matched. This is an audit, not a new experimental performance result. See the program for proposed tests. The main working checkout contains concurrent uncommitted benchmark/processing work; it was read but not modified. This specification uses an isolated worktree.

docs.title: Supported annotation types
docs.text:
Surface Actual annotation/evidence Boundary Stable annotate, cosine Reference-spectrum candidate rows with score/matched peaks, precursor metadata, reference identity and per-query q/p fields Small-molecule library retrieval; no de novo elucidation, concentration, or peptide identification Stable modified_cosine Direct and precursor-shift-aligned spectral similarity; can retrieve different-mass analogues A shifted high score does not establish the same structure or a calibrated analogue relationship CSV / experimental mzTab-shaped Multiple rows per query; Matched for score >=0.9, otherwise Putative; empty-null hits Uncalibrated, no-hit processed queries Unknown Labels are implementation categories, not validated external identification-confidence levels Experimental consensus/cascade Weighted score aggregation / staged candidate reduction; optional routing and ML engines Different score meanings and training exposure; no independent calibration demonstrated Experimental network branch (#80) Direct evidence plus graph/context hypotheses and tiers on a separate branch Not present as a stable main capability; never count propagated hypotheses as independent confirmed identifications Formula/adduct/isotope model helpers Chemical plausibility calculations and theoretical isotope envelopes Plausibility is not empirical identity verification; no observed isotope tie-break in classical/consensus search was found

annotation_tier is initialized null in classical results. structural_similarity in consensus is populated with a best individual engine score; its name does not make it an independently measured molecular-structure similarity. analog_search is a configuration field with no active use found outside configuration on the pinned source; modified-cosine shift behavior occurs independently of that flag. Do not advertise an additional validated analogue workflow on this basis.

docs.title: Scoring and filtering
docs.text:
Source locators refer to the pinned baseline; links will remain stable: similarity.py, processing.py, models.py, config.py.

  • Core engines instantiate matchms CosineGreedy and its modified-cosine greedy implementation (installed lock version 0.33.1), fragment tolerance in Da. With default matchms exponents (m/z power 0, intensity power 1), score is the sum of products of greedily paired intensities divided by the product of the full spectral L2 norms. Greedy one-to-one pairing need not be globally optimal. Modified cosine allows direct and precursor-mass-difference-shifted matches. Validate mixed frames, shared peaks and charge/adduct dependence explicitly.
  • Cosine's sparse-array path applies a query/reference precursor window: fixed Da or query-scaled resolution_ppm. Standard reported mass error uses reference m/z in its ppm denominator. Missing precursor handling differs at the direct scorer boundary versus validated file ingestion. Modified cosine does not use cosine's hard MS1 window; a larger candidate pool is expected, not necessarily increased identification sensitivity.
  • Default-on Numba modified-cosine prefilter checks peak/neutral-loss match counts before exact scoring. PR #104 demonstrates mixed-frame false pruning in main. Candidate accelerators require comparison to exhaustive scoring, not just speed.
  • Ingestion and processing perform metadata repair, optional intensity/fragment filtering, peak reduction and normalization. Structural claims trigger formula/structure/adduct-based precursor checks (repository policy: 5 ppm). Missing structural context skips parts of this check; a query's unknown true chemistry is not tested against every candidate by the model validator. Raw reference failures can abort annotate; db build instead curates/rejects. Explicit persistent stores are trusted and do not automatically revalidate.
  • Search applies score and matched-peak thresholds; main truncates top_n before the adduct/RT checks (PR #106). Default workflow requests unlimited candidates, so do not claim that capped-API defect explains every benchmark failure.
  • Adduct compatibility checks ion-mode sign; it does not require identical adduct species or compatible charge magnitudes for every direct scorer pair. Structural ingestion validation has the separate signed-charge defect demonstrated in #103.
  • RT filtering directly compares stored retention-time values with rt_tolerance. Its config describes minutes while repository spectrum governance specifies seconds, and this code does not convert units. This is a source-level contract discrepancy; no new empirical RT failure was reproduced in this audit. Disable RT in the initial benchmark pending a documented end-to-end unit resolution.
  • Native SQLite stores full spectrum metadata and float64 peak arrays. Chemical identity is not inherently a unique experimental-record ID. Main can emit reference_id="None" or repeated IDs; #107 contains synthetic reproductions, record identity assignment and serialization/provenance safeguards. Legacy stores and general append/merge collisions still need explicit handling.

docs.title: Confidence calculations: precise current procedure
docs.text:
generate_decoys (similarity.py around lines 649–842) makes one decoy per target: copy precursor and metadata; retain all peaks; permute intensities among peaks above a 1%-of-base-peak floor; jitter fragment positions uniformly by +/-1 Da (default); clip positive; sort. Uniform/degenerate intensities may be tapered, so entropy is not preserved for every case. RNG derives from seed and peak-array bytes, invariant to chunk boundaries. The jitter includes arbitrarily small shifts: source comments claiming that no fragment can remain within scoring tolerance are stronger than the implemented uniform distribution guarantees.

calibrate_query_level_fdr (around lines 1000–1099) retains the maximum qualifying target score and maximum qualifying decoy score per query. Queries without a qualified hit on one side do not enter that side's finite-score array. Both maxima can enter: this is not a paired winner-take-all competition. Both arrays are pooled and ranked. At threshold t, the implementation uses:

T(t) = count(best target score >= t)
D(t) = count(best decoy score >= t)
FDR_hat(t) = min(1, (1 + D(t)) / T(t))    [1 if T(t) = 0]
q(s) = min over thresholds t <= s of FDR_hat(t)
p(s) = (1 + count(finite best decoy scores >= s)) / (1 + N_finite_decoy)

Decoys precede targets at tied scores; cumulative raw ratios are reverse-monotone closed. A per-score lookup makes equal best-target scores share q. Empty decoy arrays give p=1 and all target q-values 1/N_target after closure (when targets exist). The code and sidecar flag this as fdr_uncalibrated; it is an arithmetic rank output, not a demonstrated conservative statistical error bound.

Workflow _process_single_file calls calibration after assembling all chunks for that input file. It attaches the query's best-target q and p to every target candidate row and accepts all such rows if q <= fdr_threshold; p is diagnostic only. Decoys are removed from normal output. Thus the calibration family is an input file, the statistic is a best-target query score, and exported candidate rows are not independent discoveries. A low-ranked incorrect row can inherit a q-value determined by a different, higher-ranked target for the same query. Changing file partitioning can change q outputs. The study must test the actual one-call/query decision separately from all-row exports.

The source claims pooling heterogeneous engines is valid because of null exchangeability. Using the same engine within a target/decoy pair does not itself establish this assumption; routed score distributions and gate asymmetry require empirical examination. A warning that fewer than about 2,000 library entries is statistically weak does not supply a validated sufficiency threshold. Statistical power depends on independent query/error counts, null quality, library composition and the decision procedure, not one universal library size.

docs.title: Evidence that exists
docs.text:
Evidence inspected What it supports What it does not support test_mathematical_proof.py, precursor/adduct/isotope boundary suites Hand-crafted numerical scoring and chemistry contracts; optional-dependency behavior Measured selectivity in real unknown mixtures tests/scientific_validation/ground_truth_*.msp/json, generator and golden suite Deterministic end-to-end integration and known-answer arithmetic, mostly constructed spectra An independent experimental cohort or acquisition-independent chemical truth test_fdr_statistics.py, FDR invariants and golden q values Formula/tie/empty-null/chunk contracts, some fake-engine fixtures Exchangeability of false target hits and synthetic decoys, or observed error control Existing saved MoNA VF-NPL cross-instrument outputs Limited retrospective connectivity retrieval under specified configurations Strict full-key accuracy, matrix identification, new-version reproducibility, or calibrated FDR PR #103–#107 evidence reports Reproduced synthetic correctness/provenance defects and focused corrections on their branches Empirical defect prevalence; merged corrections; chemical identification validation

Saved output recount, not a fresh rerun:

Quantity 0.01/0.01 Da MS1/MS2 0.02/0.02 Da MS1/MS2 Selected queries (label ledger) 600 600 Loaded / rejected / searched (saved report) 600 / 100 / 500 600 / 100 / 500 Qualified target candidate rows (CSV recount) 472 508 Queries with a target call (CSV recount) 148 155 Correct top-1 connectivity (saved truth-ID mapping + CSV recount) 116 116 End-to-end connectivity retrieval, correct / selected 19.33% 19.33% Correct among calls 78.38% (116/148) 74.84% (116/155) True structure represented among candidates 134 136 LTQ-source calls 0 0

No top-score ties occurred in either saved output. Both runs have an empty decoy null and Uncalibrated hits. Library: 28,260 records / 2,226 connectivity labels; queries: 300 LTQ and 300 QTOF against QExactive. Both use cosine, score 0.4, three matched peaks, q threshold 1.0 and dirty checkout at the baseline SHA. Both MS1 and MS2 tolerances changed, so this is not a causal comparison of either parameter.

The recount confirms arithmetic from candidate rows and the existing label map; it does not independently authenticate purchased-standard identities, audit all near duplicates, reconstruct missing raw acquisitions, or rerun the software. Exact-peak exclusion in the harness does not establish cross-acquisition lineage. The LTQ zero-call discrepancy versus earlier reported behavior remains unresolved. Saved provenance lists several requirement strings as package keys with <not installed> despite the executed workflow; dependency versions need repair before this bundle supports exact computational reproduction. Original MoNA licensing and frozen-download provenance are not established by these outputs.

docs.title: Claims that exceed the inspected evidence
docs.text:
• docs/user-guide/scientific_validation.md calls the golden suite authoritative for scientific meaning. Its authority can govern intended software semantics; it cannot substitute for experimental identification accuracy or null calibration. The cited Li paper develops entropy similarity, not this entropy-preserving jitter-decoy procedure. Its discussion explicitly raises risks of computational decoys; the citation does not validate this generator.
  • docs/user-guide/validation.md says every spectrum/molecule is scientifically sound and that the 5-ppm gate prevents unsupported lucky matches. Missing-context exemptions, trusted stores, unknown query structure and reproduced defects make those universal statements untenable. Five ppm is repository policy for a declared domain, not an instrument-independent law of measurement.
  • The same guide describes isotope-based consensus tie-breaking. Classical search and current consensus scoring do not consume measured isotope agreement as that claimed tie-break; model-envelope calculations alone do not implement it.
  • Score-based Matched and query-q inheritance must not be interpreted as confirmed identity or candidate-specific error probabilities. Header/docstrings calling benchmark labels objective do not audit label correctness or stereo equivalence.
  • The claim that the default accelerator is numerically identical to full scoring is contradicted on main by the mixed-frame reproduction in PR #104.

docs.title: Open work, verified live
docs.text:
Issues #68 and #91: zero-decoy investigation; #70: impact of the 5-ppm metadata gate; #71: modified-cosine signal/noise; #97: benchmark metrics/provenance; #95: fragment filter contract. These are unresolved validation/correctness work, not completed scientific evidence. Performance issues #61/#65–#67 do not validate identification.

PR Open head at audit Scope; release-validation implication #101 db774aa Missing precursor as NaN; reconcile with fragment-window contract #103 113df60 Charge/adduct contradiction; declared chemistry and cache semantics #104 134a204 Mixed-frame prefilter recall #105 93fc25b Fragment filtering and cache semantics #106 f377ef3 Capped search eligibility order #107 2f8d408 Acquisition record identity/provenance; legacy-store limitations #92 e5b62e5 Advisory diagnosis only; does not resolve FDR calibration #80 73deedf Separate experimental network branch; unmerged, not stable evidence

None were merged when checked. Multiple standalone PRs change processing-fingerprint semantics; eventual integration needs a new coherent revision, fresh libraries, full qualification and empirical reruns. This specification changes no algorithms, confidence formulas, fixtures, dependencies or scientific thresholds, and creates no GitHub issues or releases.

docs.title: Ordered GitHub-ready validation issues
docs.text: These are local drafts, not newly posted issues or claims of completion. Use existing issues when scopes overlap; no automatic merge/release is authorized. Dependencies are scientific gates, not permission to combine unrelated patches.

docs.title: V01 — Qualify one exact baseline and reconcile scientific claims
docs.text:
Priority: release-critical prerequisite. Reuse #95 and PR #101/#103–#107 for their existing fixes; link rather than duplicate their implementations. Related #92.

Problem: Unmerged correctness/provenance changes and overbroad claims prevent a stable interpretation of new benchmark results.

Scope: Choose a human-reviewed release candidate; resolve affected charge, prefilter, fragment-window, missing-ID and capped-search defects; reconcile combined processing revision/cache behavior. Audit RT unit contract. Replace claims of confirmed identity, universal 5-ppm soundness, isotope tie-breaking and entropy-decoy calibration with precise supported behavior. No new scoring model.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [ ] Record clean application SHA, lock hash and installed dependency versions.
  • [ ] Run full mandatory coverage, core, lint and typing gates on that exact SHA.
  • [ ] Show prior failing cases and passing corrected controls; do not regenerate goldens to hide numerical disagreements.
  • [ ] Prove source-record traceability and rebuild stores into new paths.
  • [ ] Resolve RT seconds/minutes or exclude RT claims and disable that arm.
  • [ ] Publish an evidence/claim table; software verification remains distinct from experimental accuracy/calibration. No merge is performed by this issue draft.

Deliverables: qualification report, check logs and bounded residual-risk list. Depends on: human review/integration decisions. Blocks: confirmatory validation; diagnostic runs may proceed with explicit known-defect labels.

docs.title: V02 — Freeze a rights-cleared reference-standard corpus and identity ledger
docs.text:
Priority: first data work. Depends on V01 for software runs, but inventory can start independently. Primary source: MassBank 2026.03; alternatives per datasets.md.

Problem: Repository names and InChIKeys do not establish measured-standard truth, acquisition independence or redistribution permission.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [ ] Freeze source tag/commit, byte hashes, original records, rights and attribution.
  • [ ] Inventory measured/simulated/merged status, ionization method, inlet type, centroid/profile representation and required metadata before scoring.
  • [ ] Keep chemical identity separate from source-record/acquisition/duplicate IDs.
  • [ ] Review full-key/connectivity mappings, stereo/salt/isotope limitations and labels.
  • [ ] Audit mirrors, same-acquisition CE variants and near duplicates across sources.
  • [ ] Produce protocol-schema manifests, full exclusion ledger and deterministic development/test/reference splits; report whether 120 independent pairs exist.
  • [ ] Verify two fresh retrievals produce identical frozen bytes; unresolved rights block redistribution, not silently convert to an assumed open license.

Deliverables: immutable manifest/record ledger, rights report and feasibility counts. No fabricated replacement spectra if the requested cohort cannot be assembled.

docs.title: V03 — Add an independent query-accounting and metric evaluator
docs.text:
Priority: required harness work. Reuse/reconcile existing #97 and uncommitted benchmark_reporting.py work before implementing another evaluator. Depends on V02.

Problem: Candidate rows, accepted calls, searched queries and selected queries have different denominators; repeated structure records can fill top five slots.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [ ] One terminal state per selected query including whole-file failures.
  • [ ] Distinct-structure top-1/top-5 with deterministic ties plus tie bounds.
  • [ ] Strict full-key and explicitly secondary connectivity endpoints.
  • [ ] Correct precision/recall/coverage/FDP/open-set definitions with raw counts; zero denominators serialize as null; no invented WRONG labels.
  • [ ] Freeze evaluator fixtures with hand-calculated ranks, missed truth, false calls, rejected queries, duplicate structures and zero-call batches.
  • [ ] Preserve all source-record IDs and private label separation.
  • [ ] Recount historical outputs independently; retain unresolved LTQ behavior and environment/label limitations under #97 instead of silently replacing results.

Deliverables: versioned standalone evaluator, meaningful tests and accounting tables. No production scoring changes are part of this issue.

docs.title: V04 — Measure candidate and preprocessing losses against exhaustive search
docs.text:
Priority: mechanism before optimization. Related #70/#71/#95. Depends on V01–V03.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [ ] Retain truth presence and first-loss reasons at every P4 checkpoint.
  • [ ] Compare accelerator on/off to exhaustive exact greedy scoring on identical processed inputs; no dropped eligible true pairs allowed by a claimed exact accelerator. Document floating-point threshold handling.
  • [ ] Separate 5-ppm metadata rejection from precursor search-window losses.
  • [ ] Compare MS1/MS2 tolerances using a locked 2x2 design, not a two-knob causal claim.
  • [ ] Report losses by source/analyzer/adduct/CE/missing-metadata group, including zeros.
  • [ ] Retain failed raw-library builds and version any curated rerun.

Deliverables: candidate funnel tables, paired diffs and bounded hypotheses. A physics/notation mismatch is investigated before proposing tolerance changes.

docs.title: V05 — Execute MVB-1 closed-set and paired open-set benchmark
docs.text:
Priority: smallest useful experimental retrieval evidence. Depends on V01–V04.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [ ] Preregister 20 development / 100 test structures from distinct connectivity groups, with group-level split/absence assignment, or document a prospective amendment if feasible independent pairs are fewer.
  • [ ] Freeze L0 and L50 with realistic background and verified absence assignments.
  • [ ] Run four primary searches (two engines x two libraries), plus P0 controls and separately labelled deployment-policy checks; archive all candidates/maxima.
  • [ ] Report all primary metrics, uncertainty and per-source counts; label analogues incorrect for exact-identity endpoints.
  • [ ] Compare exhaustive matchms, precursor-only and random eligible baselines.
  • [ ] State that this pilot is not adequate to certify 1% FDR or matrix performance.

Deliverables: frozen run bundle and report distinguishing observed/proposed/unknown. Stop if leakage or truth adjudication fails; retain the negative audit result.

docs.title: V06 — Validate confidence semantics and empirically challenge the decoy null
docs.text:
Priority: blocks calibrated-FDR claims. Reuse #68/#91; #91 remains analysis-only. Depends on V05 and a separately frozen precision/sample-size plan.

Problem: Best-target/best-decoy pooling, gate truncation, empty-null rank values, per-file families and candidate-row inheritance have untested empirical meaning.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [ ] Independently recompute current q/p formula and lookup on saved maxima.
  • [ ] Compare estimated and observed FDP at locked thresholds with counts and uncertainty; distinguish a fixed-batch FDP from expected procedure FDR. Recompute q during group resampling; do not use binomial exact intervals for dependent q-based calls merely because query structures are unique.
  • [ ] Evaluate mixed/all-absent batches, actual wrong target tails, gate attrition, empty-null frequency, file partitioning and seed sensitivity.
  • [ ] Evaluate one top structure/query separately from all exported candidate rows.
  • [ ] Treat current decoys as unvalidated until empirical evidence supports the null; entropy or score-scale similarity alone is not acceptance.
  • [ ] Size independent cohorts for a declared error/utility decision; no universal library-size threshold and no declaration that nominal 1% implies actual 1%.
  • [ ] Preserve failures and unsupported strata. Alternative estimators/decoy methods require a separate research protocol and implementation review.

Deliverables: calibration/uncertainty report or a precise negative/inconclusive finding. Do not patch thresholds to force significance or substitute new software for missing empirical evidence.

docs.title: V07 — Expand acquisition strata and noise/preprocessing transfer tests
docs.text:
Priority: after pilot interpretation. Depends on V05; calibration claims depend V06.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [ ] Independently held-out source/laboratory cohort; both polarities and supported adduct/charge combinations only where real labelled records exist.
  • [ ] CE units and acquisition derivatives audited; no NCE/eV equivalence assumed.
  • [ ] Run prespecified noise/preprocessing grids with frozen seeds and paired structure-level uncertainty; label synthetic perturbations as such.
  • [ ] Preserve missing strata and insufficient precision as limitations.
  • [ ] If ML/meta-engines are assessed, inventory training overlap and score semantics first; no borrowed calibration from the classical engines.

Deliverables: stratum evidence matrix and scope-limited claims, not a pooled universal accuracy number.

docs.title: V08 — Prospective blinded standard-mixture validation and release evidence review
docs.text:
Priority: application-specific confirmation after retrospective design is useful. Depends on V05–V07 and an explicitly stated analytical use case.

Acceptance criteria:

  • [ ] Design independent standard identities, blinded mixture composition, blanks, matrix spikes and acquisition days/laboratories for the intended workflow.
  • [ ] Declare identification truth, relevant orthogonal confirmation, false-call cost and missed-call cost before acquisition/unblinding.
  • [ ] Choose sample/replicate counts and useful precision from those decisions; distinguish technical replicates from independent compounds/batches.
  • [ ] Publish accepted, wrong, absent, rejected and inconclusive outcomes with provenance and uncertainty; no concentration or LOD claim without its own study.
  • [ ] Classify each exact-version/domain feature using the four release categories in the program; require human review, with no automatic merge/release.

Deliverables: prospective study protocol/results and a human-reviewed evidence package, or a documented reason why the intended claim remains unvalidated.

docs.title: Frozen dataset and run manifest contract
docs.text:
Status: proposed schema v1. JSON schemas and an empty draft template accompany this document. The template contains no experimental records or invented labels; it deliberately cannot qualify as a frozen benchmark.

  • Dataset schema
  • Record-row schema, one JSON object per line in records.jsonl
  • Empty draft template

docs.title: Files in a dataset freeze
docs.text:
File Required content manifest.json Schema/version/status, protocol hash, identity policy, split policy, asset/derivative hashes, row-ledger hash and record count records.jsonl One immutable experimental spectral record per row, including excluded records; schema below structures.jsonl Original and standardized representations, full/first-block keys, salt/tautomer/isotope policy, evidence tier and adjudication acquisitions.jsonl Raw-file/native-scan/sample/standard-lot groups, lab/instrument/method, derivative parent links and independence evidence duplicates.jsonl Exact/near-duplicate links, rule/version, source evidence, adjudication and retained/excluded decision selection.jsonl Entire eligible ordered population, hash-based selection/reserve order, split, absence assignment, exclusion reason and timestamp licenses.jsonl Per-source/record license identifier/text locator, authors, required attribution, access and redistribution decision with evidence labels.private.jsonl Evaluator-only query truth, full/connectivity identity, truth-present flags for each frozen library and independent verification library-L0.*, library-L50.*, queries.* Exact search inputs; each parser record maps to one record UID; query truth fields removed conversions.jsonl Parent/derivative hashes, converter/version/options, field mapping, units, rounding and rejected records

The dataset schema checks types and local constraints; it does not establish rights, truth, independence or referential integrity. A future manifest validator must implement the semantic checks below. A schema-valid freeze alone is not scientific validation. The entire selection population and excluded records must be auditable, not just the successful final inputs.

docs.title: Record row fields
docs.text:
Field group Contract record_uid, source Globally unique record UID; source namespace, accession nullable, source asset ID, zero-based parser ordinal, native scan nullable and source annotation revision nullable. Source asset references a frozen file SHA-256 chemical_identity Internal structure_key; original and standardized full keys nullable; first-block key nullable; standardization policy ID; truth tier and evidence links. Never use these fields as acquisition identity measurement Experimental/simulated/consensus kind, MS level, centroid/profile representation, ionization method and original method text, inlet type, precursor m/z, adduct, signed integer charge, polarity, instrument model/analyzer and collision energy value/unit/original text; null/unknown for missing values lineage Acquisition group nullable, raw-file hash nullable, laboratory, sample/standard-lot group nullable, derivative parents, duplicate component, and independence verdict/evidence rights License identifier nullable, attribution text, evidence URLs, redistribute allowed/restricted/unresolved spectral_content Exact original peak hash, normalized peak hash nullable, peak count; hashing rule/version; intensity and m/z numeric types are float64 in derived files selection Eligible/excluded/challenge, reasons, development/test/reference-only/excluded split, query/reference/background roles. A query is never its own independent reference

Original metadata must be retained as a hashed asset even when normalized fields exist. Missing scientific values serialize as JSON null (JSON does not permit NaN); loaders convert to float64 NaN where numeric missingness is required. Missing CE, RT, adduct, formula or charge must never become scientific zero. Known zero collision energy is distinct from missing CE. RT, if present, is in retention_time_seconds; preserve source value/unit and conversion lineage. NCE/%/eV/unknown are distinct units. Do not infer equivalence between them.

Hash source-file bytes before parsing; capture source immutability throughout parsing. Hash peaks using a documented canonical little-endian float64 encoding, array length, sorted m/z/intensity pairs and policy for duplicate m/z/zero intensities. Keep raw and normalized hashes because normalization can mask copied spectra. Hash equality is sufficient to flag duplication, not to prove chemical identity.

docs.title: Mandatory semantic validation before freezing
docs.text:
1. Every asset exists and matches its declared SHA-256 and byte length; every UID is unique. Record source asset IDs and derivative/structure/group references resolve; parser ordinals map to original source records, including quarantines.
  2. Count totals reconcile: imported = eligible + excluded + challenge under the declared exclusive disposition policy. Record-ledger rows equal record_count. The separate manifest-selection population includes all labelled queries selected before pipeline processing; a runtime rejection cannot delete its entry.
  3. Every primary eligible query/reference is measured genuine ESI MS2, has verified centroided representation or documented validated centroiding provenance, documented truth, positive finite precursor and compatible declared polarity/adduct/charge, and passes protocol eligibility independent of MassFlow scores. Missing/contradictory source data remain visible in exclusions/challenges.
  4. Primary development/test query structures, connectivity groups and acquisition/duplicate components do not overlap. Test query acquisition groups do not occur in the reference library. Shared test structure identity across query and reference is required for closed-set retrieval, not a leak in itself.
  5. Each closed-set truth has >=1 qualified independent reference. Each open-set truth has zero connectivity-equivalent references after all alias mappings and source mirrors; save removal counts. Do not inspect only the output accession.
  6. Every record has a rights verdict and preserved attribution. No unresolved record may be included in a redistributed freeze. Verified-standard truth requires supporting evidence; a full InChIKey alone is insufficient.
  7. Query search files contain no answer-bearing chemical labels. Stored references retain source record IDs/metadata. Reopen/round-trip every selected record and verify peak arrays, record identity, adduct/charge, CE and instrument/source fields.
  8. Freeze requires completed protocol/identity-policy/split-policy hashes, immutable source versions and a clean harness version. An empty draft must fail promotion.

docs.title: Per-run artifacts and query accounting
docs.text:
Each run records application/harness commits, clean/dirty state and diff hash, lockfile hash, resolved package versions, host details, effective config and hash, commands, RNG seeds, library/input hashes, cache/store lineage, processing revision, backend, worker/chunk layout and FDR family (file/batch membership).

Required tables: query_accounting.jsonl, candidate_stages.jsonl, all_candidates.parquet or lossless CSV, query_maxima.jsonl, calls.jsonl, metrics.json, calibration.json, failures.jsonl, artifact_checksums.json. Store raw target and decoy scores, gate status and full record UID for every retained candidate. Counterfactual diagnostic passes are separate run IDs.

Exactly one terminal accounting state per selected query:

selected = processing_failed_or_rejected
         + searched_without_qualified_target
         + searched_with_qualified_target

A separate status indicates q-based abstention, accepted correct/incorrect call, truth presence, first-loss stage, source/stratum and reason. A whole-file failure must still generate a terminal state for each selected query through the harness. Only processed queries may appear as Unknown rows in native exports, so do not use export row count as the selected-query denominator. Native CSV can have several rows per query; left join the independent selection ledger to account for all queries. Null metrics must retain numerator and denominator, never silently zero.

docs.title: Audit evidence and reproducibility
docs.text: This folder records an audit and program design, not a newly executed chemical identification/calibration study. verification.json records checks performed on the delivered specification. The application baseline is ffef50bff913fcf400cb3de72595dab50e4f3fd8; production code, tests and lockfile are unchanged in this branch.

docs.title: Historical recount
docs.text:
recount_saved_outputs.py uses only Python's standard library. It reads historical files without writing to them or importing MassFlow:

python3 docs/validation/program/evidence/recount_saved_outputs.py \
  --base /tmp/massflow-benchmark-20261018 > /tmp/massflow-validation-recount.json

Compare runs and asset_hashes with audit-snapshot.json. The original private/local historical files are not redistributed here; if they are unavailable, the recount cannot be rerun from this folder alone. Each file is identified by SHA-256 and size. The helper uses the existing label-to-library-ID mapping, requires no tied best score (and fails explicitly if one appears), and checks no new chemical truth. Preprocessing rejection counts come from historical sidecars, not reconstructed execution. Candidate rows with empty scores are Unknown rows and do not count as calls.

github-snapshot.json records the live issue/PR metadata inspected; it is a dated snapshot, not a continuing status monitor. PR test claims are not independent evidence that a correction is merged or chemically validated.

docs.title: Specification checks
docs.text:
Run from this worktree root:

uv sync --locked
uv run mkdocs build --strict
uv run ruff check docs/validation/program/evidence/recount_saved_outputs.py
uv run ruff format --check docs/validation/program/evidence/recount_saved_outputs.py
uv run mypy docs/validation/program/evidence/recount_saved_outputs.py
uv run pytest tests/test_mathematical_proof.py tests/test_fdr_statistics.py tests/test_scientific_validation.py -q
uv run pytest --cov=src/MassFlow --cov-report=xml --cov-fail-under=80 -v

Validate the JSON schemas/template without adding a project dependency:

uv run --with jsonschema python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json
import jsonschema
root = Path('docs/validation/program')
for filename in ('manifest.schema.json', 'record.schema.json'):
    jsonschema.Draft202012Validator.check_schema(json.loads((root / filename).read_text()))
schema = json.loads((root / 'manifest.schema.json').read_text())
template = json.loads((root / 'manifest.template.json').read_text())
validator = jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema, format_checker=jsonschema.FormatChecker())
validator.validate(template)
template['status'] = 'frozen'
assert len(list(validator.iter_errors(template))) == 6
print('Two valid schemas; empty draft allowed; empty frozen manifest rejected.')
PY

These checks verify document links/build, schema logic, recount arithmetic and existing application tests. They do not validate acquisition independence, original data rights, chemical identity or FDR. The empty template is not a frozen dataset.

docs.title: Independent review
docs.text:
A separate read-only reviewer inspected the specification and relevant pinned source. Three substantive design findings were corrected and checked again:

  1. Split/select/assign absence by whole connectivity groups, keeping full keys for strict scoring; this prevents variant leakage and accidental removal of a supposedly present truth.
  2. Match intended-use scope to ESI reference-spectrum retrieval and capture ionization/inlet/centroiding evidence; no LC/matrix validation inferred from FIA.
  3. Limit binomial intervals to justified fixed-rule independent sampling; recompute q during grouped resampling, and label pilot resampling as sensitivity evidence.

The reviewer reported no remaining P1 finding in that focused follow-up. This review is a design check, not empirical validation or release authorization.
